Question No. 1 Residences in the proposed precinct

Chris Hanley registered the following question:
Has council contacted all residential and commercial owners in the proposed 30 hectare SEP zone and advised them specifically of their inclusion in the zone and has any detailed assessment as to the impact on property values been undertaken?  Is there also a specific buffer zone distance around the SEP zone that requires notification by council?

The Mayor took the question on notice.

Question No. 2 BSC Enforceability of Biodiversity Protection

Dean Prosser registered the following question:
The Seacliffs Community Title was approved by council in 2007 with a restriction for cats and dogs included in the Community Management Statement. All owners were made of this restriction in their pre-purchase information. A recent breach resulted in a report to council and a Development Control Order to cease use issued. That order was appealed to the Land and Environment Court and in a Conciliation Conference between the parties was deemed invalid, due to the council failure to apply the restriction consent condition on the dwelling consent, despite the property consent and the CMS identifying the restriction. Did council receive legal advice and how does it propose to rectify the situation?

The Mayor took the question on notice.

25-317 Resolved that pursuant to Section 4.16 of the Environmental Planning and Assessment Act 1979, Development Application No. 10.2025.98.1 for a Dwelling House including Demolition of the Existing Building and a New Swimming Pool be granted consent subject to the conditions of approval in Attachment 2 (E2025/78283) and Conditions 34 and 76 being amended to read:

34.

Landscaping Plan required

The application for a Construction Certificate is to include plans and specifications that indicate the landscaping of the site.  Such landscaping plan must incorporate adequate detail to demonstrate compliance with the provisions of Chapter B9 of Development Control Plan 2014. Native Species identified in Chapter B9 of Development Control Plan 2014 endemic to the North Coast of NSW to be planted at the rear of the site including Prickly Alyxia Alyxia ruscifolia, Coffee Bush Breynia oblongifolia, Hairy Psychotria Psychotria loniceroides, Palm Lily Cordyline petiolaris, stricta or rubra.

The landscaping plan must indicate:

  1. proposed location for planted shrubs and trees
  2. botanical name of shrubs and trees to be planted
  3. List of weeds on the site and removal strategy
  4. mature height of trees to be planted
  5. location of grassed and paved areas, and
  6. location of trees identified for retention in the development application plans.
  7. The plan is to be prepared by a suitably qualified landscape architect / architect /ecologist who has appropriate experience and competence in landscaping.

Such plans and specifications must be approved as part of the Construction Certificate. 

76.

Landscaping works and weed removal to be completed

Landscaping and weed removal are to be implemented in accordance with the updated and approved Landscaping Plan prior to issue of the occupation certificate for the development. A site meeting must be arranged with Council to determine satisfaction of this condition or alternatively a report must be provided from a qualified and experienced Landscape Architect.


The motion was put to the vote and carried unanimously.
Crs Lyon, Lowe, Hauge, Ndiaye, Dods, Warth, Swain and Pugh voted in favour of the motion.
Nil voted against the motion.

Moved: Cr Hauge Seconded: Cr Ndiaye
25-313 Resolved that Council:

  1. Receives an report or reports on the Special Entertainment Precinct Kickstart Grant that includes:
    1. A progress report and status update on work undertaken so far, for the period both before and since the grant was applied for and received
    2. The mapped area and details of licensed venues (including trading hours, liquor licenses, and relevant development consent conditions) within that area
    3. An explanation of how the SEP can extend, reduce, or incentivise the extension of trading hours for licensed venues, and how decisions about these trading hours are made (e.g. by council, or by other authorities)
    4. Current Bureau of Crime Statistics and Research (BOSCAR) figures and trends for Byron Bay town and the wider Shire, focussing on alcohol-related violence, sexual assault and anti-social behaviour
    5. Current plans, budgets, and known grant options for addressing community safety, public transport and road safety concerns
    6. Details of how the areas of investigation at Step 1.1, 1.2 and 1.3 of the NSW SEP Handbook, that should’ve been undertaken prior to applying for the grant and or initiating the SEP, were addressed, including:
      1. Establishing whether council has sufficient resourcing
      2. Preparing a transport review
      3. Establishing the strategic merit for the precinct area
      4. Whether “early consultation with key stakeholders” took place with community, businesses, venues and emergency services
      5. Whether a Memorandum of Understanding has been established with NSW Police
    7. Mechanisms by which the changes to the LEP made for the SEP trial can be reversed if the trial is not successful

  2. Establish a community reference group (“working group”) to guide the Special Entertainment Precinct trial, as per mandatory Step 1.3.4 of the SEP Handbook, that:
    1. includes, but not exclusively, emergency services, local small business owners, creative industry representatives, local residents, representatives from Music NSW, Destination Byron, Arts Northern Rivers, NORPA, tourism industry representatives, and Byron Bay Masterplan Group representatives, and that the makeup of the working group be brought to council for approval
    2. advice to council on desired outcomes and measures of success for the trial, or if an alternative to the trial is more appropriate to achieve the desired outcomes

  3. Receives a further report on why Council ceased to operate the Safer Communities Compact after the 2013-16 and 2016-19 plans, what community safety strategies replaced it, and if there is a need to re-instate the compact or a similar action plan.

  4. To compliment the proposed Special Entertainment Precinct (SEP), and acknowledging the documented harms attributable to alcohol consumption, coupled with the State’s intent to increase tourism numbers, council request the NSW State Government to allocate funding for emergency services and first responder provisions based on the combined totals of residents and visitor numbers rather than resident population figures, noting that this year’s figures are estimated at 1.9 million visitors to the Byron Shire. 
The motion was put to the vote and carried unanimously.

Moved: Cr Hauge Seconded: Cr Ndiaye
25-341 Resolved:
That Council:

  1. Acknowledges the progress of the Community Battery Working Group;

  2. Confirms the new direction for a Feasibility Study to investigate behind the meter Battery Energy Storage System for Byron Shire on Council assets, such as community centres, with the potential to operate as a Virtual Power Plant that could provide a return to the grid, community access to renewable energy and or an income stream, to be determined by the study;

  3. Proceeds with the procurement of a renewable energy consultant using the Terms of Reference (Attachment 4 -  E2025/71832) to inform the procurement;

  4. Allocates $40,000 from the Property Development Reserve to fund the Community Battery Feasibility Study;

  5. Notes the feasibility study will incorporate maintenance costs and inform asset owners of relevant implications to Council; and

  6. Awaits a further report on the outcomes of the feasibility study.

Moved: Cr Lowe Seconded: Cr Lyon
25-363 Resolved: 
That Council:

  1. Notes the outcomes of the Councillor Workshop held on 5 June 2025, with an external Legal Counsel presenting on key matters relating to Council’s enforcement functions.

  2. Returns to a detailed risk-based compliance approach via a Council resolved priority program and adopts the ‘Compliance Priorities Program’ for 2025 as provided below:
1.   Very High Priorities:
1.1    Developments, actions, works, activities or uses that places people’s lives at immediate risk or that cause or are likely to cause a significant risk of environmental harm or pollution.
1.2    Significant environmental and public health incidents.
1.3    Dangerous and/or menacing dogs.
1.4    Livestock on public roads.
1.5    Traffic, parking and unapproved camping activity. Camping enforcement, with an emphasis on environmentally sensitive areas.
1.6    Asbestos containing material being illegally dumped on public land.
 
2.       High Priorities
2.1    Unauthorised events, wedding receptions, parties, 'doof and rave' parties where significant environmental harm or risk to people’s lives.
2.2    Breaches of the NSW Fair Trading’s ‘Code of Conduct for the Short-Term Rental Accommodation Industry’ where the breach falls within the jurisdiction of Council’s enforcement powers.
2.3    Responses to complaints about recurring noise disturbance, public nuisance from premises, maintenance of alcohol-free zones.
2.4    Uncontrolled dogs and/or cats including those kept on land where development consent prohibits it.
2.5   Responses to serious breaches of the Food Act.

3.       Medium Priorities
3.1    Development or activities without consent, or non-compliance with consent, permit or licence conditions where these appear to pose no immediate threat to life, property, public health or the environment.
3.2    Non-compliant signage on public land.
 
4.       Routine Priorities
4.1    Companion animals with a high emphasis on high visibility enforcement and public education.
4.2    Seasonal public health issues and community preparedness.
4.3    Tourist and visitor accommodation swimming pool safety, including legislative requirements.
4.4    Onsite sewage management systems (including OSMS programme inspections).
4.5    Routine Food Safety Inspections.
4.6   Awareness of current public health requirements.

Moved: Cr Swain Seconded: Cr Ndiaye
25-329 Resolved:
That Council:

  1. Formally retires the Section 355 model of governance for the management of community facilities by
    1. Acknowledging that the Section 355 model is no longer suitable for meeting Council’s risk management and compliance obligations; 
    2. Respectfully revoking existing delegations and dissolving Section 355 Committees over the course of 12 months, with sincere recognition of the long-running and valuable service provided by community volunteers, and the invitation to continue their involvement through the proposed Friends of the Halls volunteer program; and
    3. Undertaking this process in a staged and supported manner, with the following indicative timeframes:
      1. Within 3 months: Mullumbimby Civic Memorial Hall, Marvell Hall, Brunswick Heads Memorial Hall and Bangalow A&I Hall 
      2. Within 6 months: South Golden Beach Hall and Ocean Shores Community Centre
      3. Within 12 months: Suffolk Park Community Hall and Durrumbul Hall 
      4. Following consent from the Minister for Lands and Property: Bangalow Showground. 

  2. Transitions to new governance approaches over the next 12 months, whereby Council:
    1. Assumes direct management of Bangalow A&I Hall, Brunswick Heads Memorial Hall, Marvell Hall, Mullumbimby Civic Memorial Hall, Ocean Shores Community Centre, South Golden Beach Hall, and Suffolk Park Community Hall; 
    2. Seeks consent from the Minister for Lands and Property responsible for NSW Crown Lands to delegate the Land Manager function of Durrumbul Hall to a suitable incorporated community association, and, 
      1. provided consent is granted, offers, upon application, the opportunity for an eligible incorporated community association to enter into a community license for Durrumbul Hall, and 
      2. if consent is not granted, or if a license with a suitable incorporated communication association is not established by 29 August 2026, Council assumes direct management of Durrumbul Hall;
    3. Seeks consent from the Minister for Lands and Property responsible for NSW Crown Lands to resign as Crown Land Manager for Bangalow Showground, thereby supporting the potential appointment of an eligible incorporated community association as Crown Land Manager, and, if consent is not granted, Council assumes direct management of Bangalow Showground; and
    4. Establishes and coordinates a new volunteer program, Friends of the Halls, to enable continued community stewardship, user support and facility activation to complement Council operations.

  3. Identifies the funding for implementation in the 2025-26 financial year in a future Quarterly Business Review; and

  4. Notes a review will be undertaken within three years of the transition, with a report to the Audit Risk and Improvement Committee, on the effectiveness of the new governance model/s in mitigating the identified risks of the current Section 355 model of management.

The motion was put to the vote and carried unanimously.

  2. Council undertakes a consultation process with the Local Area Commander of Police to recommend that all of Lot 2 DP 827049, being the area known as Railway Park, declared an Alcohol Prohibited Area (at all times);

  3. If no submissions are received from the Local Area Commander of Police during the consultation process of 1, Council declares all of Lot 18 DP 1269368, being the areas known as Apex Park, Dening Park and Main Beach, an Alcohol Prohibited Area (at all times);

  4. If no submissions are received from the Local Area Commander of Police during the consultation process of 2, Council declares all of Lot 2 DP 827049, being the area known as Railway Park, an Alcohol Prohibited Area (at all times);

  5. Subject to 1 and 3, if declared an Alcohol Prohibited Area, Council install Alcohol Prohibited Area signs within Lot 18 DP 1269368, being the areas known as Apex Park, Dening Park and Main Beach;

  6. Subject to 2 and 4, if declared an Alcohol Prohibited Area, Council install Alcohol Prohibited Area signs within part of Lot 2 DP 827049, being the area known as Railway Park;

  7. If declared, Council's General Manager liaise with the Local Area Commander of Police to determine if Council's Authorised Officers are suitable for an enforcement role under Section 632A of the Local Government Act 1993; and

  8. If declared, the above Alcohol Prohibited Area's be reviewed by Council in conjunction with the four yearly review of Council's Alcohol-Free Zones.

Moved: Cr Pugh Seconded: Cr Ndiaye
25-333 Resolved:
  1. That pursuant to Section 10A(2)( (d)(i) of the Local Government Act 1993, Council resolves to move into Confidential Session to discuss the report Policy - Commercial Activities on Coastal and Riparian Crown Reserve;
  2. That the reason for closing the meeting to the public to consider this item be that the report contains prejudice the commercial position of the person who supplied it
  3. That on the balance it is considered that receipt and discussion of the matter in open Council would be contrary to the public interest, as it contains confidential commercial information.

The motion was put to the vote and carried unanimously. 

Moved: Cr Pugh Seconded: Cr Ndiaye
25-334 Resolved:
That Council:

  1. Notes that National Parks and Wildlife Services made the decision to take the tender process for surf schools off Council.

  2. Adopts the recommended outcomes and issue sub-licence for:

    Group Surf Schools
    Operator 1:   Let’s Go Surfing Byron Bay
    Operator 2:   Soul Surf School Pty Limited
    Operator 3:   Byron Bay Surf School Pty Limited
    Operator 4:   Style Surfing School Byron Bay

    Personalised Surf Schools
    Operator 1:   Surf Research (Rusty Miller Personalised Surfing Instruction)
    Operator 2:   Ability Surf Pty Ltd

    Sea Kayak tours 
    Operator 1:  Go Sea Kayak Byron Bay Pty Ltd
    Operator 2:  Cape Byron Kayaks Pty Ltd

  3. Requests an extension of current Group Surf School sub-licence to Black Dog Surfing Pty Ltd for 12-months. During the first 6 months of this extension, request that NPWS, Council and stakeholders review the possibility of increasing the Group Surf Schools number to 5, including investigation of an additional licence outside of the controlled area of National Parks and Wildlife Services.

  4. Endorses an Expressions of Interest process for renewal of sub-licence for commercial equestrian access through Lot 407 DP 729057 prior to the current sub-licence expiring;

  5. Notes Lot 428 DP 729272 is no longer suitable for equestrian operations and place a hold on the issuing  of any additional sub-licence for equestrian activities until an operator is able to confirm a suitable location, confirm safe systems of work, and provide evidence of approvals from other parties, such as Crown Lands, National Parks & Wildlife Services, and Marine Parks, for any proposed access point, including required approvals to construct access pathways;

  6. Notes intention to further engage with community around potential for amendments to Policy - Commercial Activities on Coastal and Riparian Crown Reserves limited to areas outside of Walgun - Cape Byron State Conservation Area; and

  7. Delegates authorisation to negotiate and enter into future sub-licence agreements, subject to compliance with the Local Government Act 1993, to the General Manager.

The motion was put to the vote and carried.
Crs Lyon, Kay, Hauge, Ndiaye, Dods, Warth, Swain and Pugh voted in favour of the motion. 
Cr Lowe voted against the motion.

Procedural Motion:

Moved: Cr Pugh Seconded: Cr Lyon
25-370 Resolved That the meeting move out of Confidential Session.
The motion was put to the vote and carried unanimously.

Moved: Cr Pugh Seconded: Cr Ndiaye
25-335 Resolved:
That Council:

  1. Acknowledges the heartfelt loss of Paul “Campo” Campton—deeply mourned “heart and soul of this Community”—and affirms the urgent need to enhance pedestrian safety in his honour;

  2. Receives the community petition signed by Byron Shire residents, calling for:
    1. Traffic calming measures on Keith Street and Raftons Road to discourage use as bypass routes;
    2. Enhanced safety infrastructure at the Keith–Leslie–Raftons intersection;
    3. Improved pedestrian protections along Raftons Road;

  1. Notes Council already has detailed plans for pedestrian walkways on Leslie Street and Raftons Road that are waiting for grant funding to build;

  2. Immediately conducts a safety audit with the view to taking a staged approach to addressing safety concerns on Raftons Road, Keith Street and Leslie Street including:
    1. Stage 1 – utilising the Fatal Crash Response funding to investigate and, if appropriate, implement as soon as possible:
      1. reducing the speed limit on all three streets to 40km/h
      2. appropriate street signage and/or road painting including SLOW – KOALAS, SLOW – CHILDREN CROSSING or other appropriate wording on Raftons Road.
      3. installing an electronic radar speed warning signs in both directions on Raftons Road
      4. changing the Give Way sign on Leslie Street/ Raftons Road to a STOP sign.
    2. Stage 2
      1. Continue to advocate for grant funding to implement the existing Get NSW Active plans for a shared path on Leslie Street and Raftons Road
      2. Investigate changing the pedestrian crossing to a raised pedestrian crossing
      3. Investigate appropriate street lighting, considering safety and the impact on local wildlife.
    3. Stage 3 - Investigate further improvements such as 
      1. Additional traffic calming measures
      2. Options to reduce traffic on Leslie Street such as no right turn from Leslie into Granuaille, or from Raftons Road into Leslie Street
      3. Other measures as appropriate;
  1. Consults directly with those submitting the petition about any changes as well as other community stakeholders, including impacted residents, the Bangalow Childrens Centre and Bangalow Koalas;

  2. Ensures the petition and safety audit are referred without delay to the Transport and Infrastructure Advisory Committee and relevant Council staff for community engagement and execution; and

  3. Formally writes to and advocates through the following funding channels:
    1. NSW Regional Roads Fund (administered by Transport for NSW)—supporting roundabout, lighting, and pedestrian infrastructure grants Herald Sun+15NSW Government+15infrastructure.gov.au+15The Guardian+4NSW Government+4The Courier-Mail+4;
    2. Australian Government Road Safety Program (joint Commonwealth–NSW funding up to $437M to 2026) infrastructure.gov.au;
    3. Local Roads and Community Infrastructure (LRCI) Program—Phase 4 providing $1\u202Fbillion for local road enhancements The Courier-Mail+2investment.infrastructure.gov.au+2davidlittleproud.com.au+2;
    4. Roads to Recovery Program—$4.4\u202Fbillion over 2024–29 to support local road works The Guardian+13investment.infrastructure.gov.au+13Daily Telegraph+13.
The motion was put to the vote and carried unanimously.

Moved: Cr Lowe Seconded: Cr Lyon
25-373 Resolved: 
That Council:

  1. Notes the 2025 Authorisation and Delegation Instrument for Councils (Attachment 2 E2025/89483) by Transport for NSW (TfNSW);

  2. Renames the Local Traffic Committee to the Local Transport Forum and updates the Terms of Reference to align with the 2025 Authorisation and Delegation Instrument for Councils;

  3. Adopts the new streamlined processes as outlined in A guide for councils using the Authorisation and Delegation Instrument;

  4. Notes that functions delegated to Council by the 2025 Authorisation and Delegation Prescribed Traffic Control Devices and Regulation of Traffic may be carried out and/or subdelegated by the General Manager;

  5. Acknowledges that the General Manager has been delegated (Resolution 25-114):
    1. "ALL the powers and functions of the Council subject to the express conditions or limitations as listed separately in the schedule..." including:
        1. BSC105 Administration of roads under the Roads Act 1993 - Delegations do not include the power to make an application for the permanent closure of any road for which Council is the roads authority.
        2. BSC115 Delegations to Council - Traffic Management and Roads Act 1993 Pedestrian Works Temporary Delegation to Councils Road Transport Act 2013 (Temporary to 30 June 2026) - Carry out functions set out in Schedule 1 of "Traffic Management and Pedestrian Works Temporary Delegation to Councils" dated 12 December 2023 (E2023/65912) from Transport for NSW subject to the Delegation's Schedule 4. In addition, be authorised to install or display (or interfere with, alter or remove) any prescribed traffic control device as set out in the TfNSW "Traffic Signs Database" and indicated as "Delegated to Council for Authorisation - Yes", as required to give effect to functions exercised under this delegation, including any portable traffic control lights, but NOT any internally illuminated traffic control device; and

  6. Acknowledges that the General Manager's instrument of delegation allows  "Where any function or power provided by these delegations is amended by a subsequent Act or Regulation, the delegations continue so amended," and accordingly amends BSC115 to:
    1. BSC115 Delegations to Council - Prescribed Traffic Control Devises and Regulation of Traffic (Roads Act 1993, Road Transport Act 2013) - Carry out functions set out in Schedule 1 of "Prescribed Traffic Control Devices and Regulation of Traffic" dated 21 July 2025 (E2025/89483) from Transport for NSW subject to the Delegation's Schedule 4. In addition, be authorised to install or display (or interfere with, alter or remove) any prescribed traffic control device as set out in the TfNSW "Traffic Signs Database" as required to give effect to functions exercised under this delegation, including any portable traffic control lights, but NOT any internally illuminated traffic control device.

","reportContent":null,"minutesDiscussion":"Moved: Cr Hauge Seconded: Cr Lowe
Moved that Council:

  1. Commits to upholding the highest ethical standards in all its procurement and investment decisions; 

  2. Notes: 

    1. Section 2.1 of Council’s Investments Policy:
      “The Council’s criteria relating to an SRI are those which: 
      - direct investment towards the socially and environmentally productive activities listed below 
      - avoid investment in the socially and environmentally harmful activities  listed below 
      … 
      Socially harmful activities are considered to be: 
      - abuse of Human Rights and Labour Rights 
      - involvement in bribery/corruption 
      - production or supply of armaments 
      - manufacture of alcohol, tobacco or gambling products”
    2. Council’s Business Ethics Statement (which guides Ethical Behaviour as  per Part 4 of Council’s Procurement and Purchasing Policy): 
      “Council will ensure its business relationships are ethical, honest, fair,  and consistent. Business dealings will be as transparent and as open to  public scrutiny as possible.” 

  3. Notes:

    1. the International Court of Justice (ICJ) in its Advisory Opinion of 19th  July 2024 declared Israel's prolonged occupation of Palestinian territories  as illegal in its entirety, constituting violations of peremptory norms  including the right to self-determination and the prohibition on racial  segregation and apartheid; 

    2. the issuing, by the ICJ, of provisional measures requiring Israel to  prevent genocidal acts; 

    3. the International Criminal Court (ICC) issued arrest warrants for Israeli  officials for war crimes and crimes against humanity

  4. Notes that:

    1. On 27 June 2024 Council passed a resolution condemning the actions of the Israeli Government in Gaza, called for all hostages to be released and calling for a permanent cease fire. This motion also acknowledges the trauma that this conflict was causing for many in our local community.

    2. This Motion proposes that we consider human rights impacts in local planning and procurement, aims to create awareness and enable solidarity at a local level, and acknowledges that meaningful economic pressure requires action from all levels of government. 

  5. Notes the list of organisations identified in Attachment A, compiled from United Nations sources: 

    1. “Business enterprises involved in listed activities” in the UN Human Rights Council “Database of Business Enterprises  Pursuant to Human Rights Council Resolutions 31/36 and 53/25“  (UNHCR, 2023), which details all business enterprises involved in  specified activities related to the Israeli settlements in the Occupied  Palestinian Territory, including East Jerusalem (available here);
    2. “From economy of occupation to economy of genocide” Report of the Special Rapporteur on the situation of human rights in the Palestinian territories occupied since 1967 (Albanese, July 2025) which details how corporate entities have profited from Israel’s economy of illegal occupation, apartheid and now, genocide (available here);
   and that these sources are currently being reviewed and updated and our policy may have to be updated to add or remove organisations in the future.

  1. Requests the General Manager to ensure that Council’s procurement and investment decisions do not contribute to grave human rights violations or international crimes in Gaza and the West Bank, such that:

    1. Statutory and legal obligations, including the Ministerial Investment Order (2011), are met; 

    2. Council ceases to directly invest in or conduct business with any company identified in Part 4, where this is not reasonably practical, Council creates a plan to transition away within 12 months, or a reasonably practical timeframe;

    3. Adverse financial implications are reported to council;

    4. A compliance mechanism is developed to screen new and renewing contracts and investments against the database identified in Part 5 

  2. Delegates to the General Manager implementation of Part 5, and requests a  report on any procurement or investment decisions where it is not reasonably practicable to comply with this policy under 5(b). Council may determine to write to these companies outlining human rights concerns at this time.

  3. Reviews its Investments Policy, Procurement and Purchasing Policy, and Business Ethics statement to strengthen Council’s commitment to the social objectives set out therein, and also to reflect UN Guiding Principles on Business and Human Rights (UNGPs).

The motion was put to the vote and declared lost.
Crs Lyon, Dods, Warth, Swain, and Pugh voted against the motion.

 

Foreshadowed Motion:

Moved: Cr Pugh Seconded: Cr Hauge
25-328 Resolved:
That Council: 

1. Commits to upholding the highest ethical standards in all its procurement and  investment decisions; 

2. Notes: 

a. Section 2.1 of Council’s Investments Policy: 

“The Council’s criteria relating to an SRI are those which: 

- direct investment towards the socially and environmentally productive  activities listed below 

- avoid investment in the socially and environmentally harmful activities  listed below 

… 

Socially harmful activities are considered to be: 

- abuse of Human Rights and Labour Rights 

- involvement in bribery/corruption 

- production or supply of armaments 

- manufacture of alcohol, tobacco or gambling products” 

b. Council’s Business Ethics Statement (which guides Ethical Behaviour as  per Part 4 of Council’s Procurement and Purchasing Policy): 

“Council will ensure its business relationships are ethical, honest, fair,  and consistent. Business dealings will be as transparent and as open to  public scrutiny as possible.” 

3. Notes: 

a. the International Court of Justice (ICJ) in its Advisory Opinion of 19th  July 2024 declared Israel's prolonged occupation of Palestinian territories  as illegal in its entirety, constituting violations of peremptory norms  including the right to self-determination and the prohibition on racial  segregation and apartheid; 

b. the issuing, by the ICJ, of provisional measures requiring Israel to  prevent genocidal acts; 

c. the International Criminal Court (ICC) issued arrest warrants for Israeli  officials for war crimes and crimes against humanity

  1. Notes that 
    1. On 27 June 2024 Council passed a resolution condemning the actions of the Israeli Government in Gaza, called for all hostages to be released and calling for a permanent cease fire. This motion also acknowledge the trauma that this conflict was causing for many in our local community.
    2. Whilst this Motion proposes that we consider human rights impacts in local procurement, and aims to create awareness and enable solidarity at a local level, council acknowledges that foreign policy remains the domain of federal government.
  2. Notes: 
    1. The list of organisations identified in list B “Business enterprises involved in listed activities” in the UN Human Rights Council “Database of Business Enterprises  Pursuant to Human Rights Council Resolutions 31/36 and 53/25“  (UNHCR, 2023), which details all business enterprises involved in  specified activities related to the Israeli settlements in the Occupied  Palestinian Territory, including East Jerusalem (available here); 
    2. that this list is currently being reviewed and updated by the Office of the High Commissioner of Human Rights at the United Nations and our policy may have to be updated to add or remove organisations in the future.

6.  Requests the General Manager to ensure that Council’s procurement and investment decisions do not contribute to grave human rights violations or international crimes in Gaza and the West Bank, such that: 

a. Statutory and legal obligations, including the Ministerial Investment Order (2011), are met; 

b. Council ceases to directly invest in or conduct business with any company identified in Part 4 and creates a plan to transition away within 12 months, or a reasonably practical timeframe; Where it is not reasonably practical to implement this, the General Manager will report this to council

c. Adverse financial implications are reported to council; 

d. A compliance mechanism is developed to screen new and renewing contracts and investments against the database identified in Part 5 

7. Delegates to the General Manager implementation of Part 5, and requests a report on any procurement or investment decisions where it is not reasonably practicable to comply with this policy. Council may determine to write to these companies outlining human rights concerns at this time.

8. Reviews its Investments Policy, Procurement and Purchasing Policy, and  Business Ethics statement to strengthen Council’s commitment to the social  objectives set out therein, and also to reflect UN Guiding Principles on Business  and Human Rights (UNGPs).

Question No. 1 Clifford Street/Broken Head Road Intersection

Elizabeth Levy asked the following question:
Regarding the March resolution on preparation for safety improvements for the said intersection: how far has action progressed with developing a complicit roundabout design and has Council undertaken valuations of likely necessary land acquisition or held any preliminary discussions with the relevant land holders? Further, in accordance with the resolution, what funding was earmarked in the Quarterly Budget Review for any or all of these purposes?

Acting Director Infrastructure Services responded:
A report is being currently being prepared for Council's consideration, and that will cover the points raised in that question.

Question No. 2 Special Entertainment Precinct

Brooke Crowle, on behalf of the People of Byron, asked the following question, which was read by staff.
The consultation has not been very clear about a number of aspects buried in the SEP. It says in the Position Paper, (Early Phase 1) May to September that during this period the Council will be "submitting the Planning Proposal for Gateway Determination" does this mean 'changing the LEP/DCP' - if not, can the Council tell the community if changing the LEP/DCP has to happen before you vote to proceed with the Trial?
This is not a question but a request as many people are concerned that the next period of Public Exhibition and Consultation (Phase 2) states "December to early 2026" - this sounds like January school holidays etc. and is when people in Byron are either at their busiest with summer visitors or taking time out. Can this be reviewed and pushed back to February/March 2026?

Director Sustainable Environment and Economy responded:
I'll provide more in detail, in writing, but there was an anomaly in one of the tables that was published, which gave a conflict in terms of the phases, easily corrected, and I'll do that in writing in the next Agenda and updated on the webpage.

The Mayor also took the question on notice.

Question No. 3 Supporting Rail Service and Bike Trail within Railway Corridor

Lydia Kindred, on behalf of Northern Rivers Rail Ltd, asked the following question:
That Northern Rivers Rail Ltd ask the Byron Shire Councillors to move and carry a motion to express ‘in principle’ support for a low emission train service, with the potential bike/walking path to also run, within the railway corridor, along the length of the Byron Shire section of line, between Booyong and Yelgun, to create a more sustainable future for the Northern Rivers.

Cr Lyon responded: I’m not supportive.

Councillors asked clarifying questions regarding the survey of businesses. The speaker was asked and clarified that the question was about whether Councillors were, in principle, supportive of a rail service from Booyong to Yelgun, with a bike trail.

Cr Lowe responded: In principle, I would support – if you could have both, I would absolutely support that. I don’t know if you can, but in principle, I’m 100% supportive of both.

Cr Dods responded: In principle, I support the current Resolution to look at investigating mixed-use between Mullum and Byron. I think there’s a lot of merits there, obviously the cost being the prohibitive one but if that could be integrated into some kind of mixed-use transit orientated development between Mullum and Byron – they’re the two biggest population centres, and there’s a lot of travelling between the two – that’s a good idea. I’d ask you, Lydia, don’t you think you’d be more successful if you re-focused your efforts on something more pragmatic like that? A train to Booyong, it’s just never going to happen, there’s no demand for it, there’s no link to any population centre or business. Why not focus your group’s efforts on something more tangible like just a Byron to Mullum light rail service?

Cr Swain responded: In my short time on Council, I realise that it’s the people who just keep on at it that maybe get things done. However, I can’t support this, I think that it’s unrealistic. Everybody loves a train, I love a train, it would be so beautiful, but I just can’t see that it’s going to happen so that’s my position.

Mayor Ndiaye responded: I guess I would say that I’m comfortable with Council’s current position of exploring it between Mullumbimby and Byron. Similarly to what Cr Dods has said, I think I can see that as a viable option but given that the surrounding Shires have gone with a rail trail – it’s been very popular – and there’s a lot of people that I speak to that are very in favour of that going ahead. I’m definitely in favour of Council’s current position, and I’m going to say thank you very much.

Moved: Cr Ndiaye Seconded: Cr Lyon
25-398 Resolved: 
That Council replaces Resolution 25-206 with the following amended resolution.
 
That Council:

  1. Proceeds with the Planning Proposal (Attachment 1 #E2025/32579) to amend Byron LEP 2014 to rezone the subject land from RU2 Rural Landscape to E4 General Industrial, C2 Environmental Conservation and C3 Environmental Management, and apply other relevant planning controls;
 
  1. Accepts the applicant’s letter of offer to enter into a Planning Agreement (Attachment 11 #E2025/42998) with Council as part of this Planning Proposal;
 
  1. Requires that a draft Planning Agreement be prepared in accordance with the letter of offer and exhibited concurrently with the Planning Proposal;

  2. As part of requesting a Gateway determination, Council advises NSW Planning’s of the requirement for the proponent to work with Crown Lands, who will work with Bundjalung of Byron Bay Aboriginal Corporation “BOBBAC” (Arakwal), to:
  1. confirm both Crown Lands BOBBAC support the proposed rezoning of Lot 7022 in DP 1113424
  2. advise of any requirements either have around actions that need to occur prior to a Gateway determination and/or post a Gateway determination but during the public exhibition period.  

  1. Pending a positive Gateway determination and completion of further supporting information, undertakes public exhibition of the planning proposal in accordance with the determination requirements;

  2. Notes that legal drafting of the draft Planning Agreement will be prepared and exhibited alongside the Planning Proposal; and

  3. Considers a Submissions Report post-exhibition that includes any recommended changes to the Planning Proposal for final adoption.

The motion was put to the vote and carried unanimously.

  1. That pursuant to Section 10A(2)(f) of the Local Government Act 1993, Council resolves to move into Confidential Session and into Committee to discuss the report Outcome of Property Audit (Res 24-503 and Res 25-160).

  2. That the reason for closing the meeting to the public to consider this item be that the report contains matters affecting the security of the council, councillors, council staff, or council property

  3. That on the balance it is considered that receipt and discussion of the matter in open Council would be contrary to the public interest, as the discussion will include sensitive information about Council property.
The motion was put to the vote and carried unanimously.

25-400 Resolved:

25-401 Resolved:
That Council move out of Committee and resume the Planning Meeting.
The motion was put to the vote and carried unanimously.

Moved: Cr Hauge Seconded: Cr Ndiaye
25-393 Resolved: 

That Council:

  1. Expands the audit of Council-owned or managed land and buildings, undertaken in response to Resolution 24-503 and Resolution 25-160, to include:
    1. Land within a 5km radius of towns and villages, including industrial areas
    2. Road reserve tracts >200m2
    3. Community Land that is not used for public recreation and >200m2

  2. Progress an investigation into the provision of emergency housing at a Council owned site (The address of the land is confidential to protect the personal safety of the vulnerable people accessing services at the address and to maintain law and order) and consider a budget allocation for this work in the next quarterly budget review.

  3. Progress work with Queer Family to identify a suitable site (including neighbour/stakeholder engagement) for the following sites:
    1. Lot B DP 6733 Station St Mullumbimby
    2. BLD237 Bangalow Scout Hall, listed in the draft property audit has having an expired lease but no other constraints
    3. Lot 45 DP 772011

The motion was put to the vote and carried.
Cr Lyon voted against the motion.

Moved: Cr Ndiaye Seconded: Cr Hauge
25-385 Resolved: 
That Council:

  1. Notes the outcomes of the Brunswick Heads Community Opportunity Workshop held on 24 March 2025, along with the resulting draft Community Action Plan (Attachment 1);

  2. Updates the Community Action Plan to specify maintenance timelines and agency responsibility for the action items identified in Appendix A of the plan.

  3. Acknowledges the complexity of land ownership and responsibilities in Brunswick Heads. That multiple stakeholders manage different parts of the foreshore, and successful implementation of the Community Action Plan will require ongoing collaboration and coordination;

  4. Acknowledges that the Community Action Plan outlines potential actions to address the issues and opportunities raised during the Community Opportunity Workshop. That these actions are intended to be pursued collaboratively, subject to available funding, capital works programs, and agency capacity;

  5. Notes the establishment of and supports the ongoing quarterly meetings of the Brunswick Heads Interagency Group as discussed in the Community Action Plan and invites community representatives to at least one interagency meeting per year; and

  6. Thanks all stakeholders for their participation in this matter.

The motion was put to the vote and carried unanimously.

The meeting adjourned at 6:32pm for a break and reconvened at 6:50pm.

That Council:

  1. Notes all Essential Public Asset Restoration works that are completed are financially closed and further weed management works cannot be funded by Natural Disaster funding arrangements;

  2. Seeks Essential Public Asset Restoration funding for the long-term maintenance of revegetation works currently under construction in order to minimise the risk of weed growth in the future;

  3. Ensures all future works environmental planning approvals under the Infrastructure Recovery Program recommends long term maintenance of any revegetation works in order to minimise the risk of weed growth in the future; and

  4. Receives a further report if the proposed measures in 2 and 3 are not supported by the Reconstruction Authority.

The motion was put to the vote and carried unanimously.

Moved: Cr Lyon Seconded: Cr Swain
25-437 Resolved: 
That Council:

  1. Notes the works progressed since the previous Committee meeting and acknowledges the status updates to:
    1. The Broken Head Road Upgrade Concept Design Report completion. This correlates to the advancement of item 8 of the 64 priority projects.
    2. Coogera Detention Basin's Construction Completion - item 9 of the 64 priority projects
    3. The project 'Investigate SGB and Fern Beach Flood Levy Upgrades' - item 21 of the 64 priority projects
    4. The project 'Investigate Flood pump for Western SGB levee' - item 22 of the 64 priority projects.
    5. Acknowledges the updated project Gantt chart displaying project statuses of the Flood Advisory Committee's 64 priority projects.

  2. Incorporates the 'high priority' findings documented in Table 3 of the 'Investigate SGB and Fern Beach Flood Levy Upgrades' project's report into Council's works program for financial year 2026-2027.

  3. Notes the $4.2 million cost estimation to implement a pump system for South Golden Beach West.
    1. Acknowledges this is a significant infrastructure investment with ongoing cost implications for Council.
    2. Recommends Council investigate the traditional three way program of wet proofing, house raising and buy back for South Golden Beach West.
    3. Recommends Council prioritise penstocks as a secondary back-up for flap gate failure at South Golden Beach outlets.
    4. Recommends Council ameliorate and improve the existing gravity drainage system in South Golden Beach prior to the introduction of future pump inclusions.

Moved: Cr Warth Seconded: Cr Dods
25-411 Resolved: 
That Council submits a Motion to the LGNSW Annual Conference on 23-25 November 2025 calling on Local Government NSW to:

  1. Acknowledge the chronic underfunding of many NSW Councils;

  2. Lobby the NSW Government for Land Tax reforms, where:
    1. A portion of Land Tax raised within the LGA to be allocated directly and untied into the relevant Council’s General Fund; and
    2. In LGAs where land values are not as high, an allocation of Land Tax can be drawn from the consolidated pool of NSW Land Tax; and

  3. Note that the current level of Land Tax in NSW is causing serious economic and social problems and has a direct inflationary effect and therefore this is not to be seen as an opportunity to raise extra Land Tax.

The motion was put to the vote and carried unanimously.

","reportContent":null,"minutesDiscussion":"
Moved: Cr Ndiaye Seconded: Cr Hauge
25-384 Resolved: 
That Council:

  1. Supports the following motion to be considered for inclusion in the Local Government NSW Conference:
    1. Maternity, paternity and adoption leave:
      1. That establishing formal parental leave entitlements for elected Mayors and Councillors, including provisions for maternity, paternity, and adoption leave be added to LG NSW’s Policy Platform - Part 19 Councillor Conditions and Remuneration.
      2. Advocates for legislative amendments to align Section 254A of the Local Government Act with the parental leave timeframe provided by Services Australia.

    2. Reviewing the current remuneration framework and ensuring access to sick leave and carers leave:
      1. Supports legislative reform to provide Mayors and Councillors with access to sick leave and carers leave.
      2. Urges the New South Wales Government to review and overhaul the current remuneration framework for Mayors and Councillors to better reflect the scope and complexity of their roles, including the removal of Section 242A of the Local Government Act 1993. This would enable the Local Government Remuneration Tribunal to use the annual base salary of a Member of the New South Wales Legislative Assembly as a benchmark for determining mayoral and councillor pay.
      3. Ensures that Acting Mayors and Councillors are fairly compensated without penalising those who take leave for personal reasons or family responsibilities.
      4. Ensures that Deputy Mayors, when filling in for a Mayor during their necessary leave of absence (such as for maternity, sick, or carers leave), are appropriately remunerated for taking on additional responsibilities, without requiring the Mayor to forgo their stipend; and

  2. Writes to the Minister for Local Government and relevant State MPs advocating for fair and appropriate remuneration and conditions for Mayors and Councillors as set out in LGNSW Policy Platform Part 19 and parental leave.

The motion was put to the vote and carried unanimously.

Moved: Cr Ndiaye Seconded: Cr Pugh
25-415 Resolved: 
That Council:

  1. Congratulates the NSW Government on the announcement of the establishment of the Great Koala National Park, and thanks Premier Chris Minns, Environment Minister Penny Sharpe, and Agriculture Minister Tara Moriarty for fulfilling their commitment to biodiversity protection, through:
    1. The safeguarding of habitat for:
      1. Over 12,000 koalas,
      2. Approximately 36,000 nationally endangered Southern Greater Gliders,
      3. More than 100 other threatened species, including the Spotted-tailed Quoll, Hastings River Mouse, and Rufous Scrub-bird;
    2. The protection of old-growth forests and critical water catchments;
    3. The declaration of a 476,000-hectare reserve, including an immediate moratorium on timber harvesting within the proposed park boundary.

  2. Notes the Premier's commitment to funding programs that support:
    1. The employment of Indigenous Rangers, recognising and protecting cultural heritage and values within the park;
    2. Transition support for displaced timber industry workers and businesses;
    3. Ecological restoration of degraded areas;
    4. The development of an eco-tourism economy for the North Coast region.

  3. Recognises and commends the decades of tireless and principled advocacy by community members and environmental organisations, in particular the Bellingen Environmental Council, Nambucca Valley Conservation Association, Clarence Environment Centre, North Coast Environment Council (NCEC, National Parks Association (NPA), and North East Forest Alliance (NEFA) and the North Coast Environment Council (NCEC), whose extraordinary activism and independent research has been instrumental in:
    1. Defending and preserving endangered species habitat from native forest logging;
    2. Maintaining public and political pressure for stronger environmental protections;
    3. Championing a transition away from native forest logging toward a more sustainable and biodiverse future.
       
  4. Affirms that Byron Shire Council will continue to work with relevant stakeholders to support and protect local koala populations, including by:
    1. Implementing and strengthening the Byron Coast Comprehensive Koala Plan of Management;
    2. Supporting habitat restoration and tree-planting projects on both public and private land;
    3. Collaborating with Traditional Owners, local landholders, Landcare groups, and wildlife organisations to identify and protect critical koala corridors;
    4. Advocating for state and federal funding for koala conservation initiatives in the Byron region;
    5. Ensuring planning and development decisions are consistent with koala habitat protection;
    6. Promoting community education and engagement around koala conservation efforts.

The motion was put to the vote and carried unanimously.

25-430 Resolved: 

That Council:

  1. Withdraws from the grant funded signalised intersection project;

  2. Seeks funding to produce concept plans for both a ‘mini roundabout’ option (as per attachment E2025/102435), and a standard roundabout option, incorporating pedestrian safety elements, and design solutions from;
    1. Austroads ‘Guide to Road Design Part 7: New and Emerging Treatments, part 2.5 Roundabouts with Raised Platforms on Approach’, and
    2. TfNSW’s ‘Design of Roads and Streets Manual’;

  3. Seeks design input from Council’s Place Planning team to incorporate place making elements and defined arrival experience elements into the designs;

  4. Presents both roundabout concept plans to the Transport and Infrastructure Advisory Committee;

  5. Seeks formal written comment from TfNSW on both roundabout options, and for those comments to be shared with Councillors;

  6. Seeks future funding opportunities to deliver the project, subject to further community consultation; 

  7. Receives a report within 12 months on whether a roundabout within the current road reserve is possible and supported by TfNSW; and

  8. Seeks alternative funding for pedestrian upgrades at the RSL lifecare/Beech Dr as described in previous resolutions.

The motion was put to the vote and carried.
Crs Swain and Pugh voted against the motion.

Question No. 1  13.13 Staff Report - Clifford St BHR Intersection Upgrade


Elizabeth Levy (as read by staff) asked the following question:
I was told that the report would cover my previous question on this issue, but it does not address:
Has Council undertaken valuations of likely necessary land acquisitions for a compliant roundabout and/or had any preliminary discussions with the relevant land holders? What funding was earmarked in the Quarterly Budget Review for these purposes?

The Mayor took the question on notice.


Question No. 2  57 Station Street, Mullumbimby


Gillian Lomath (as read by staff) asked the following question:
I have heard that the development for 57 Station St Mullumbimby is to be revised, and that a repeat public exhibition will occur. Can you give a 100% firm commitment to that new public exhibition process?

The Mayor took the question on notice.


Question No. 3  Destination Management Funding


Sarah Anderson asked the following question:
For the current financial year and next two financial years, what does Council intend to spend on pro-active Destination Management? For example, strategy and planning consultation for destination management, product development (e.g. supporting the development of new bookable tourism experiences that align with community values), storytelling of the Byron story (via PR, marketing, social media). Please exclude infrastructure, waste management and signage.

The Mayor took the question on notice.


Question No. 4  Byron Shire Council Relationship with Landcom


Jan Barham (as read by staff) asked the following question:
Will council release the Terms Sheet Agreement with Landcom which was entered into in 2022 and updated in June 2023 update to inform the community of the scope and arrangements relating to public land, 57 Station Street and the Public Interest, noting that any commercial in confidence issues may be redacted to allow publication as per Guidelines issued by the NSW Information and Privacy Commissioner? If not, could an explanation be provided the reasons for non-disclosure.

The Mayor took the question on notice.


Question No. 5  11.1 Petition - 57 Station Street Mullumbimby


Sonia Laverty (as read by staff) asked the following question:
Could council provide advice on the next stage for 57 Stations Street, including a timeframe for public exhibition if an amended DA is proposed and update BSC website and whether the NRPP has been notified of the delays and if it’s necessary to change a date set or planned for a determination of DA 10.2025.212.1?

The Mayor took the question on notice.


Question No. 6  Mullumbimby Road Stage 2 Documentation


Sharon McGrath (as read by staff) asked the following question:
In order to provide transparency and ensure the community is fully informed about the Stage 2 upgrade of Mullumbimby Road, will Council release the following documentation:
- Project budgets and any supporting grant application documentation
- Construction program, including sequencing and duration of works
- Summary of planned night works
- Cost estimates and feasibility analysis for night works
- Risk assessments for detour routes (Coolamon Scenic Drive and Myocum Road), with staff sign-off
- Economic impact assessment for Mullumbimby and surrounding towns, including Brunswick Heads
- Traffic Impact Assessments (TIA) and Road Safety Audits (RSA) for Mullumbimby Road, Coolamon Scenic Drive, and Myocum Road, including the roundabouts at their intersections with Hinterland Way and Brunswick Valley Way
And if Council is not prepared to release this information, will it please state the reasons why?

The Mayor took the question on notice.


Question No. 7  Councillors Awareness of Detour Routes & Duration


Sharon McGrath (as read by staff) asked the following question:
Were Councillors informed of both the duration and the currently advertised detour routes — via Myocum Road and Coolamon Scenic Drive (Tunnel Road) — at the time they approved the Mullumbimby Road upgrade works?

The Mayor took the question on notice.

Questions
Question No. 2 Special Entertainment Precinct
Maxine Hawker, asked the following question, which was read by staff:
I have not been able to find any information regarding what will deem the trial a success or failure. What will be measured? For example, will it be economic such as business trading, or number of people in the SEP precinct at certain times or positive/negative feedback from businesses?

The Mayor took the question on notice.

Question No. 3 Special Entertainment Precinct
Brooke Crowle, on behalf of the People of Byron, asked the following question, which was read by staff:
Has council finalised the audit of all licensed venues with the Development Consent details and licensing approvals in the proposed SEP area? If so, when will it be released?

The Mayor took the question on notice.

Question No. 4 SEP Compliance
Alison Drover asked the following question, which was read by staff:
How does Council plan to address resourcing compliance and other to ensure there is a reasonable response time i.e. for noise complaints, parking issues etc, garbage overflow, breaching alcohol laws etc. which will increase as a result of the SEP. These issues are not being dealt with now, so how is this going to be funded and resourced?

The Mayor took the question on notice.

Question No. 5 Mullumbimby Road Stage 2 Document Request
Sharon McGrath asked the following question:
How long do Councillors consider is an appropriate period of time for community members to wait for documentation that is fundamental to transparency on such a critical issue, and at what point does the delay become unacceptable?

Manager Works (Mr Frumpui) responded:
The Stage 2 documentation has been finalised now and should be available on Council's website. Under "Mullumbimby Road upgrade", it should be at the bottom, when you scroll down with the updates for the project list, there should be all the documentation for Stage 1 and Stage 2 as well.

Question No. 6 Mullumbimby Road Stage 2 Grant Variation
Sharon McGrath asked the following question:
Regarding the Mullumbimby Road upgrade, has Council sought a variation from the relevant grant authorities to allow for modification of the construction plan which would provide for two-way traffic, thereby minimising disruption, economic impacts and public safety?

Manager Works (Mr Frumpui) responded:
No, we haven't applied for it.

The Mayor also took the follow up questions on notice.

Question No. 7 Merivale Group Development and Byron Public School
Rachael Calvert asked the following question, which was provided via an audio recording:
Given that clause 2.5 of the Byron Shire Council's Liquor Licensing and Approvals Policy states the council may not provide approval for any new licensed venues within 100 metres of any of a school, place of worship, residential homes, etc. - can you please explain why the Byron Bay Public School with over 600 students (and only 69 metres away) and 2 different church organisations were not notified of the size, nature, and scale of the Merivale redevelopment including the proposed expansion and how can the Byron Bay community (especially our most vulnerable members - the children) be confident that you are advocating for their amenity and safety before the commercial interests of the Merivale Group, and does the community assessment report show how this has been evidenced?

The Mayor took the question on notice.

Moved: Cr Lyon Seconded: Cr Hauge
25-468 Resolved: 
That Council:
  
  1. Adopts the following documents with amendments as detailed in point 2 and 3:
    • Affordable Housing Contribution Policy 2025 (Attachment 6 - E2025/97691);
    • Affordable Housing Contribution Scheme Procedure 2025 (Attachment 7 - E2025/99159),
    • Affordable Housing Planning Agreement Procedure 2025 (Attachment 8 - E2025/97694); and
    • Affordable Housing Contributions Distribution Plan 2025 (Attachment 9 - E2025/97696).
  1. Amend the Affordable Housing Contribution Scheme Procedure 2025 as follows:
    • Amend Section 2.2 point 3 to read:
       ‘Council staff will determine if sufficient grounds have been established to justify a review of the impact of the factors identified on the viability of the adopted contribution rate and, if satisfied, is responsible for undertaking the review.’
    • Amend Section 2.2 point 6 to read:
       ‘Should exceptional circumstances be established as impacting on the viability of levying affordable housing contributions, the elected Council may amend the contribution rate to be applied to the maximum reassessed viable contribution, or 50% of the original rate, whichever is greater. In circumstances where development yield has reduced or unforeseen infrastructure costs have impacted viability, a reduced rate will only be available where:
      • In the case of an applicant arguing that development yield has reduced, if the yields specified in the planning proposal are consistent with the reduced yield identified in the application for review of the contribution rate; and/or
      • In the case of an applicant submitting that unforeseen infrastructure costs will impact viability, that the projected increased costs are borne by the applicant or subsequent developer and not shared with or subsidised by another unrelated party, such as government or an adjoining landowner.’

  2. Amends the Affordable Housing Contributions Distribution Plan 2025 as follows:
    • Amend the final list item in Section 8 to read ‘Monitoring and reporting requirements to enable Council to fulfill the reporting obligations set out in Section 9 below;’
    • Delete the last two sentences of the paragraph at the end of Section 8;
    • Include a new list item in Section 8 to read ‘Any post-agreement arrangements.’
    • Include a new sentence at the end of part 8 that reads: ‘Council may place a covenant on the title of any land it provides to ensure its continued use for the purposes of affordable housing.’
  1. That the amended documents be published on Council’s website.

The motion was put to the vote and carried unanimously.

That Council:

  1. Notes the update on Resolution 23-602 and that there are no new or alternate legislative mechanisms in NSW to constrain the future use of dwellings for the purposes of providing affordable and/or permanent accommodation instead of short-term rental accommodation.

  2. Notes financial incentives cited in this report are enabled, funded and implemented by State Government, not local councils as far beyond their financial capacity.

  3. Notes that an expression of interest to landowners to convert their short-term rental properties into long-term rentals will not be progressed.

  4. Instead of progressing the expression of interest, will rely on other legislation, policies, and programs to address local housing needs.

The motion was put to the vote and carried unanimously.

[IGNORE_INDENT][OUTLINE_NUMBER_FULL_NO_PERIOD][AGENDA_ITEM_NAME]
","reportContent":null,"minutesDiscussion":"Cr Lyon left the meeting at 5:55pm.

Cr Lyon returned to the meeting at 6:08pm.

Moved: Cr Hauge Seconded: Cr Lowe
25-450 Resolved: 
That Council:

  1. Writes to the Prime Minister Anthony Albanese, NSW Premier Chris Minns, NSW Minister for Recovery Janelle Saffin, and Federal Minister for Emergency Management Jenny McAllister:
    1. Expressing Council's concern at the lack of consultation regarding the $100 million re-allocation of funding for raises and/or retrofits to buybacks under the NSW Resilient Homes Program;
        
    2. Requesting increased transparency from the NSW Reconstruction Authority regarding:
      1. Which homes in Byron Shire lost eligibility for assistance as a result of this funding reduction;
      2. Clear timelines for program delivery and community communication;
      3. Updated statistical breakdowns of Byron Shire applications, approvals, and completions across all Resilient Homes Program streams;
      4. Monthly publicly available updates of these statistical breakdowns; 
      5. A searchable case-by-case map for Byron Shire residents informing them of which priority stream (1, 2, 3, or 4) their home falls into and the anticipated timeframe for delivery;
         
    3. Requesting an increase to the $1.5 billion identified as needed to deliver 6,000 buybacks, raises, and retrofits across the Northern Rivers region, as promised to communities following the 2022 floods;

    4. Advocating for comprehensive flood resilience funding to ensure raises and/or retrofits are available for all homes below the 1% AEP flood levels, recognising that climate change is increasing flood frequency and intensity;
       
    5. Calling for equitable program delivery ensuring raises and retrofits are fairly funded and accessible to all eligible households without discrimination based on location, property value, or socioeconomic status;
       
    6. Requesting urgent Commonwealth co-funding to address the $620m shortfall between current program funding ($880 million) and the community's legitimate expectation of $1.5 billion in comprehensive flood recovery assistance for at least 2,000 buybacks and 4,000 houses raises and retrofits; and
       
  2. Supports the Mayor to write to Byron Shire's Federal and State parliamentary representatives seeking their support for this advocacy, and to coordinate with other Northern Rivers councils (e.g. through the NRJO) for joint advocacy initiatives.

The motion was put to the vote and carried unanimously.

Moved: Cr Ndiaye Seconded: Cr Pugh
25-459 Resolved: 
That Council:
 
  1. Notes that Byron Shire Council has declared a housing emergency and is responding strongly to address community concerns over housing and homelessness and to build more housing. This includes conducting a land audit, building affordable housing on council carparks, releasing new land at Saddle Road and elsewhere, introducing an Affordable Housing contribution scheme, supporting the Assertive Outreach Program and the Ending Rough Sleeping Collaboration, introducing a comprehensive Residential Strategy, amongst other initiatives.

  2. Notes with concern that the Environmental Planning and Assessment (Planning System Reforms) Bill 2025 reduces local planning control and transparency, increases the risk of corruption in planning processes, and will significantly limit community input and confidence in planning decisions.

  3. Notes that the expressed purpose of these changes are to enable the building of housing while expanding the scope of the laws to apply to all development applications including industrial, commercial and infrastructure development.

  4. Notes that key issues for Byron Shire include the removal of public interest and environmental considerations in decision-making, the loss of vital biodiversity and habitat protections, the exclusion of climate change impacts, reduced community participation, and compressed determination timeframes that could result in automatic approvals.

  5. Writes to the Premier, the Leader of the Opposition, the Minister and Shadow Ministers for Planning and Public Spaces, and the Member for Ballina, expressing Council’s strong opposition to the passage of the Bill in its current form and requesting a formal public consultation process before any further progression of the reforms.

  6. Advocates through the Northern Rivers Joint Organisation and other regional bodies for a coordinated and public response to the Bill.

  7. Submits a motion to the 2025 LGNSW Conference calling on the NSW Government to withdraw the Bill and work collaboratively with councils and communities to deliver genuine, evidence-based planning reform that supports building more and better housing without undermining our planning system.

  8. Encourages the community to make a submission if the Bill is referred to a Parliamentary inquiry.

The motion was put to the vote and carried unanimously.

Procedural Motion:
Moved: Cr Ndiaye Seconded: Cr Lowe
25-453 Resolved:
That Council move into Committee to allow for free debate.
The motion was put to the vote and carried unanimously.

Moved: Cr Ndiaye Seconded: Cr Kay
25-475 Resolved:
That Council move out of Committee and resume the Ordinary Meeting.

Moved: Cr Ndiaye Seconded: None
25-454 Resolved: 
That Council:

  1. Confirms that during Stage 2 of the Mullumbimby Road upgrade (between Gulgan Road and Saddle Road), road access into Mullumbimby will remain open to inbound (one-way) traffic for the duration of the works.

  2. Confirms that:
    1. Myocum Road will serve as the primary southbound diversion route, including for heavy vehicles.
    2. Coolamon Scenic Drive will serve as the primary northbound diversion route for general traffic.

  3. Endorses extended construction hours for the duration of the works, from 7:00am to 6:00pm, Monday to Saturday, to support efficient project delivery.

  4. Confirms Saddle Road will remain open during the roadworks but will be made temporarily one-way (eastbound from Mullumbimby Road to Gulgan Road), as a detour for light vehicles for drivers who feel unable to take Coolamon Scenic Drive with the following measures to ensure road safety and usability:
    1. Installation of temporary speed reduction signage lowering the speed limit to 40 km/h for the duration of the detour.
    2. Traffic calming measures, as required, such as speed cushions or temporary chicanes, to slow vehicle speeds and protect local road users.
    3. Regular maintenance of the road surface, including the use of a water cart as needed to manage dust and surface conditions.
    4. Ongoing inspection and maintenance to ensure the road remains safe and accessible throughout the detour period.

  5. Endorses that, during Stage 2 works, heavy vehicles are to be directed exclusively via Myocum Road, and are not permitted to use Saddle Road or Coolamon Scenic Drive.

  6. Notes that the Stage 2 Traffic Guidance Scheme will not be implemented until current drainage works on Station Street and Fern Street, Mullumbimby, are completed to enable southbound one-way access to be reinstated.

  7. Requests that staff undertake urgent maintenance works on Coolamon Scenic Drive North, including:
    1. Pothole and pavement repairs.
    2. Installation of advisory signage, including but not limited to speed reduction to 60 km/h and relevant warning signage.
    3. Shoulder repairs, where appropriate.
    4. Consideration of improved signage for cyclists and pedestrians.

  8. Requests that staff consult with Mullumbimby High School to consider additional traffic control measures at the pedestrian crossing on Jubilee Avenue, to support safe traffic and pedestrian movement during the works.

  9. Directs staff to continue providing timely updates to NSW Police, Emergency Services, and Transport for NSW (including bus operators) regarding the status of the road works and associated Traffic Control Plans.

  10. Requests that staff review and update Council’s media and communications to ensure public messaging clearly reflects the intent of this resolution and keeps the community well-informed.

The motion was put to the vote and carried unanimously.

Procedural Motion:
Moved: Cr Ndiaye Seconded: Cr Dods
25-472 Resolved:
That Cr Ndiaye be granted a two minute extension to their speech.
The motion was put to the vote and carried unanimously.","isPublic":false,"isPublished":false,"isCurrentItem":false,"meeting":null,"reports":[{"id":1091,"name":"Mayoral Minute","isUploaded":0,"reportTemplateId":31,"wordTemplateId":2,"pdfMediaFullPath":"stream/BYRON/tmp_d16a826bea.pdf","token":"6052273c-05d0-4b58-9282-1addf1e97f27","isPublic":false}],"attachments":[],"actionSheets":[],"bookmarks":[{"id":193,"name":"8","eventId":172,"title":"Mullumbimby Road Stage 2 Works – Gulgan Road to Saddle Road","text":"Mullumbimby Road Stage 2 Works – Gulgan Road to Saddle Road","startTime":9001,"duration":null,"itemId":3392,"sortOrder":9,"minutesSortOrder":9,"parentId":-1,"additionalParentId":-1}],"minutes":[{"id":648,"motionedByName":null,"secondedByName":null,"motionAction":null,"voteForNames":null,"voteAgainstNames":null,"voteAbstainNames":null,"voteResult":null,"motionText":"I move that Council:

25-457 Resolved: 
That Council:

  1. Investigates the establishment of a local program to support the design of a solar panel recycling scheme for Byron Shire / Northern Rivers, with the aim of:
    1. Attracting investment and capacity-building opportunities;
    2. Facilitating collaboration with Southern Cross University, local industry, and the broader community;
    3. Supporting a circular economy approach to solar infrastructure;

  2. Endorses the Smart Energy Council’s Joint Statement on Mandatory Product Stewardship (attached), which calls for a national, regulated approach to PV panel recycling; and

  3. Supports, via a motion of endorsement, the NSW Minister for Energy’s advocacy for a nationally mandated scheme to prevent solar panels from ending up in landfill.

The motion was put to the vote and carried unanimously.

Moved: Cr Warth Seconded: Cr Hauge
25-484 Resolved: 
That Council:

  1. Endorses the Byron Youth Council as per the operational model presented in E2025/102128;

  2. Notes that staff have undertaken analysis of other contemporary youth engagement models to inform this report;

  3. Notes that subject to this report, further consultation with young people is still required in order to inform the scope, Terms of Reference, preferred name, branding and activities of the Byron Youth Council;

  4. Notes that subject to this report, staff will consider further resourcing and financial requirements to support program implementation in 2026/27;

  5. Notes that subject to this report, staff will undertake an expression of interest process, inviting eligible young people to nominate for the Byron Youth Council; and

  6. Requests that following 12 months of operation, staff prepares a further report, outlining the evaluation outcomes of the Byron Youth Council.

The motion was put to the vote and carried unanimously.

Moved: Cr Dods Seconded: Cr Lyon
Moved that Council:

  1. Adopts the Place Plan for New Brighton, South Golden Beach and Ocean Shores (Attachment 1, E2025/109206) as a place planning strategy document for Byron Shire, with the following action amendments and any consequential changes to the text or images to accommodate these:

    1. Action 12: change wording ‘Improving the path around the lake – extending as much as possible’ to “Constructing a complete walking circuit/path around the lake at Waterlily Park with connections to the surrounding road reserve access points”
    2. Action 23: change Action to ‘Undertake an urban design review of the Ocean Shores E1 zone area to enable the development of a Precinct Plan, with the aim of supporting the centre’s viability and enabling the evolution of a mixed-use town centre precinct.’
    3. Action 24: change Action to ‘Assess employment land needs in the West Ocean Shores area to support the establishment of a local mixed-use neighbourhood precinct.
    4. Retain Action from the Draft Exhibited Place Plan: ‘Investigate the viability, including assessment of environmental impacts, of a Marshalls Creek Boardwalk, connecting the Ocean Shores shopping area to the beach’, and that this investigation prioritise Item OS023 in the Byron Shire Pedestrian Access & Mobility Plan
       

  2. Thanks The Hon Penny Sharpe MLC, Minister for the Environment for her letter welcoming further investigation of the project, including investigations of various route options, and acknowledges that National Parks have been asked to continue to engage with Council on the assessment of options and the preferred routes for assessment.

  3. Thanks the stakeholder reference group and the wider community for their contributions in developing the Place Plan; and

  4. Notes that a Place Planning Collective North will be established through an Expression of Interest process for a one-year trial, and that applications for membership, and the final charter or terms of reference, will be reported to Council for confirmation.


The motion was put to the vote and declared lost.
Crs Lowe, Kay, Hauge, Ndiaye and Warth voted against the motion.

FORESHADOWED MOTION:
Moved: Cr Hauge Seconded: Cr Ndiaye
25-513 Resolved: 
That Council:

  1. Adopts the Place Plan for New Brighton, South Golden Beach and Ocean Shores (Attachment 1, E2025/109206) as a place planning strategy document for Byron Shire, with the following action amendments and any consequential changes to the text or images to accommodate these:
    1. Action 12: change wording ‘Improving the path around the lake – extending as much as possible’ to “Constructing a complete walking circuit/path around the lake at Waterlily Park with connections to the surrounding road reserve access points”
    2. Action 23: change Action to ‘Undertake an urban design review of the Ocean Shores E1 zone area to enable the development of a Precinct Plan, with the aim of supporting the centre’s viability and enabling the evolution of a mixed-use town centre precinct.’
    3. Action 24: change Action to ‘Assess employment land needs in the West Ocean Shores area to support the establishment of a local mixed-use neighbourhood precinct.
    4. Action 9: add to the "What" section wording "This could include: Prepare a Plan of Management for Bob Bellear Sports Field and the surrounding land (Lot 5/DP880917), considering both sports needs and natural values on the site.” and the title of the action "Considering the Natural Values of the Site".

  2. Removes the Marshalls Creek Boardwalk concept from consideration in the future development of the Active Transport Plan and other strategic council documents where this project may be considered.

  3. Thanks the Hon. Penny Sharpe MLC for her letter outlining the outstanding natural values of the Marshalls Creek area, and the legal framework the underpins Nature Reserves in NSW.

  4. Thanks the stakeholder reference group and the wider community for their contributions in developing the Place Plan; and

  5. Notes that a Place Planning Collective North will be established through an Expression of Interest process for a one-year trial, and that applications for membership, and the final charter or terms of reference, will be reported to Council for confirmation.

The foreshadowed motion was put to the vote and declared carried.
Crs Lyon, Dods, Swain and Pugh voted against the motion.

The meeting adjourned at 6.57pm for a break and reconvened at 7.35pm.

Procedural Motion: 
Moved: Cr Ndiaye
Moved to change the order of business to deal with Report 13.10 next on the Agenda.
