Moved: Cr Ndiaye Seconded: Cr Kay
25-487 Resolved: 
That Council:

 Adopts the Disability Inclusion Action Plan 2025–2029, as shown at Attachment (E2025/107173), with the following amendments:

  1. Applies consistent section numbering throughout the document.
    Note: The Executive Summary currently numbers themes/focus areas — this numbering should be continued and applied across the full document for ease of navigation;

  2. Relocates or summarises the Action Table (currently on pages 34–45):
    1. Brings the table forward to directly follow the Executive Summary, or
    2. Includes a summarised version of the actions early in the document
    3. Ensures each action in the table is clearly numbered, and that the associated Key Focus Area is identified for each
    4. Reviews the action list for duplication, and consider combining or aligning similar actions for clarity and efficiency;

  3. Updates the measure for Action LC8 to:
    1. Include both the completion of upgrades and
    2. Provisions for ongoing maintenance; and

  4. Adds a new action under the outcome area ‘Improved Accessible Transport Options’:
    1. Council to advocate for expanded transport services, including on-demand buses, improved timetables, and broader service coverage.

The motion was put to the vote and carried unanimously.

25-479 Resolved: 
That Council:

  1. Notes the vital pedestrian and cycle link provided by the Tallow Creek Footbridge to residents and visitors of Suffolk Park;

  2. Commits to reconstructing or replacing the Tallow Creek footbridge in Suffolk Park;

  3. Prioritises the expeditious delivery of a replacement bridge as a key project metric, ensuring design and procurement processes focus on the fastest practicable completion;

  4. Investigates the option of installing a temporary access structure to reinstate short-term access;

  5. Investigates the option of a prefabricated bridge structure to assist the expeditious reopening of the permanent bridge; and

  6. Investigates external funding opportunities, including State and Federal grants, to support and expedite delivery of the project.

The motion was put to the vote and carried unanimously.

Moved: Cr Hauge Seconded: Cr Dods
25-533 Resolved: 
That Council:

  1. Proceeds with the public exhibition of the Byron DCP 2014 amendments as summarised in this report and detailed in the attached draft DCP chapters listed below:
    1. DRAFT Byron Shire DCP 2014 Part A Preliminary (E2025/116283)
    2. DRAFT Byron Shire DCP 2014 Chapter B1 Biodiversity (E2025/116649) and subject Section B1.2.2 Clause 20 Domestic Animals being amended to read:

      Domestic Animals
      20.    Council may prohibit the keeping of domestic animals where there is an unacceptable residual risk (i.e. a risk that cannot be adequately mitigated by other measures such as exclusion fencing) arising from the development to threatened or other significant species. In such cases Council will require:
      a)      A restrictive covenant under Part 6 (Division 4) of the Conveyancing Act 1919 to ensure that the domestic animal(s) in question (e.g. dogs and cats) are not kept or brought onto the allotment; and
      b)      Multiple Occupancy and Community title development to incorporate restrictive provisions into plans of management and Neighbourhood Management Statements that prohibits the keeping of the domestic animals in question (e.g. dogs and cats)
      c)      Conditions of consent to prohibit domestic animals entering the site during construction
      d)     Subsequent development applications for development on land where such restrictions already apply either on the property title or within approved Plans of Management or Neighbourhood Management statements must include conditions of consent prohibiting domestic animals as per the restriction on title or the provisions within the approved Plans of Management.

    3. DRAFT Byron Shire DCP 2014 Chapter B5 Providing for Cycling (E2025/112286)
    4. DRAFT Byron Shire DCP 2014 Chapter B9 Landscaping (E2025/116664)
    5. DRAFT Byron Shire DCP 2014 Chapter B13 Access and Mobility (E2025/116692)
    6. DRAFT Byron Shire DCP 2014 Chapter C1 Non-indigenous Heritage (E2025/109075)
    7. DRAFT Byron Shire DCP 2014 Chapter D1 Residential Accommodation in Urban Village and Special Purpose Zones (E2025/107554)
    8. DRAFT Byron Shire DCP 2014 Chapter D5 Industrial Development (E2025/108888)
    9. DRAFT Byron Shire DCP 2014 Chapter D6 Subdivision (E2025/116079)
    10. DRAFT Byron Shire DCP 2014 Chapter E1 Suffolk Park (E2025/116700)
    11. DRAFT Byron Shire DCP 2014 Chapter E8 West Byron Urban Release Area (E2025/116703)
    12. DRAFT Byron Shire DCP 2014 Chapter F1 Tree and Vegetation Management (E2025/107573)
    13. Amend Section B3.2.1 Provision of Services, Prescriptive measure 2(b) of Byron Shire DCP 2014 to read:

      2. Electricity Supply
      b) Alternative electricity sources for development other than urban, commercial, industrial and residential subdivision, may be considered where the applicant can demonstrate that the development can be adequately supplied with alternate forms of renewable energy such as solar and battery. Details are to be provided with the development application on the type and size of system proposed in terms of battery size and kilowatts generated and the like. Such information to be provided by a suitably qualified specialist such as an electrical engineer or renewable energy provider, demonstrating the development can operate without the need to rely upon backup fuel generators. Conditions to apply in relation to relevant restrictions on title advising that no grid connected power is available to the development if approved.

  2. Receives a further report following the public exhibition period for consideration of submissions received.

  3. Notes that should there be no submissions received on a particular DCP chapter, adopt the exhibited amendments to that chapter at the close of the statutory public exhibition period and notify these accordingly.

  4. Notes the draft DCP provisions, contained in this report, propose to establish an All-Electric (No Gas) requirement for new buildings in the Shire.

  5. Requests staff to proceed with direct industry and stakeholder engagement about the draft All-Electric (No Gas) provisions in the DCP to determine the feasibility of these being applied; and

  6. Receives a further report for consideration on the engagement in point 5 and submissions received including staff advice on options, implications, and amendments to the draft provisions needed following industry and stakeholder engagement.
The motion was put to the vote and carried unanimously.
Crs Lyon, Lowe, Kay, Hauge, Dods, Warth, Swain, and Pugh voted in favour of the motion.
Nil voted against the motion.

Moved: Cr Pugh Seconded: Cr Dods
25-491 Resolved: 
That Council:

  1. Notes that:
    1. The Bangalow Bowlo has been a vital sporting and cultural hub in Bangalow since it was established in 1910.
    2. The Bangalow Bowlo's role in the community, considering it as a sporting and cultural hub where people gather informally, gives it both cultural and social significance.
    3. The Bangalow Bowlo is the major sponsor of all local Bangalow sporting teams.
    4. The Bangalow Bowlo has hosted many notable and emerging Australian bands, including INXS, and more recently Hockey Dad.
    5. Norths Collective (North Sydney Leagues Club) ceased trading at the Bangalow Bowlo on Friday, 24 October and is now exploring options to sell the asset.

  2. Requests a report on:
    1. The current land use zoning and what planning instruments allow on the site.
    2. Heritage listing options to ensure the Bangalow Bowlo continues as a sporting and cultural hub for the community.

  3. Recognises the strong community concern and anger over Norths Collective's decision to close the Bangalow Bowlo and affirms its commitment to maintaining the Bangalow Bowlo as a community hub for sport and culture.
The motion was put to the vote and carried unanimously.

Moved: Cr Pugh Seconded: Cr Ndiaye
25-548 Resolved: 
That Council:
  1. Respectfully revokes existing delegations and dissolves four Section 355 Committees, effective at 4pm on 30 January 2026, namely:
    1. Bangalow A&I Hall Section 355 Management Committee
    2. Brunswick Heads Memorial Hall Section 355 Management Committee
    3. Marvell Hall Section 355 Management Committee
    4. Mullumbimby Civic Memorial Hall Section 355 Management Committee;

  2. Notifies the Section 355 Committee members of the end of their membership in the Committee, and expresses Council's gratitude for years of service to Council and the community, with encouragement to continue volunteer involvement in the Friends of the Hall program where desired; and

  3. Ensures assets and funds currently managed by the Committee are returned to Council’s direct control prior to dissolution.

The motion was put to the vote and carried unanimously.
Cr Hauge was not present for the vote.

","reportContent":null,"minutesDiscussion":"Procedural Motion:
Moved: Cr Ndiaye Seconded: Cr Dods
25-536 Resolved That Cr Ndiaye be granted a two minute extension to her speech.
The motion was put to the vote and carried unanimously.

Moved: Cr Ndiaye Seconded: Cr Hauge
25-574 Resolved: 

That Council:

  1. Thanks the Mullumbimby Hospital Site Action Group, Project Working Group and other community members involved in securing the site and developing the community’s vision for the site;

  2. Notes that funding was received from the Commonwealth Government’s Housing Support Program – Stream 1 to explore options for facilitating development of the Former Mullumbimby Hospital Site for future housing, and that this work is now complete to enable grant acquittal;

  3. Notes the recommendations outlined in the Development Options Report (Confidential Attachment 2, E2025/128046) and Development Strategy (Delivery Program) (Confidential Attachment 1, E2025/12009), including that the preferred Development Model recommended in the Development Options Report is an englobo sale. This approach is presented as the best balance of development quality, community benefit, and financial return, while minimising risk and complexity for Council;

  4. Supports in principle the englobo sale of the site to the NSW Government for the delivery of public, social, affordable and Aboriginal housing, and as a priority, invites the Minister for Housing, The Hon Rose Jackson, and representatives from the relevant State Housing Agencies, such as Homes NSW and the Reconstruction Authority, to a round table discussion with Council, noting the recommended Development Model, the Built Form and Housing outcomes identified in the current Site-Specific Development Control Plan (as referred to in Parts 6 & 7), and the recommendations of the Mullumbimby Hospital Site Project Reference Group endorsed by Council on 22 November 2018 (Agenda item 13.9, File no. I2018/2012);

  5. Reports the outcomes of Part 4 to Council for endorsement to the April 2026 Council Ordinary meeting;

  6. Endorses the public exhibition of the Site-Specific Development Control Plan (DCP) (Attachment 3, E2025/25114 & Attachment 4, E2025/250917) in early 2026;

  7. Notes that, once finalised and approved by Council, the DCP will inform a Site-Specific Reference Scheme. This Scheme will confirm the development and built form parameters expected by Council and will be used to guide the Expression of Interest (EOI) process to gauge market interest in the site;

  8. Notes that further technical work may be required by staff in response to the final Site Reference Scheme. This may include updated specialist reports, infrastructure assessments, and a valuation of the site to support an Expression of Interest (EOI) process; and

  9. As a priority, engages with key community stakeholders on the Development Options, Development Model, and Site-Specific Development Control Plan, including inviting the previous Project Reference Group to an update and discussion on the project.

The motion was put to the vote and carried unanimously.

Notes the recommendations outlined in the Development Options Report (Confidential Attachment 2, E2025/128046) and Development Strategy (Delivery Program) (Confidential Attachment 1, E2025/12009), including that the preferred Development Model recommended in the Development Options Report is an englobo sale. This approach is presented as the best balance of development quality, community benefit, and financial return, while minimising risk and complexity for Council;

  4. Supports in principle the englobo sale of the site to the NSW Government for the delivery of public, social, affordable and Aboriginal housing, and as a priority, invites the Minister for Housing, The Hon Rose Jackson, and representatives from the relevant State Housing Agencies, such as Homes NSW and the Reconstruction Authority, to a round table discussion with Council, noting the recommended Development Model, the Built Form and Housing outcomes identified in the current Site-Specific Development Control Plan (as referred to in Parts 6 & 7), and the recommendations of the Mullumbimby Hospital Site Project Reference Group endorsed by Council on 22 November 2018 (Agenda item 13.9, File no. I2018/2012);

  5. Reports the outcomes of Part 4 to Council for endorsement to the April 2026 Council Ordinary meeting;

  6. Endorses the public exhibition of the Site-Specific Development Control Plan (DCP) (Attachment 3, E2025/25114 & Attachment 4, E2025/250917) in early 2026;

  7. Notes that, once finalised and approved by Council, the DCP will inform a Site-Specific Reference Scheme. This Scheme will confirm the development and built form parameters expected by Council and will be used to guide the Expression of Interest (EOI) process to gauge market interest in the site;

  8. Notes that further technical work may be required by staff in response to the final Site Reference Scheme. This may include updated specialist reports, infrastructure assessments, and a valuation of the site to support an Expression of Interest (EOI) process; and

  9. As a priority, engages with key community stakeholders on the Development Options, Development Model, and Site-Specific Development Control Plan, including inviting the previous Project Reference Group to an update and discussion on the project.

The motion was put to the vote and carried unanimously.

The motion was put to the vote and carried unanimously.

25-589 Resolved That Cr Dods be granted a two minute extension to his speech. 
The motion was put to the vote and carried unanimously.


Moved: Cr Warth Seconded: Cr Dods
Moved: 
That Council:
  1. Pauses all work on progressing the proposed Byron Bay Special Entertainment Precinct (SEP) Planning Proposal, Draft DCP Amendment, and Precinct Management Plan, to allow Councillors and the community to collaboratively develop a clear vision for the Byron Bay Town Centre with respect to entertainment, cultural activation, events, and night-time trading.

  2. Prior to any submission of the SEP Planning Proposal for Gateway Determination or public exhibition, requests staff to identify funding sources for the programs and initiatives required to support a trial SEP, including but not limited to:
    1. A Town Centre Activation Plan;
    2. An Events and Activations Program and Calendar;
    3. Safety initiatives, including Purple Flag accreditation, implementation of CPTED safety audit recommendations, wayfinding signage, and a comprehensive lighting audit;
    4. Transport initiatives, including late-night local bus service extensions, a community Night Rider bus, coordinated private transport services, and options for on-demand public transport;
    5. State Government agency resourcing, including formal Memoranda of Understanding with Liquor & Gaming NSW and NSW Police to ensure adequate venue compliance monitoring and precinct safety during the trial period.
  1. Requests staff prepare a project plan outlining delivery pathways, funding estimates, and potential partnership opportunities for the programs and initiatives listed in Point 2.

  2. Continues discussions with the Hon. John Graham, Minister for Transport, Minister for the Arts and Minister for Music and the Night-Time Economy, regarding the securing of funding and implementation of the initiatives identified in Point 2, and provides the Minister’s office with a consolidated list of community-identified needs prior to commencement of any SEP trial.

  3. Receives a report detailing how the NSW Cultural SEPP can be utilised to activate the Railway Corridor, facilitate temporary street closures, and enable cultural activation, small-scale festivals, and creative industry events within public spaces across the Byron Bay Town Centre.

The motion was put to the vote and declared lost.
Crs Lyon, Kay, Hauge and Warth voted in favour of the motion.
Crs Lowe, Ndiaye, Dods, Swain and Pugh voted against the motion.


Foreshadowed Motion:
Moved: Cr Ndiaye Seconded: Cr Pugh
25-577 Resolved: 
That Council:
  1. In support of a Special Entertainment Precinct in Byron Bay Town Centre Council has:
    1. Undertaken early community consultation and stakeholder engagement (Attachment 1, E2025/120724); and
    2. Prepared the Planning Proposal (Attachment 2, E2025/126586), Development Control Plan (DCP) amendment (Attachment 3, E2025/126046), and Precinct Management Plan (PMP) (Attachment 4, E2025/126/564).

  2. Notes that feedback received from the community and stakeholders referred to in 1(a) has informed the trading hours and sound management controls in the Precinct Management Plan.

  3. Requests staff to submit the Planning Proposal to the Department of Planning, Housing and Infrastructure (DPHI) for Gateway Determination with an amendment to remove Area South from the Special Entertainment Precinct Area Map (and from the DCP amendment and Precinct Management Plan).  If Gateway approval is obtained, staff will place the Planning Proposal, DCP amendment, and Precinct Management Plan on public exhibition in accordance with the Gateway requirements.

  4. Notes that staff will review feedback received during the public exhibition from the local community, residents, and businesses, and update the Planning Proposal, DCP amendment, and Precinct Management Plan as required.

  5. Notes that staff will prepare a report on point 4 for Council consideration and decision to approve the finalised Planning Proposal, DCP amendment, and Precinct Management Plan to proceed to a trial Special Entertainment Precinct.

  6. Subject to point 3, requests staff to establish a Precinct Working Group comprising internal and external stakeholders to support the establishment, operation, and monitoring of the trial Special Entertainment Precinct, taking into consideration the Template Terms of Reference for a Special Entertainment Precinct Working Group and Resolution 25-313(2).

  7. Investigates Purple Flag accreditation for the same boundary as the proposed Special Entertainment Precinct.

  8. Acknowledges the need to prepare a Town Centre Activation Plan, alongside the trial Special Entertainment Precinct, to guide and deliver entertainment and activation events in the Town Centre. It also notes that existing Council policies may need to be reviewed and updated to align with the Plan and streamline event approvals.

  9. Acknowledges the need to identify a funding source for the following programs and plans required to support a trial Special Entertainment Precinct:
    1. Town Centre Activation Plan;
    2. Events and Activations program and calendar;
    3. Safety initiatives including Purple Flag Accreditation, CPTED safety audit recommendations and wayfinding signage;
    4. Transport initiatives including a night time local bus service extension, night rider community bus, coordinated private transport service, and on-demand bus service;
    5. State Government agency resourcing and presence in the precinct to monitor venue compliance and improve safety. In particular MOUs are needed with Liquor and Gaming NSW and NSW Police. 

  10. Requests staff to put together a project plan, funding estimate and potential partners for the delivery of the programs and plans in point 9.

  11. Requests a meeting with the Hon. John Graham, Minister for Transport, Minister for the Arts, and Minister for Music and the Night-time Economy, to discuss the delivery of programs and plans outlined in points 8 and 9 needed to support a trial Special Entertainment Precinct in the Byron Bay Town Centre. This meeting to occur at the earliest available time early 2026.

The foreshadowed motion was put to the vote and declared carried.
Crs Lowe, Ndiaye, Dods, Swain and Pugh voted in favour of the foreshadowed motion.
Crs Lyon, Kay, Hauge and Warth voted against the foreshadowed motion.


The meeting adjourned at 7.11pm for a break and reconvened at 8.00pm.

Moved: Cr Ndiaye Seconded: Cr Swain
25-537 Resolved: 
That Council:
  1. Acknowledges the extensive process undertaken to reach this stage and thanks the community, industry and staff for their patience and engagement throughout the Strategy's consultation and development;

  2. Adopts the Byron Shire Economic Strategy 2025–2035 (Attachment 1, E2025/121606), which provides a clear framework for how Council will work alongside local businesses and industry groups, noting that delivery of the Strategy will occur through a series of economic focus area Action Plans.

  3. Notes that the following (draft) economic focus area Action Plans have been prepared by staff and are included as Part B of the Strategy:
    1. Business and Industry Action Plan (Attachment 2, E2025/121679);
    2. Destination Management and Visitor Economy Action Plan (Attachment 3, E2025/121717); and
    3. Events Action Plan (Attachment 4, E2025/121738). 
  1. Notes the next steps outlined in the report to deliver the Strategy:
    1. Council will establish an Economic Activation Group as a priority action, following an invitation and expression of interest process, to be reported to Council for confirmation in early 2026.
    2. Once established, sub-working groups for each economic focus area will be set up with defined responsibilities to:
      1. Review the Action Plans;
      2. Recommend amendments; and
      3. Report to Council by mid-2026 with any proposed changes for final adoption.
    3. Staff will initiate discussions with relevant universities and other research organisations via an academic collaboration framework to support delivery of the Economic Strategy.
    4. Staff will progress new Action Plans, including a Night-time Economy Action Plan.

The motion was put to the vote and carried unanimously.

25-542 Resolved: 
We move that Council:
  1. Notes the significant social, educational and cultural value of public libraries to the Byron Shire community;

  2. Acknowledges the role of the Richmond Tweed Regional Library (RTRL) in delivering high-quality, accessible library services across the region;

  3. Reconfirms its commitment to continuing as a member Council of the RTRL service under a revised Deed of Agreement (post June 2027) which strengthens governance, accountability and funding model transparency;

  4. Authorises the RTRL Committee and Leadership Team to negotiate amendments to the Deed to include appendices covering risk management, service charters, cyber security and planning protocols; and

  5. Notes that, as per the functions outlined in s335 of the Local Government Act, the General Manager will negotiate the employment arrangements of Byron Shire library staff (including consideration of whether staff should remain employed by the Executive Council or be transferred to their respective member Councils) following assessment of the relevant implications.

The motion was put to the vote and carried unanimously.

Questions

Question No. 1  Special Entertainment Precinct Inclusion

Ralph Mamone asked the following question:
Can the Council and community owned Byron Bay War Memorial Swimming Pool and Fish Heads Restaurant site as a whole, be included in this precinct and what was the criteria to determine the boundaries in the first place?

The Mayor took the question on notice.

Question 2  STRA Regular Update

David Wallace (as read by staff) asked the following question:
During the term of the previous Council, a motion was unanimously passed that a report on short term rental accommodation (STRA) be presented at a Council Meeting every 3 months. The last STRA report was presented at the 22 February 2025 Ordinary Meeting. This was part of a report on compliance and enforcement in Byron Shire. At which future Council meeting can Councillors and interested residents expect to receive this overdue STRA report?

The Director Sustainable Environment and Economy replied:
The resolution that was corresponding to that Report allowed Council to do an annual Report on STRA and that will come to Council in February 2026 as part of the Compliance Priorities Report.

Question 3  Development Approval

Jan Barham (as read by staff) asked the following question:
Can an explanation be provided as to why council approved development application 10.2023.488.2 for 115 Jonson Street, Byron Bay that removed conditions of consent from the primary consent that defined the number of patrons, hours of operation and restriction on the use of the outdoor courtyard. What policy or planning guidelines support the approval and is it usual practice to remove essential conditions that define compliance issues? Was the DA reported to Planning Review Committee and if so, when?

The Director Sustainable Environment and Economy took the question on notice.

Question 4  Mullumbimby Road Upgrade Detour

Sharon McGrath (as read by staff) asked the following question:
Regarding the Mullumbimby Road Upgrade, Councillors and staff have failed to address the question I asked on 25 September adequately. I have received two identical responses from separate Council staff, neither of which addresses the crux of the question. As such, I ask that Councillors respond to the question. Specifically, were they advised of the four-month one-way detour when they approved the Mullumbimby Road Upgrade works?

The Mayor took the question on notice.
 
Question 5  Public Access Documentation

Sharon McGrath (as read by staff) asked the following question:
When will staff release documents relating to the Mullumbimby Road Upgrade, as requested in September?
The documents which have not been released include, but are not limited to:
  • Project budgets
  • Construction Program and Construction Environmental Management Plan (CEMP)
  • Summary of nightworks planned
  • Cost estimates for the feasibility of nightworks
  • Risk Assessment referred to as an attachment to the TMP, but not included
  • Economic Impact Assessment
If these documents are not released, would Council explain why the public should not be informed of the details of such an impactful works program?

The Mayor replied:
Hopefully the road will be completed before we even have to publish them.

Question No. 1 Byron Bay Community Discussion
Brooke Crowle, on behalf of the People of Byron, registered the following question:
"In response to the Mayor attending a community discussion about Byron Bay's future. Given that Mullumbimby and Bangalow's Masterplans are flagged to be audited at their 5-year anniversary - can the Byron Bay community request an audit of the now 10-year-old Byron Bay Masterplan? Does the group work towards a PAMP plan, is there a Facilities Asset Management Plan, what has happened to the Culture Strategy or minimizing bulky developments like the Sub-Strategy 02: A Varied and Defined Centre or Sub-Strategy 03; a Fine Grain Village to reflect Byron's character? Before the SEP Trial diverts more time and money away from the existing plans and realities - can the Mayor's "community discussion" broaden to review this plan and include the Byron Bay community in a future meeting?"

Question No. 2 SEP Trading
Jan Barham registered the following question:
"What legal mechanism/s constrain venues from accessing extended trading hours as stated in the BSC report 27 November, page 533 that "Existing development consent conditions mean the above businesses would not be entitled to additional trading hours due to their inclusion in the proposed Special Entertainment Precinct” as the consents exceed the Precinct Plan trading hours and why Cheeky Monkeys / Merivale was excluded from the list and how many venues will be affected by November Vibrancy laws amendments that change the criteria for 'dedicated live music venues' and if this will allow extended trading hours as defined in the Precinct Plan p8'. 'Extended trading hours are possible for venues deemed dedicated live
music venues'?"

The Mayor took the question on notice.

Question No. 3 Coastal Erosion Zone Development

","reportContent":null,"minutesDiscussion":"Moved: Cr Ndiaye Seconded: Cr Dods
25-620 Resolved
  1. That pursuant to Section 10A(2)(a) of the Local Government Act 1993, Council resolves to move into Confidential Session to discuss the report "Confidential - Annual Review of General Manager's Performance Agreement".

  2. That the reason for closing the meeting to the public to consider this item be that the report contains:
    (a) personnel matters concerning particular individuals (other than councillors)

  3. That on the balance it is considered that receipt and discussion of the matter in open Council would be contrary to the public interest, as it provides information regarding the General Manager's Performance.
The motion was put to the vote and carried unanimously.

Moved: Cr Pugh Seconded: Cr Ndiaye
25-622 Resolved that Council move into Committee to allow for free debate.
The motion was put to the vote and carried unanimously.

Moved: Cr Ndiaye Seconded: Cr Dods
25-623 Resolved that Council move out of Committee and resume the Ordinary Meeting.
The motion was put to the vote and carried unanimously.

Moved: Cr Pugh Seconded: Cr Ndiaye
25-602 Resolved: 
That Council:
  1. That Council notes the findings and endorses recommendations from the performance review panel with respect to the annual performance review for the General Manager contained in Confidential Attachment 1 (E2025/133609).

  2. That Council endorses the 2025/2026 draft Performance Agreement for the General Manager to finalise with the Mayor on behalf of the Councilors, contained at Confidential Attachment 2 (E2025/132660).

The motion was put to the vote and carried unanimously.

Moved: Cr Ndiaye Seconded: None
25-624 Resolved that the meeting move out of Confidential Session.
The motion was put to the vote and carried unanimously.

Moved: Cr Hauge Seconded: Cr Ndiaye
25-540 Resolved: 
That Council:
  1. Notes that the current Advisory Committee process, requiring committees to decide at one meeting whether an item can be substantively discussed at a subsequent meeting, creates delays of two to five months between when an issue is raised by a committee member and when it can be meaningfully addressed.

  2. Amends the Terms of Reference template (for all advisory committees):
    1. To replace the requirement for committee members to request items 14 days prior to the meeting with a standing “Future Agenda Planning” item at the end of each meeting, this would:
      1. allow members to propose topics for future consideration
      2. support the committee to collectively decide whether a report should be prepared for the next meeting. 
    2. To include a "business arising" item at the end of each meeting to allow Committee members to provide updates on activities relevant to the Advisory Committee's purpose.

The motion was put to the vote and carried unanimously.

Moved: Cr Lowe Seconded: Cr Pugh
25-541 Resolved: 
That Council:
  1. Writes to the Premier of NSW, Chris Minns, requesting an amendment to Clause 209 of the Gaming Machines Act 2001 on the grounds that it undermines local democracy and prioritises gaming industry interests over community wellbeing.

  2. Writes to the Member for Ballina, Ms Tamara Smith MP, and Minister David Harris, requesting that they advocate for the review and amendment of Clause 209 of the Gaming Machines Act 2001 on the grounds that it undermines local democracy and prioritises gaming industry interests over community wellbeing.

  3. Requests Ms Smith MP to raise this matter in the NSW Parliament and with the relevant Minister, advocating for legislative reform that restores the ability of councils and communities to have meaningful input into decisions regarding gaming machine applications.

  4. Receives a report back on responses from Ms Smith MP, Minister David Harris and/or the Premier and any actions taken within six months of this resolution.

  5. Requests staff prepare a proposed motion for LGNSW Annual Conference 2026.

The motion was put to the vote and carried unanimously.

Moved: Cr Ndiaye Seconded: Cr Warth
25-613 Resolved that Cr Lowe be granted a two minute extension to their speech.
The motion was put to the vote and carried unanimously.

Moved: Cr Swain Seconded: Cr Dods
25-549 Resolved: 
That Council:
  1. Notes that Kolora Way / New Brighton Rd bridge is a vital pedestrian and cycle link between North Ocean Shores and New Brighton;

  2. Notes that currently there is no safe way for pedestrians and cyclists to cross this bridge due the lack of shoulder or verge for approximately 50 metres east of the bridge;

  3. Notes that the community has been requesting a safe pedestrian and cycle link across this bridge for a decade or longer;

  4. Notes that a pedestrian and cycle link across this bridge is a Priority A project (OS003) in Council’s adopted PAMP and Bike Plan;

  5. Notes that improving pedestrian and cyclist safety across this bridge is a key action in Council’s adopted place plan for New Brighton, South Golden Beach and Ocean Shores;

  6. Notes that this bridge will become a key connection between the Northern Rivers Rail Trail and New Brighton via the existing Old New Brighton Rd shared path;

  7. Prioritises the planning, design and construction of a shared path on the north side of the road which extends from Redgate Rd to Kolora Way, and complies with current design regulations;

  8. Ensures the design includes consideration of crossing points across Redgate Rd to the existing shared path, and across Kolora Way to the Old New Brighton Rd shared path;

  9. Investigates an interim solution that creates a narrow pathway on the north side of the road (within the road reserve and outside mapped wetlands) by moving the traffic lanes southward on the eastern side of the bridge; and

  10. Investigates external funding opportunities, including State and Federal grants, to support and expedite delivery of the project.

The motion was put to the vote and carried unanimously.

Moved: Cr Ndiaye Seconded: Cr Lowe
25-614 Resolved that Cr Swain be granted a two minute extension to their speech.
The motion was put to the vote and carried unanimously.

","reportContent":null,"minutesDiscussion":"Moved: Cr Ndiaye Seconded: Cr Hauge
25-605 Resolved that the item "Urgency on Resilient Homes Program Deadlines" be discussed as a matter of urgency, the urgency being that the next Council Meeting won't be held until after the deadlines.
The motion was put to the vote and carried unanimously.

The Mayor ruled the matter "Urgency on Resilient Homes Program Deadlines" of great urgency.

Moved: Cr Hauge Seconded: Cr Lowe
25-604 Resolved: 
That Council:
  1. Notes with concern the recently-announced Resilient Homes Program deadlines:
    1. Buyback applications by 31 Dec 2025, and relocations by end of 2026
    2. Raises and retrofits (resilient measures) applications by 31 March 2026, and works completed by 31 March 2027

  2. Notes that the updated prioritisation mapping for the Northern Rivers Resilient Homes Program was made available in July 2025, leaving less than one year between a change in eligibility criteria and the closure of program applications

  3. Notes that at 31 October 2025, only 16.5% of raises and retrofits in the Byron shire had been finalised, and that the Reconstruction Authority had months of “targeted outreach” planned to reach homeowners in the Byron Shire yet to even apply to the program.

  4. Notes that delays including development assessment, weather, and builder availability are beyond the control of flood-affected community members accessing the program.

  5. Urgently writes to the Reconstruction Authority, MP Janelle Saffin (NSW Minister for Recovery), Tamara Smith (State Member for Ballina), Premier Chris Minns, Justine Elliot (Federal Member for Richmond) and Prime Minister Anthony Albanese to request:
    1. Application period extension to December 2026 given the ongoing community outreach and new prioritisation measures
    2. Works completion extension to at least 24 months after determination of applications received by December 2028
    3. Public monthly reporting of statistics on RHP applications (i.e. submitted, determined, works completed, finalised) by local government area
    4. Information on what program will be replacing the Resilient Homes Program to support the community to move from a state of “recovery and reconstruction” to “planning and preparedness”.
The motion was put to the vote and carried unanimously.

Moved: Cr Ndiaye Seconded: Cr Lowe
25-601 Resolved that Cr Hauge be granted a two minute extension to their speech.
The motion was put to the vote and carried unanimously.

25-610 Resolved That the item "Old Bangalow Road" be discussed as a matter of urgency, the urgency being that to enable staff to act on this matter as soon as possible.
The motion was put to the vote and carried unanimously.

The Mayor ruled the matter "Old Bangalow Road" of great urgency.

Moved: Cr Lowe Seconded: Cr Kay
25-611 Resolved: 
That Council:
  1. Acknowledges the community concerns about unsafe and speeding traffic on Old Bangalow Road

  2. Acknowledges the work already undertaken by the Local Transport Forum and staff

  3. Requests staff hold an on site meeting with community representatives to discuss their concerns

  4. Requests that staff conduct a safety audit to identify any additional possible solutions to community concerns

  5. Receives a report on the safety audit to the February meeting, including possible budget requests to implement solutions.
The motion was put to the vote and carried unanimously.



There being no further business, the meeting concluded at 03:09 PM.



I hereby certify that these are the true and correct Minutes of this Meeting
as confirmed at Council’s Ordinary Meeting on 19 February 2026.

Mayor Sarah Ndiaye

Moved: Cr Ndiaye Seconded: Cr Hauge
25-675 Resolved: 
That Council requests the National General Assembly of Local Government calls on the Australian Government to implement a mandatory, nationally consistent solar PV product stewardship scheme that covers design, installations, safe reuse, and circular end-of-life management without cost-shifting to local government to:
  1. Build on the national solar panel recycling pilot announced on 16 January 2026 by scaling it into a permanent, nationally consistent program;

  2. Recognise local government as a key delivery partner and provide funding and policy support to enable councils to participate in collection, education and regional circular economy solutions;

  3. Develop national standards for the safe handling, transport, storage, reuse and recycling of end-of-life solar panels; and

  4. Ensure responsibility for solar panel waste is shared across the supply chain and does not result in unfunded liabilities for local government.

The motion was put to the vote and declared carried.
 Crs Lyon, Lowe, Kay, Hauge, Ndiaye, Warth, Swain and Pugh voted in favour of the motion. 
 No Crs voted against the motion.

Moved: Cr Ndiaye Seconded: Cr Kay
25-672 Resolved: 
That Council:
  1. Acknowledges the work of the Public and Environmental Services Team; and

  2. Maintains a detailed risk-based compliance approach via a Council resolved priority program and adopts the ‘Compliance Priorities Program’ for 2026 as provided below:
1.   Very High Priorities
1.1  Developments, actions, works, activities or uses that places people’s lives at immediate risk or that cause or are likely to cause a significant risk of environmental harm or pollution.
1.2  Significant environmental and public health incidents.
1.3  Dangerous and/or menacing dogs.
1.4  Livestock on public roads.
1.5  Traffic, parking and unapproved camping activity including camping enforcement, with an emphasis on environmentally sensitive areas.
1.6  Asbestos containing material being illegally dumped on public land.

2.       High Priorities
2.1  Unauthorised events, wedding receptions, parties, 'doof and rave' parties where significant environmental harm or risk to people’s lives.
2.2  Tourist and visitor accommodation swimming pool safety, including legislative requirements.
2.3  Breaches of the NSW Fair Trading’s ‘Code of Conduct for the Short-Term Rental Accommodation Industry’ where the breach falls within the jurisdiction of Council’s enforcement powers.
2.4  Responses to complaints about recurring noise disturbance, public nuisance from premises, maintenance of alcohol-free zones.
2.5  Uncontrolled dogs and/or cats including those kept on land where development consent prohibits it.
2.6  Responses to serious breaches of the Food Act.

3. Medium Priorities
3.1     Development or activities without consent, or non-compliance with consent, permit or licence conditions where these appear to pose no immediate threat to life, property, public health or the environment.
3.2     Non-compliant signage on public land.

4. Routine Priorities
4.1  Companion animals with a high emphasis on high visibility enforcement and public education.
4.2  Seasonal public health issues and community preparedness.
4.3  Onsite sewage management systems (including OSMS programme inspections).
4.4  Routine Food Safety Inspections.
4.5  Awareness of current public health requirements.
4.6  All other matters.

The motion was put to the vote and declared carried.
 Crs Lyon, Lowe, Kay, Hauge, Ndiaye, Warth, Swain and Pugh voted in favour of the motion. 
 No Crs voted against the motion.

Moved: Cr Hauge Seconded: Cr Lyon
25-647 Resolved: 
That Council:

  1. Thanks the Byron Bay Surf Life Saving Club for their service to our community;

  2. Notes the request to amend the Byron Foreshore Concept Plans to show potential Surf Club expansion into Apex Park;

  3. Confirms Council's commitment to the location and footprint of the Apex Park amenities as per the Concept Plans, and ensures detailed architectural designs of the amenities considers the interface and integration with the Surf Club;

  4. Confirms Council's commitment to the location of the Apex Park playground, with a reduced footprint to enable a 10m buffer zone adjacent to the Surf Club for potential future expansion and path relocation, and provides a letter of support for the Surf Club‘s discussions with Crown Lands regarding the potential future expansion into this buffer zone; and

  5. Allocates $5,000 from the Community Buildings Reserve to undertake a detailed structural assessment of the Surf Club to inform future strategic planning for both Council and the Surf Club.

The motion was put to the vote and declared carried.
 Crs Lyon, Lowe, Kay, Hauge, Ndiaye, Warth, Swain and Pugh voted in favour of the motion. 
 Crs Ndiaye voted against the motion.

Moved: Cr Lowe Seconded: Cr Lyon
25-649 Resolved: 
That Council:
  1. Notes the requirement to manage Reserve R1041692 as Community Land under section 3.22(1)(a) of the Crown Land Management Act 2016 (CLM Act);

  2. Assigns to R1041692 the category of General Community Use under sections 3.23 CLM Act and 36(4) of the Local Government Act 1993 (LG Act);

  3. Authorises the draft Plan of Management for Sandhills Wetlands Reserve R1041692 #E2026/9478 (PoM) to be updated to align with Council's Resolution on the separate report to this meeting titled "Proposed Wildlife Protection Area - Sandhills Wetlands";

  4. Endorses the updated draft PoM for the purposes of engagement with Crown Lands and public exhibition;

  5. Notifies Crown Lands of the draft PoM under s39 of the LG Act and seek Minister's consent to adopt the draft PoM under clause 70B of the Crown Land Management Regulations 2018;

  6. Places the draft PoM, with any changes required by Crown Lands as owner of the land, on public exhibition under section 38 of the LG Act; and

  7. Notes that after public exhibition the draft PoM will be reported back with details of the submissions received, for Council's further consideration.    

The motion was put to the vote and declared carried.
 Crs Lyon, Lowe, Kay, Hauge, Ndiaye, Warth, Swain and Pugh voted in favour of the motion. 
 No Crs voted against the motion.

Moved: Cr Ndiaye Seconded: Cr Kay
25-673 Resolved: 
That, pursuant to Section 4.16 of the Environmental Planning & Assessment Act 1979, Development Application No. 10.2025.265.1 for alterations and additions to existing hotel and bottle shop, be refused for the following reasons: 

  1. A Biodiversity Development Assessment Report has not been provided in accordance with Section 7.7 of the Biodiversity Conservation Act 2016 and insufficient information has been provided demonstrating that the development does not exceed the Biodiversity Offsets Scheme threshold;

  2. Pursuant to Section 4.15(1)(a)(i) of the Environmental Planning and Assessment Act 1979, the proposed development is inconsistent with Chapter 2 Coastal Management, Section 2.8 of the State Environmental Planning Policy (Resilience and Hazards) 2021. In particular, insufficient information has been provided to demonstrate that the proposed development will not significantly impact the biophysical, hydrological, or ecological integrity of the adjoining coastal wetland, or the quantity and quality of surface and groundwater flows to and from the wetland;

  3. Pursuant to Section 4.15(1)(a)(ii) of the Environmental Planning and Assessment Act 1979, the proposed development is inconsistent with the following parts of Byron Development Control Plan 2014:
    1. Chapter B1, Part B1.2.1 ‘Development Envelope Controls’.
    2. Chapter B4, Part B4.2.2 ‘Parking Layout Standards’.
    3. Chapter B9, Part B9.9.2 ‘Landscaping of Car Parking and Open Storage Areas’;

  4. Pursuant to Section 4.15(1)(b) of the Environmental Planning and Assessment Act 1979, the proposed development will likely result in a significant loss of amenity for adjoining residences due to increased traffic noise and car headlights shining into bedrooms as vehicles exit the site;

  5. Pursuant to Section 4.15(1)(b) of the Environmental Planning and Assessment Act 1979, insufficient information has been provided demonstrating that the proposed development will not have a significant adverse impact on the natural environment including threatened species and ecological communities;

  6. Pursuant to Section 4.15(1)(c) of the Environmental Planning and Assessment Act 1979, the proposal has not demonstrated that the site is suitable for the proposed development; and

  7. Pursuant to Section 4. 15(1)(e) of the Environmental Planning and Assessment Act 1979 the proposal is contrary to the public interest and would create an undesirable precedent. 
The motion was put to the vote and declared carried.
 Crs Lyon, Lowe, Kay, Hauge, Ndiaye, Warth, Swain and Pugh voted in favour of the motion. 
 No Crs voted against the motion.

Moved: Cr Hauge Seconded: Cr Ndiaye
25-645 Resolved: 

That Council:

  1. Does not proceed with the Byron Bay Town Centre Special Entertainment Precinct planning proposal given NSW government feedback that:

    1. The introduction of any sound criteria within a Precinct Management Plan will result in more restrictive sound controls for entertainment sound from licensed venues which is currently not subject to any decibel-based sound controls as a result of recent Vibrancy Reforms. The introduction of sound criteria will therefore disadvantage licensed venues operating before the establishment of a SEP which is inconsistent with the NSW Special Entertainment Precinct Guidelines;
    2. The trading hours within the draft Precinct Management Plan (6am to midnight for indoor and 6am to 11pm for outdoor), which were informed by a review of existing business trading hours, development consents, exempt development provisions and community consultation, represent minimal opportunity for uplift in business trading hours. These trading hours will require most licensed venues to submit a development application to trade late which is inconsistent with the NSW Special Entertainment Precinct Guidelines;

  2. Instead of 1, proceeds with the planning proposal attached to this report (Attachment 5 - E2026/5525) to amend LEP 2014 to permit certain temporary events in the Byron Bay Rail Corridor as development permitted without consent, with amendments:

    1. That temporary events may proceed between 6am-10pm without consent, but outside these hours only with consent

  3. Forwards the planning proposal (Attachment 5 - E2026/5525) to the NSW Department of Planning, Housing and Infrastructure for a Gateway determination;

  4. Pending a positive gateway determination and completion of further studies (if required), undertakes public exhibition of the planning proposal in accordance with the determination requirements, and ensures the management policy and plan of management for the area are exhibited at the same time and include:

    1. event application processes
    2. prioritisation of local events and events outside of peak seasons including school holidays
    3. noise considerations and mitigation of impacts to adjoining residential areas
    4. alcohol considerations and risk mitigation

  5. Considers submissions in a report post-exhibition that includes any recommended changes to the planning proposal for final adoption;

  6. Notes the update on Vibrancy Reforms and the implications for licensed venues in Byron Shire;

  7. Subject to point 1, does not proceed with the establishment a Special Entertainment Precinct Working Group as per Resolution 25-577; and

  8. Subject to 2, supports the preparation of a Town Centre Activation Plan to guide and deliver entertainment and activation events in the Town Centre and Rail corridor as per Resolution 25-577. 


The motion was put to the vote and declared carried.
 Crs Lyon, Lowe, Kay, Hauge, Ndiaye, Warth, Swain and Pugh voted in favour of the motion. 
 No Crs voted against the motion.

Moved: Cr Ndiaye Seconded: Cr Hauge
25-591 Resolved: 
I move that Council submits the following Motion for consideration at the National General Assembly calling on the Federal Government to:
  1. Establish a National River and Coastal Catchment Health Fund providing dedicated, ongoing funding for the recovery and long term management of Australia’s most degraded river systems, including both inland and coastal rivers that meet one or more of the following criteria:
    1. Poor or very poor ecological condition based on recognised monitoring frameworks.

    2. Repeated fish kills, blackwater events or severe water quality incidents.

    3. Significant downstream impacts on estuaries, coastal waters or marine ecosystems.

    4. Substantial social or economic impacts on communities, including fisheries, aquaculture, agriculture, tourism or drinking water.

    5. Complex governance arrangements spanning multiple local government or state boundaries.

  2. Appoint independent River Commissioners for priority river systems identified through these criteria, with statutory responsibility to improve the health of rivers, their catchments, tributaries, estuaries and connected marine environments.

  3. Ensure funding prioritises nature based and place based solutions, grounded in scientific research and monitoring and incorporating First Nations leadership and knowledge systems, including community education, riparian fencing and erosion control, wetland and floodplain restoration, catchment revegetation, soil regeneration and weed management, recognising the long term environmental, economic and climate resilience benefits of these approaches.

  4. Establish clear federal, state and local government coordination frameworks that recognise rivers frequently cross local government and state boundaries and require integrated catchment to coast planning and long term investment.

  5. Provide River Commissioners with appropriate powers to promote transparency and accountability, including the ability to identify sources of pollution and require proportionate, evidence based rectification and restoration actions, while supporting collaboration with landholders, industries, Traditional Owners and communities.

  6. Require public annual reporting to Parliament on river health outcomes, including water quality, ecological condition, economic and community impacts and progress against agreed recovery objectives.

The motion was put to the vote and declared carried.
 Crs Lyon, Lowe, Kay, Hauge, Ndiaye, Warth, Swain and Pugh voted in favour of the motion. 
 No Crs voted against the motion.

Moved: Cr Hauge Seconded: Cr Lowe
25-618 Resolved: 
I move that Council writes to the relevant NSW State Government Ministers and MPs seeking their urgent support to improve the health of the Richmond River, including by:

  1. Appointing a Richmond River Commissioner with a statutory obligation to improve the health of the Richmond River, its catchment, tributaries and estuary;

  2. Providing ongoing funding of the Northern Rivers Watershed Initiative, including increased funding for research and education on River recovery, fencing provisions for riverbanks, wetland restoration, catchment revegetation, and weed management; and

  3. Establishing a revolving land acquisition fund and a voluntary covenant program for the purchase and sale of key pieces of low lying agricultural land, based on the prior work of Rous County Council’s “Operation Recovery” Stages 1 and 2.

The motion was put to the vote and declared carried.
 Crs Lyon, Lowe, Kay, Hauge, Ndiaye, Warth, Swain and Pugh voted in favour of the motion. 
 No Crs voted against the motion.

Moved: Cr Ndiaye Seconded: Cr Hauge
25-621 Resolved: 
I move that Council:
  1. Notes the Australian Government’s 16 January 2026 announcement of $24.7 million over three years to deliver a national pilot for recycling solar panels and establish up to 100 pilot collection sites nationwide, to be administered through a pilot administrator under the Australian Government’s product stewardship framework;

  2. Writes to the relevant Federal Minister(s) acknowledging Council’s support for the national pilot program and expressing Byron Shire Council’s interest in participating in the trial, including advocating for the Northern Rivers to host one of the pilot collection sites;

  3. Requests that the Northern Rivers Joint Organisation formally incorporate solar panel reuse and recycling into the remit of the Regional Residual Waste Steering Committee, and seek in-principle commitment from member councils to participate in a regional pilot should the opportunity arise;

  4. Supports, in principle, the investigation of a Northern Rivers Solar Recovery Hub, subject to:
    1. Regional endorsement through the Northern Rivers Joint Organisation;
    2. Commitment from participating Northern Rivers councils; and
    3. Identification of an appropriate governance model, delivery partner and funding pathway; and

  5. Requests that the General Manager continue advocacy and engagement with the pilot administrator, industry bodies (including the Smart Energy Council), and Northern Rivers councils, and report progress to Council via the Climate Change and Resource Recovery Advisory Committee, including advice on governance, site options, resource implications and any funding opportunities should they become available.

The motion was put to the vote and declared carried.

Moved: Cr Pugh Seconded: Cr Lyon
25-646 Resolved: 
That Council:
  1. Notes the significant social and economic success of the "on-formation" sections of the Northern Rivers Rail Trail (NRRT) already completed in the Tweed, Lismore and Richmond Valley Shires, which have generated substantial regional tourism and local business opportunities;

  2. Acknowledges that preliminary access assessments and environmental reports demonstrate that a "multi-use" (rail with trail) model for the Mullumbimby to Byron Bay section would result in significant technical complexity and environmental impacts;

  3. Seeks funding to progress the planning, design, and implementation of an "on-formation" rail trail in stages to enable the completion of the entire length of the rail corridor within the Byron Shire, including the Mullumbimby to Byron Bay section (acknowledging that the Byron Solar Train has a lease over a section), to ensure a technically consistent and cost-effective regional project;

  4. Ensures the planning and design stages of Part 3 respond to the recommendations of the Flora Assessment. The design of the rail trail and review of environmental factors shall to the fullest extent possible assess the environmental impacts of the project including but not limited to the addressing the NSW Biodiversity Conservation Act 2016 and the Environment Protection and Biodiversity Conservation Act 1999. The review of environmental factors shall include mitigation measures to limit the impact on threatened species; and

  5. Continues to advocate that any approach includes ensuring the rail corridor remains in public ownership.

The motion was put to the vote and declared carried.
 Crs Lyon, Kay, Hauge, Ndiaye, Swain and Pugh voted in favour of the motion. 
 Crs Lowe and Warth voted against the motion.

Moved: Cr Hauge Seconded: Cr Warth
25-627 Resolved: 
I move that Council:
  1. Writes to the relevant Ministers and Ballina MP Tamara Smith:
    1. Expressing concern that despite the numerous and significant floods impacting the state in recent years, NSW Government funding for the 2025-26 Flood Management Program amounted to only 16% of the total funds request by councils to undertake critical risk assessments and flood studies to protect our communities;

    2. Requesting grant funding for the Brunswick River Floodplain Risk Management and Prioritisation studies be allocated as a matter of urgency, noting that the adopted 2020 study has not been updated since the 2022 floods; and

  2. Once grant funding is allocated and the study commences, includes nature-based solutions such as catchment revegetation as a flood mitigation option for consideration in the study and invites researchers and practitioners from the “Nature-based Solutions: Building Flood Resilience” Wilsons River project to an upcoming Floodplain Risk Management Advisory Committee meeting to discuss the evidence-base for this approach.

The motion was put to the vote and declared carried.
 Crs Lyon, Lowe, Kay, Hauge, Ndiaye, Warth, Swain and Pugh voted in favour of the motion. 
 No Crs voted against the motion.

Moved: Cr Hauge Seconded: Cr Lowe
25-628 Resolved: 
I move that Council:
  1. Prepares a report on the current status of long-term tenancies (including basic information such as numbers, locations, rents, along with an overview of the compliance works program, policies and processes); and

  2. Prepares a report on options to expand the number of long-term low income tenancies, transitional housing tenancies, and long-term tenancies available to Traditional Owners at Council-owned caravan parks, including:
    1. how to ensure long-term low-income residential tenants of Council-owned caravan parks and dwellings pay no more than 30% of their income in rent/fees
    2. consideration of rezoning where required
    3. how changes would impact the current management contract
    4. if an MoU with government or a CHP would support this expansion

  3. Prepares an urgent, confidential Report for the next Council meeting on long-term residential tenancy matters currently before a tribunal or expected to go to a tribunal, including Council’s legal advice with respect to these matters. 

The motion was put to the vote and declared carried.
 Crs Lowe, Kay, Hauge, Ndiaye, Warth, Swain and Pugh voted in favour of the motion. 
 Cr Lyon voted against the motion.


The meeting adjourned at 2.54pm for a short break and reconvened at 3.14pm.

Moved: Cr Ndiaye Seconded: Cr Lowe
25-642 Resolved: 
I move that Council submits a Notice of Motion for consideration to the National General Assembly calling on the Federal Government to establish a National Sovereign Wealth Fund to capture a fair share of revenue from Australia’s non-renewable natural resources for the long-term benefit of current and future generations that:
  1. Calls on the Australian Government to ensure that such a fund is:
    1. capitalised through resource-based revenue mechanisms, including but not limited to resource rent taxes, levies or royalties on non-renewable resource extraction and exports;
    2. independently governed, transparent and protected from short-term political influence; and
    3. returns are invested in long-term national priorities, including intergenerational equity, economic resilience, infrastructure, housing, climate transition and future public services; 
    4. includes a dedicated funding stream to support Local Government climate adaptation, disaster resilience, and community transition initiatives, recognising councils as the first responders to climate impacts and critical delivery partners in the national transition; and
  2. Requests that ALGA advocate for a nationally consistent approach to resource wealth management that recognises Australia’s natural resources as collectively owned assets and ensures their extraction delivers enduring public benefit.

The motion was put to the vote and declared carried.
 Crs Lyon, Lowe, Kay, Hauge, Ndiaye, Warth, Swain and Pugh voted in favour of the motion. 
 No Crs voted against the motion.

Moved: Cr Ndiaye Seconded: Cr Warth
26-7 Resolved: 
That Council:

  1. Notes the status of the Safer Community Compact, the range of community safety initiatives undertaken across the Byron Shire and future opportunities to strengthen Council’s involvement in relevant community safety initiatives;

  2. Notes the key findings of the independent review of the Street Cruise Program included in Confidential attachment E2026/4819;

  3. Notes transitional funding arrangements proposed from July 2026 and commits to funding Byron Youth Services up to $25,000pa to deliver an alternative, mutually agreed youth safety program until June 2027, and that this proposed alternative program be confirmed subject to a further report to Council;

  4. Notes that officers will work collaboratively with Byron Youth Services management to investigate an alternative youth program, which appropriately manages operational risk, Work Health and Safety, and legislative compliance;

  5. Commits to funding targeted, evidence-based youth safety initiatives through Council's annual Community Initiatives Program;

  6. Notes that a separate report will be presented to Council to consider the updated 2026/27 Community Initiatives Funding Guidelines, which will detail a proposed Community Safety stream; and

  7. Thanks and acknowledges the important and historical outreach services delivered by, Byron Youth Services and specifically, the Street Cruise Program.

The motion was put to the vote and declared carried.
Cr Lyon, Cr Hauge, Cr Ndiaye, Cr Dods, Cr Warth, Cr Swain voted in favour of the motion. 
None voted against the motion.

26-37 Resolved
That Report No. 13.6 be lifted from the table.
The motion was put to the vote and declared carried.


Moved: Cr Lyon Seconded: Cr Dods
26-11 Resolved: 
  1. Pursuant to Section 4.16 of the Environmental Planning & Assessment Act 1979, Development Application No. 10.2025.32.1 for the formalisation of works undertaken without consent, and alterations and additions to existing restaurant and commercial premises involving two (2) restaurants, removal of vegetation be granted consent subject to the recommended conditions of approval in Attachment 3 (Council Doc # E2026/13673), subject to Conditions 18 and 82 being amended to read.
 
18. Shuttle Bus Management Plan 
 
The application for any Construction Certificate is to include details of the Shuttle Bus operation for when the restaurant is open. The Management Plan to cover the following minimum requirements:
a) Frequency of Trips being a minimum of two return trips per hour;
b) Minimum capacity of the bus to be 10 patrons or more; 
c) Ownership details of the shuttle bus and where they will be housed when not in use;
d) Booking arrangements for patrons;
e) Measures to encourage local patrons and guests to catch the shuttle bus and the catchment areas for the bus;
f) Record keeping arrangements to capture data on the effectiveness of the shuttle bus arrangements with details to be submitted to Council for the first three years of operation on a quarterly basis (every 3 months). 
g) that the plan details a pick up and drop off location on either Jonson St or Kingsley St and that patrons are not to be on-loaded or offloaded via the rear Carpark and rear laneway
 
The Management Plan to be submitted to and approved by Council prior to the issue of the Construction Certificate.
  
82. Shuttle Bus Management Plan 
 
The shuttle buses to operate at all times in accordance with the approved Management Plan and be available to take guests to and from the restaurant within the approved catchment areas. 
Details to be submitted to Council on a quarterly basis (every 3 months) on the effectiveness of the shuttle bus as required under the Shuttle Bus Management Plan
 
  1. Notes that staff are requested to review the current parking restrictions to address community concerns about existing parking conflicts during school hours in nearby streets.

The motion was put to the vote and declared carried.
Cr Lyon, Cr Hauge, Cr Ndiaye, Cr Dods, Cr Warth, Cr Swain voted in favour of the motion. 
None voted against the motion.

Moved: Cr Warth Seconded: Cr Ndiaye
26-3 Resolved: 
That Council: 
  1. Notes:
    1. There is evidence of a historical drainage outlet to the ocean north of Fern Beach within Billinudgel Nature Reserve.
    2. Coastal outlet channels can provide important ecological functions, including the creation of estuarine and coastal wetland habitat.
    3. Managed environmental outflows may assist with the movement and drainage of floodwaters from surrounding low-lying areas during major rainfall events.
    4. Investigating environmental and hydrological conditions at this location may help inform options to enhance biodiversity outcomes and improve local floodwater management.

  2. Requests staff include investigation of the recreation of an environmental outflow at the historical outlet location (approx. GPS 153.5506, -28.4856) in the Brunswick River Floodplain Risk Management Study and Plan.

  3. Requests staff prepare a report on coastal creek outlet options for flood mitigation for an upcoming Floodplain Risk Advisory Committee, with comments on the methods for:
    1. Hydrological modelling of potential flood mitigation benefits and drainage impacts.
    2. Environmental impact assessment, including potential biodiversity and habitat outcomes.
    3. Coastal processes assessment, including sand transport and shoreline stability.
    4. Land tenure and regulatory approval requirements, including consultation with the NSW National Parks and Wildlife Service and appropriate Aboriginal Stakeholders.
    5. Preliminary cost estimates and identification of potential funding sources.
    6. Staged implementation options, including temporary or seasonal trial openings where appropriate.

  4. Requests staff engage with their counterparts at Tweed Shire Council regarding their coastal creeks study and possible engagement and collaboration.

The motion was put to the vote and declared carried.
Cr Lyon, Cr Hauge, Cr Ndiaye, Cr Dods, Cr Warth, Cr Swain voted in favour of the motion. 
None voted against the motion.


PROCEDURAL MOTION

Moved: Cr Ndiaye Seconded: Cr Swain
26-2 Resolved
That the vote on the recommendations to be adopted as a whole moved by Cr Swain and seconded by Cr Lyon be recommitted to enable the reservation of item 13.11.
The motion was put to the vote and declared carried.


Moved: Cr Swain Seconded: Cr Lyon
26-6 Resolved
That Council recommits that the remaining recommendations not reserved be adopted as a whole. Each recommendation retaining its original Resolution number.
The motion was put to the vote and declared carried.


Moved: Cr Ndiaye Seconded: Cr Hauge
26-30 Resolved 
That Council change the order of business to deal with Reports 13.2 and 13.6 next on the Agenda.
The motion was put to the vote and declared carried.

Moved: Cr Ndiaye Seconded: Cr Swain
26-16 Resolved: 
That Council:
  1. Notes the report; and

  2. Authorises the following amendments to staff delegations to enable Section 4.55(1) - Minor Errors or No Environmental Impact to be determined under delegated authority to ensure council complies with the new prescribed deemed-approval provisions:

Determine Development Applications (including Section 4.55 and Modification Applications) and Complying Development Applications made under the Environmental Planning and Assessment Act 1979 and relevant Regulations


  1. To determine development applications (including applications made pursuant to Section 4.55 and Section 4.56 of the Environmental Planning and Assessment Act 1979, Complying Development Applications and Subdivision applications) that comply with relevant Acts and Regulations together with Council's LEP and DCP, any other relevant DCP and Council policies and no material objections have been received.
  2. To determine development applications (including applications made pursuant to Section 4.55 and Section 4.56 of the Environmental Planning and Assessment Act 1979 and Subdivision applications as above except where approval of the application would result in a material adverse impact on a person who made a written objection to the application due to non-compliance with a development standard in Council’s LEP.

    Delegated approval is permissible if the objection can be resolved through a condition of consent or has been addressed by way of amendment to plans.
  3. To determine applications made pursuant to Section 4.55 and Section 4.56 of the Environmental Planning and Assessment Act 1979, and relevant Regulations, where objections have been received but those objections do not raise any issues not covered when the original application was determined 
  4. To determine applications made pursuant to and in accordance with Section 4.55 and Section 4.56 of the Environmental Planning and Assessment Act 1979, and relevant Regulations, where objections have been received but those objections do not raise any issues not covered when the original application was determined.
  5. To determine Modification Applications pursuant to the Environmental Planning and Assessment Act 1979.

Note: Notwithstanding subclauses (a) and (b) above, 

 

  1. any development application or application to modify a consent under 4.55(1A), 4.55(2) and 4.56 must be referred to Council for determination, following a written request from at least two Councillors to the General Manager. 
  2. any development application or application to modify a consent under 4.55(1A), 4.55(2) and 4.56 that, in the opinion of the Director Sustainable Environment & Economy, is of significant public interest or where any determination may result in major policy implications must be referred to Council for determination.

 

Development assessment determination exceptions - Director
 

Make all determinations necessary under Part 4 Development Assessment and Consent of the Environmental Planning and Assessment Act, 1979 (Delegation DEG088) except as listed below:

  1. Any development application that is referred to Council by the Planning Review Committee except where the stated issues requiring referral are subsequently resolved to the satisfaction of the members of the Committee.

  2. Any development application:

    1. that has an estimated value exceeding $10,000,000 (inc GST) or 

    2. for subdivision of land that will create 10 or more lots. (Res 22-311)

    3. Section 4.55(1A), 4.55(2) and 4.56 applications for development applications determined by Council or the Court unless the Planning Review Committee has resolved that the Section 4.55 under 4.55(1A), 4.55(2) and 4.56 application can be determined under delegated authority.

    4. Any designated development, development pursuant to the provisions of Section 4.10 of the Environmental Planning and Assessment Act, 1979.

    5. Any development application where there is an application to vary development standards by 10% or more (except when associated with Development Applications with an estimated value exceeding $10,000,000 (inc GST) or any subdivision exceeding 10 lots). (Res 22-311)

    6. Any development application proposing strata subdivision in a 7(f2)(Urban Coastal Land Zone) under clause 32 of the Byron Local Environmental Plan (except any subdivision exceeding 10 lots). (Res 22-311)

    7. The amendment or review of all development applications, except the review of a determination made by the Council, and not by a delegate of the Council, of an application for approval or an application that may be reviewed under Section 8.2 of the Environmental Planning and Assessment Act 1979. (Res 15-234)

Note:

Except where the Development Application is proposed to be determined as a refusal as a result of inadequate information being provided for determination and/or where the application is fundamentally flawed including but not limited to significant planning control breaches and prohibited development.



The motion was put to the vote and declared carried.
Cr Hauge, Cr Ndiaye, Cr Dods, Cr Warth, Cr Swain voted in favour of the motion. 
None voted against the motion.
Cr Lyon was not present for the vote.

Moved: Cr Kay Seconded: Cr Dods
26-61 Resolved: 
  1. That Council, in accordance with s. 178 (1) (b) of the Local Government (General) Regulation 2021 (NSW) (Regulation), decline to accept the tender submitted with respect to the proposed contract for waste collection services; 

  2. That Council, in accordance with s. 178 (3) (e) of the Regulation, enter into negotiations with any person (whether or not the person was a tenderer). Specifically, negotiations with the persons identified for that purpose in the Report as Nominated Persons, in respect of the waste collection services, and in the manner described in the Report, with a view to entering into a contract for the services (for an initial services term of 10 years with extensions as detailed in the contract), as included in the RFT; 

  3. That Council notes, in accordance with s. 178 (4)(a) of the Regulation, that the reasons for Council declining to invite fresh tenders as referred to in ss. 178(3)(b)-(d) of the Regulation, include that: 
    1. it is not expected that further market testing will provide a more satisfactory result; and
    2. it is anticipated that a satisfactory result can be achieved through negotiating with one or more of the Nominated Persons in the manner described in the Report; 

  4. That Council notes, in accordance with s. 178 (4)(b) of the Regulation, that the reasons for Council determining to enter into negotiations with the Nominated Persons, include that:
    1. Council is satisfied that each of the Nominated Persons would be capable of undertaking the relevant services, pending conditions being achieved; and
    2. it is anticipated that a satisfactory outcome can be achieved through negotiations with one or more of the Nominated Persons;

  5. That Council notifies the tenderer, as appropriate, that the tender was not accepted;

  6. That, pursuant to s. 377 of the Local Government Act 1993 (NSW), Council delegates authority to the General Manager, or their nominated delegate, to directly negotiate with one or more of the Nominated Persons in the manner described in the Report, for the purpose of entering into a contract in relation to the subject matter of the RFT, and following successful negotiation, to finalise and execute the contract on behalf of Council; and

  7. That Council makes public its decision in accordance with Clause 179(b) of the Local Government (General) Regulation 2021.

The motion was put to the vote and declared carried.
Cr Lyon, Cr Lowe, Cr Kay, Cr Ndiaye, Cr Dods, Cr Warth, Cr Swain voted in favour of the motion. 
None voted against the motion.

Moved: Cr Swain Seconded: Cr Kay
26-48 Resolved: 
That Council:

  1. Respectfully revokes existing delegations and dissolves two Section 355 Committees, effective at 4pm on 29 May 2026, namely: a. Ocean Shores Community Centre Section 355 Management Committee, and b. South Golden Beach Hall Section 355 Management Committee;

  2. Respectfully revokes existing delegations and dissolves the Suffolk Park Community Hall Section 355 Committee effective at 4pm on 31 July 2026;

  3. Notifies the Section 355 Committee members of the end of their membership in the Committee, and expresses Council's gratitude for years of service to Council and the community, with encouragement to continue volunteer involvement in the Friends of the Hall program where desired; and

  4. Ensures assets and funds currently managed by each Section 355 Committee are returned to Council’s direct control prior to Committee dissolution.

The motion was put to the vote and declared carried.
Cr Lyon, Cr Lowe, Cr Kay, Cr Ndiaye, Cr Dods, Cr Warth, Cr Swain voted in favour of the motion. 
None voted against the motion.
