Council remained in Confidential Session for the following reasons:

  1. That pursuant to Section 10A(2)(d) and (g) of the Local Government Act 1993, Council resolves to move into Confidential Session to discuss the report CONFIDENTIAL - Update - Planning Agreement for Gulgan Village, The Saddle Road, Brunswick Heads.

  2. That the reasons for closing the meeting to the public to consider this item be that the report contains:
d. commercial information of a confidential nature that would, if disclosed:
i. prejudice the commercial position of the person who supplied it, or
ii. confer a commercial advantage on a competitor of the council, or
iii. reveal a trade secret,

g. advice concerning litigation, or advice that would otherwise be privileged from production in legal proceedings on the ground of legal professional privilege.

  1. That on the balance it is considered that receipt and discussion of the matter in open Council would be contrary to the public interest, as the terms of the Planning Agreement contains information that would be privileged, and of a commercial nature.

PROCEDURAL MOTION
Moved: Cr Lyon Seconded: Cr Ndiaye
26-89 Resolved that Council move into Committee to allow for free debate.
The motion was put to the vote and declared carried.
Cr Kay was not present for the vote.

The meeting adjourned at 3:21pm for a recess break and reconvened at 3:40pm.

PROCEDURAL MOTION
Moved: Cr Ndiaye Seconded: Cr Dods
26-94 Resolved that Council move out of Committee and resume the Ordinary Meeting.
The motion was put to the vote and declared carried.
Cr Kay was not present for the vote.

Moved: Cr Dods Seconded: Cr Ndiaye
26-33 Resolved: 
  1. That Council supports amendment to the planning agreement for Gulgan Village such that:
    1. Reference to the Arakwal contribution is removed from the planning agreement.
    2. A stand-alone Affordable Housing Contribution of 5% is included in the agreement, noting that this reflects the residual affordable housing contribution following the removal of the Arakwal component and is consistent with the combined 10% contribution quantum as established by resolutions 24-568 and 25-049.
    3. The combined 10% contribution quantum as established by resolutions 24-568 and 25-049 is provided in perpetuity.
    4. The planning agreement is registered on title as soon as practicable following LEP gazettal, with Council and the proponent's lawyers conferring to develop security arrangements where appropriate that protects Councils interests and mechanisms for the restriction to be removed immediately upon the subdivision works being completed for each stage if possible.

  2. That Council notes that the accelerated timing of the Gulgan Village planning proposal continues to present certain challenges in relation to key infrastructure planning, funding, and delivery which is the subject of ongoing discussions between Council and the proponent as part of the concurrent planning proposal and planning agreement process.

  3. That Council requests preparation of separate developer contributions (7.11) plan for Gulgan Village as an urban release area and that this plan includes appropriate mechanisms to offset works being provided beyond what is needed to service this stage of the development.

  4. That the Development Servicing Plan for water and sewer contributions for the entire Saddle Road precinct be prioritised with appropriate mechanisms to offset additional works beyond what is needed to service the development.

  5. That all works not listed in the VPA (Schedule 2 - development contributions requirements) will be subject to normal development assessment processes, noting that the VPA includes dispute resolution mechanism embedded within it.

  6. That the following initial planning documents to be produced by Council are finalised and publicly released as a matter of urgency:
    1. Saddle Rd Precinct Infrastructure Priority Plan
    2. Saddle Rd Precinct Structure Plan.

  7. That Council respectfully requests a copy of the agreement between Bundjalung of Byron Bay Aboriginal Corporation (Arakwal) (BOBBAC) and Creative Capital including details about the value, location, and type of housing being provided as part of the agreement, and proof that the contribution to BOBBAC is equal to the 5% contribution value that is being contributed to Council.

  8. That Council notes that the Gulgan Village planning proposal will be exhibited (with the updated draft Planning Agreement and draft Development Control Plan) in accordance with the Gateway conditions as soon as possible.

The motion was put to the vote and declared carried.
Cr Lyon, Cr Lowe, Cr Ndiaye, Cr Dods, Cr Warth, Cr Swain voted in favour of the motion. 
None voted against the motion.
Cr Kay was not present for the vote.

PROCEDURAL MOTION
Moved: Cr Ndiaye Seconded: Cr Swain
26-92 Resolved that the meeting move out of Confidential Session. 
The motion was put to the vote and declared carried.
Cr Kay was not present for the vote.

26-35 Resolved: 

  1. That Council notes that the expanded audit of Council-owned or managed land undertaken in response to Resolution 25-393, has identified nil (no new or additional) properties for further investigation as detailed in this report; and that staff will continue to investigate additional parcels as they emerge or are identified through other processes; and any future publications of the list of audited properties includes a snapshot of a map.

  2. That Council:

    1. endorses further investigation of a Council‑owned site (details not disclosed in accordance with Resolution 25‑393(2)) through an appropriate process to assess site suitability and identify the necessary pathways to support the delivery of suitable accommodation options for vulnerable women and children;

    2. allocates up to $20,000 funding at a future quarterly budget review to enable this work; and

    3. requests a further report to Council on the outcomes of this investigation and assessment

  3. That Council notes that staff will continue to work with the Queer Family to identify a suitable location for service delivery, including providing notice of upcoming expression of interest processes for leases or licenses which may be suitable.


The motion was put to the vote and declared carried.
Cr Lyon, Cr Lowe, Cr Kay, Cr Ndiaye, Cr Dods, Cr Warth, Cr Swain voted in favour of the motion. 
None voted against the motion.

Council remained in Confidential Session for the following reasons:

  1. That pursuant to Section 10A(2)(d) of the Local Government Act 1993, Council resolves to move into Confidential Session to discuss the report CONFIDENTIAL - Proposed Closure and disposal of Unconstructed Road (Laneway) between Bryce & Glasgow Streets, Suffolk Park.

  2. That the reason for closing the meeting to the public to consider this item be that the report contains commercial information of a confidential nature that would, if disclosed:

    2. confer a commercial advantage on a competitor of the council, or

  1. That Council defers this matter until the meeting of 21 May 2026; and

","reportContent":null,"minutesDiscussion":"PROCEDURAL MOTION
Moved: Cr Ndiaye Seconded: Cr Dods
26-82 Resolved:
  1. That pursuant to Section 10A(2)(g) of the Local Government Act 1993, Council resolves to move into Confidential Session to discuss the report PLANNING - Development Application 10.2025.545.1 for Alterations and Additions to an Existing Dwelling at 13 Terrace Street, New Brighton.

  2. That the reason for closing the meeting to the public to consider this item be that the report contains:
    (g) advice concerning litigation, or advice that would otherwise be privileged from production in legal proceedings on the ground of legal professional privilege

  3. That on the balance it is considered that receipt and discussion of the matter in open Council would be contrary to the public interest, to enable a question that may concern potential legal privilege.

The motion was put to the vote and declared carried.

PROCEDURAL MOTION
Moved: Cr Ndiaye Seconded: Cr Lowe
26-85 Resolved that Council move into Committee to allow for free debate.
The motion was put to the vote and declared carried.

PROCEDURAL MOTION
Moved: Cr Ndiaye Seconded: Cr Lyon
26-83 Resolved that Council move out of Committee and resume the Ordinary Meeting.
The motion was put to the vote and declared carried.

PROCEDURAL MOTION
Moved: Cr Ndiaye Seconded: Cr Dods
26-86 Resolved that the meeting move out of Confidential Session.
The motion was put to the vote and declared carried.

Moved: Cr Dods Seconded: Cr Lyon
26-40 Resolved: 
That Council:

  1. Defers determination of Development Application 10.2025.545.1 for alterations and additions to an existing dwelling at 13 Terrace Street, New Brighton, and invites the applicant to submit further information and/or amended plans to Council’s satisfaction either:
    1. demonstrating why the proposal should properly be characterised as alterations and additions to an existing dwelling, having regard to the extent of demolition, reconstruction, scale of works and the applicable provisions of Chapter 1 Part J of Byron Development Control Plan 2010; or
    2. amending the proposal so that it satisfies, or more closely aligns with, the requirements and intent of Chapter 1 Part J of Byron Development Control Plan 2010.

  2. That the matter be brought back to Council in the June 2026 Ordinary Meeting.

  3. Requests staff to provide a workshop briefing to councillors on Chapter 1 Part J of Byron Development Control Plan 2010, including:
    1. its history and policy rationale;
    2. its relationship with the relevant LEP and State Government provisions applying to development affected by coastal erosion and coastal processes, including the current coastal management framework and any relevant Coastal Management Program; and
    3. how it is interpreted and applied in the assessment of development in the coastal zone.

The motion was put to the vote and declared carried.
Cr Lyon, Cr Ndiaye, Cr Dods, Cr Warth, Cr Swain voted in favour of the motion. 
Cr Lowe, Cr Kay voted against the motion.

Moved: Cr Ndiaye
26-45 Resolved: 
That Council:

  1. Notes the Country Mayors Association of NSW "Invest in Us" campaign advocating for increased Commonwealth Financial Assistance Grants to Local Governments. The campaign seeks to restore at least 1% of total Commonwealth taxation revenue for local Councils across Australia

  2. Recognises the critical role Local Government plays in delivering essential services and infrastructure that underpin community wellbeing, economic vitality, and national resilience.

  3. Supports the campaign's core message: 'Invest in us so we can invest in them.'

  4. Commits to participating in the campaign by:
    1. Sharing campaign materials through Council communication channels
    2. Engaging with local media and community stakeholders to raise awareness.
    3. Lobbying Federal representatives to support the funding increase.

Moved: Cr Lowe Seconded: Cr Swain
26-42 Resolved: 
That Council:

  1. Investigates a partnership with a university (such as Southern Cross University, Griffith University or the University of NSW) to support a researcher (e.g. PhD student) to carry out a comprehensive study on the financial impacts of tourism on the Byron Shire.

  2. Ensures the scope of the research addresses both the positive and negative impacts of the visitor economy and explicitly considers both the direct costs and incomes to council along with important externalities. This may include:
    1. Positive impacts: Employment generation, local business vitality, the total financial contribution the Byron Shire makes to the economy of New South Wales, and how much income Byron Council receives as a result of the tourism economy
    2. Negative impacts: The cost of maintaining community and operational infrastructure, the escalation of rubbish and litter (specifically in hotspots like Byron Bay), and the deterioration of the natural environment and biodiversity, and how much the tourism economy costs Byron Shire Council

  3. Utilises the completed study as a primary evidence base to lobby the State and Federal governments for increased and sustainable funding models, exploring mechanisms such as tourism/bed taxes, land tax reallocations, or developer contributions specifically for visitor-related infrastructure.

  4. Requests that the study highlights the unique role of Byron Shire as a major "Meeting Place" and economic driver for the State, emphasizing the current disparity between the revenue generated for the State and the costs borne by local ratepayers.

  5. Requests that the study consider the potential impacts of major national events, including the Brisbane 2032 Olympic and Paralympic Games, on visitor demand, infrastructure pressures, environmental impacts and financial burden on Byron Shire.

The motion was put to the vote and declared carried.
Cr Lyon, Cr Lowe, Cr Kay, Cr Ndiaye, Cr Dods, Cr Warth, Cr Swain voted in favour of the motion. 
None voted against the motion.

PROCEDURAL MOTION
Moved: Cr Ndiaye Seconded: Cr Kay
26-79 Resolved that Report No. 9.4 "Release of documents to impacted property owners - 32 Coomburra Crescent, Ocean Shores" rest on the table.
The motion was put to the vote and declared carried.

[IGNORE_INDENT][OUTLINE_NUMBER_FULL_NO_PERIOD][AGENDA_ITEM_NAME]
","reportContent":null,"minutesDiscussion":"
Moved: Cr Ndiaye Seconded: Cr Lowe
26-43 Resolved: 
That Council:

  1. Writes to relevant MPs Ministers at NSW and federal level (including NSW Minister for Water Rose Jackson, NSW Minister for Local Government Ron Hoenig, MP for Ballina Tamara Smith, Minister for for Regional Development and Local Government Kristy McBain, MP for Richmond Justine Elliot) to address the issue of stormwater and drainage funding, including:
    1. Describing the financial unsustainability of stormwater and drainage management in regional councils such as Byron Shire, with a focus on operations, maintenance and asset renewal challenges
    2. Noting that the only dedicated, regular stormwater funding mechanism available — the Stormwater Management Services Charge — has lost approximately half its real value since 2006 due to the absence of indexation, and that it has taken more than two years since the Parliamentary Inquiry handed down its findings for this simple mechanism to be reviewed, further demonstrating the inadequacy of current arrangements
    3. Asserting that stormwater and drainage infrastructure serves a broad public good that extends well beyond individual ratepayers, and that the cost burden of managing this infrastructure should not fall primarily on residents and businesses through charges and rates; and that direct government grants and recurrent funding are the appropriate mechanism to address the current shortfall
    4. Requesting that Byron Shire Council be invited to participate in future consultation and discussion on stormwater and drainage funding reform
    5. Advocating for the establishment of a dedicated recurrent funding stream for stormwater and drainage maintenance, operations and renewal in regional councils
    6. Identifying major maintenance and renewal works that are unfunded, such as the Brunswick Heads Bayside stormwater upgrades, or addressing systematic issues with properties in overland flow paths

  2. Writes to the Chair of the Northern Rivers Joint Organisation requesting that the financial sustainability of stormwater and drainage infrastructure be placed on the agenda for consideration, with a view to developing a joint regional advocacy position to present to the NSW Government.

  3. Engages with Stormwater 2030 and the Sydney Coastal Councils Group to align advocacy efforts on stormwater funding reform

  4. Receives a report including:
    1. Asset maintenance and renewal backlogs specific to stormwater and drainage infrastructure
    2. Current and projected funding gaps over Council’s long term financial planning horizon
    3. An overview of available funding options for both capital works and recurrent maintenance

The motion was put to the vote and declared carried.
Cr Lyon, Cr Lowe, Cr Kay, Cr Ndiaye, Cr Dods, Cr Warth, Cr Swain voted in favour of the motion. 
None voted against the motion.

Moved: Cr Ndiaye Seconded: Cr Dods
26-95 Resolved
That Council move into Committee to allow for free debate.
The motion was put to the vote and declared carried.

Moved: Cr Ndiaye Seconded: None
26-96 Resolved
That Council move out of Committee and resume the Ordinary Meeting.
The motion was put to the vote and declared carried.


Moved: Cr Dods Seconded: Cr Hauge
26-88 Resolved: 
That Council:
  1. Resolves to publicly exhibit the draft Byron Shire Local Infrastructure Contributions Plan 2026 (CP) for a minimum period of 28 calendar days; 
  2. Requests the General Manager to prepare a report to Council, addressing any comments received during the exhibition period, and present the draft Byron Shire Local Infrastructure Contributions Plan 2026 (CP) for adoption by Council or, in the event that no submissions are received, adopt the CP as exhibited; 
  3. Notes feedback received from pre public exhibition period community engagement activities; and
  4. Notes updates made to draft work schedules from pre public exhibition period community engagement activities.
The motion was put to the vote and declared carried.
Cr Lyon, Cr Lowe, Cr Kay, Cr Hauge, Cr Ndiaye, Cr Dods, Cr Warth, Cr Swain, Cr Doherty voted in favour of the motion. 
None voted against the motion.

Moved: Cr Ndiaye Seconded: None
26-97 Resolved: 
I move that Council:
  1. Notes:
    1. The introduction of the Crown Land Management Amendment (Statutory Review) Bill 2026, which proposes significant amendments to the Crown Land Management Act 2016 following the statutory review.
    2. That while the Bill contains some positive elements, these are substantially outweighed by provisions that create significant legal, financial and governance risks for local government.

  2. Notes with serious concern that the Bill proposes to:
    1. Enable the transfer of substantial financial and legal liability from the State Government to local councils.
    2. Allow, via Regulation, councils to be required to indemnify the State Government for past and future liability for:
      1. Native title compensation; and
      2. Other types of compensation, including civil and contractual claims.
    3. Introduce retrospective provisions that may:
      1. Expose councils to liabilities for historic activities, regardless of when they occurred or how those activities occurred;
      2. Enable recovery of costs from councils for legacy land uses, for example former waste or night soil sites on Crown land;
      3. Validate past invalid acts and apply current corrections retrospectively, altering legal rights, Aboriginal Land Rights and land management outcomes.
    4. Expand Ministerial powers to:
      1. Direct how councils manage Crown land;
      2. Require and dictate the content of Plans of Management and new types of strategic plans;
      3. Issue directions, compliance orders, and penalties;
      4. Require councils to undertake works or allow the State to undertake works and recover costs as a debt against local councils.
    5. Shift key governance matters from primary legislation into Regulations and Rules, reducing transparency and parliamentary and public oversight.
    6. Introduce additional administrative, compliance, and reporting obligations, including:
      1. Reintroduction of mandatory annual reporting requirements for local councils, which were abolished years ago to ‘reduce costly administrative burdens on councils’;
      2. Potential requirements to stand up advisory groups;
      3. Expanded record-keeping and data-sharing obligations;
      4. Unspecified future obligations relating to a range of obligations and processes, for example native title processes, that will be defined in future Regulations or Rules.

  3. Recognises that the Bill would also:
    1. Create unquantifiable and potentially uninsurable financial risks for councils.
    2. Limit councils’ ability to mitigate exposure to liabilities, particularly those arising from retrospective provisions.
    3. Enable the assignment of State-negotiated lease obligations and liabilities to councils without consent.
    4. Allow for the resumption of land previously vested in councils, potentially overriding existing agreements.

  4. Considers that:
    1. The Bill represents a significant cost-shifting exercise from the State Government to local government.
    2. Responsibilities are proposed to be transferred without commensurate funding, risk protection or adequate safeguards.
    3. The retrospective nature of key provisions is inappropriate and inconsistent with principles of good governance and legal certainty.
    4. The proposed framework undermines the capacity of councils to sustainably manage Crown land and deliver services to their communities.

  5. Notes the specific implications for Byron Shire Council:
    1. Council manages extensive Crown land assets of high environmental, cultural, and economic value.
    2. The Shire’s coastal and community lands are subject to high levels of public use and environmental sensitivity, increasing exposure to risk.
    3. The proposed changes may significantly impact Council’s financial sustainability and its ability to maintain and manage these assets.
    4. Ratepayers may be exposed to liabilities arising from historic State actions or legacy land uses.

  6. Notes with serious concern the Bill’s adverse impacts on Aboriginal Land Rights and that:
    1. The New South Wales Aboriginal Land Council (NSWALC) has formally lodged a complaint with the Australian Human Rights Commission (AHRC) regarding the Crown Land Management Amendment (Statutory Review) Bill 2026 (the Bill).
    2. Their complaint raises a number of serious concerns, arguing that the Bill disproportionately impacts Aboriginal People, directly undermines Aboriginal land rights in NSW established under the Aboriginal Land Rights Act 1983 (NSW), that there was a complete lack of consultation with the Land Rights network prior to the Bill’s introduction and that the way the Bill and its impacts have been publicly framed has contributed to misunderstandings about the Bill and about Land Rights.

  7. Calls on the NSW Government to:
    1. Withdraw the Bill pending comprehensive review.
    2. Undertake genuine, transparent, and good-faith consultation with local government and Land Rights network.
    3. Ensure any future amendments:
      1. Do not transfer financial or legal liability to councils, or impose on councils operational or administrative obligations, without full funding and indemnity;
      2. Respect prior and existing agreements and management arrangements
      3. Remove or significantly limit retrospective provisions;
      4. Provide clear, certain and State-funded legislative frameworks for Native Title compensation;
      5. Respect Aboriginal Land Rights;
      6. Retain key provisions within primary legislation to ensure appropriate parliamentary scrutiny.

  8. Requests that:
    1. This Mayoral Minute be forwarded to:
      1. The NSW Premier
      2. The Minister for Lands and Property
      3. The Minister for Aboriginal Affairs
      4. The Local Member for Ballina
      5. Local Government NSW (LGNSW)
      6. The Country Mayors Association of NSW
      7. The Leader of the NSW Opposition and the Shadow Minister for Crown Lands
    2. Local Government NSW and the Country Mayors Association advocate strongly for the withdrawal and substantial revision of the Bill.
The motion was put to the vote and declared carried.
Cr Lyon, Cr Lowe, Cr Kay, Cr Hauge, Cr Ndiaye, Cr Dods, Cr Warth, Cr Swain, Cr Doherty voted in favour of the motion. 
None voted against the motion.

Moved: Cr Ndiaye Seconded: Cr Swain
26-116 Resolved: 
That Council:

  1. Accepts the terms of the offer from Healthy North Coast Ltd (HNC) offer to acquire the relocatable structure (the pods) at 15 Tincogan Street Mullumbimby, specifically:
    1. to acquire the pods for $1 in as as-is condition and release HNC from any future claims in relation to maintenance of the asset including site rectification and/or make-good costs;
    2. licence the site to a health and/or medical service(s) that delivers low-cost services to the community; and 
    3. partner with HNC to support the selection of an appropriate service(s) to licence the site;

  2. Notes that development consent (10.2024.1999.1) permits use of the site as a community facility until 16 August 2029, with further approvals required for use beyond this date;

  3. Notes the estimated asset lifespan of approximately 15 years, initial rectification costs of approximately $5,000, annual maintenance costs of approximately $2,000, and estimated decommissioning costs of $20,000, for which a future funding approach is to be considered;

  4. Supports the ongoing use of the community facility at this site for the duration of the building lifespan, subject to development consent.

  5. Supports the proposed collaboration with Healthy North Coast Ltd to
    1. establish a satellite location of a Medical Mental Health Centre or other mental health service aligned with the Medicare Mental Health Centre model, or otherwise  
    2. attract low-cost health and medical services to meet the needs of Byron Shire residents;

  6. Requests a further report to Council prior to allocation or licensing of the asset, addressing:
    1. Proposed use options, including alignment with the MMHC model;
    2. Licensing arrangements, including term (up to 16 August 2029), and fees informed by lifecycle costs;
    3. The outcome of a compliant Expressions of Interest (EOI) or market‑sounding process to identify suitable service providers;

  7. Authorises the General Manager to undertake all actions necessary to finalise the acquisition and prepare the subsequent allocation report, consistent with this resolution.

The motion was put to the vote and declared carried.
Cr Lyon, Cr Lowe, Cr Kay, Cr Hauge, Cr Ndiaye, Cr Dods, Cr Warth, Cr Swain, Cr Doherty voted in favour of the motion. 
None voted against the motion.

  3. Notes the estimated asset lifespan of approximately 15 years, initial rectification costs of approximately $5,000, annual maintenance costs of approximately $2,000, and estimated decommissioning costs of $20,000, for which a future funding approach is to be considered;

  4. Supports the ongoing use of the community facility at this site for the duration of the building lifespan, subject to development consent.

  5. Supports the proposed collaboration with Healthy North Coast Ltd to
    1. establish a satellite location of a Medical Mental Health Centre or other mental health service aligned with the Medicare Mental Health Centre model, or otherwise  
    2. attract low-cost health and medical services to meet the needs of Byron Shire residents;

  6. Requests a further report to Council prior to allocation or licensing of the asset, addressing:
    1. Proposed use options, including alignment with the MMHC model;
    2. Licensing arrangements, including term (up to 16 August 2029), and fees informed by lifecycle costs;
    3. The outcome of a compliant Expressions of Interest (EOI) or market‑sounding process to identify suitable service providers;

  7. Authorises the General Manager to undertake all actions necessary to finalise the acquisition and prepare the subsequent allocation report, consistent with this resolution.

  4. Converts the high ambition net zero pathway into an action plan and implementation roadmap, in the Climate Change Response Strategy and Action Plan, including implementation of the next steps outlined by consultants, 100% Renewables, in their report (Attachment 1 E2026/14746, pg13)

  5. Acknowledges that a future Report to Council will present the draft Climate Change Response Strategy and Action Plan for Councils consideration.

The motion was put to the vote and declared carried.
Cr Lyon, Cr Lowe, Cr Kay, Cr Hauge, Cr Ndiaye, Cr Dods, Cr Warth, Cr Swain, Cr Doherty voted in favour of the motion. 
None voted against the motion.

[IGNORE_INDENT][OUTLINE_NUMBER_FULL_NO_PERIOD][AGENDA_ITEM_NAME]
","reportContent":null,"minutesDiscussion":"
Moved: Cr Ndiaye Seconded: Cr Lowe
26-98 Resolved:
That Council:

  1. Adopts a vision to prioritise natural turf over synthetic turf in public open spaces, recognising synthetic turf as a high‑impact material and restricting its use to circumstances where natural alternatives are demonstrated to be unviable.

  2. Commits to the following principles:
    1. Public open spaces design will seek to minimise heat‑intensive materials and look to contribute to cooling, soil health and climate adaptation, particularly in a warming climate. 
    2. Landscapes should wherever possible primarily function as living systems that support biodiversity, water infiltration and habitat, rather than sealed or plasticised surfaces. 
    3. Council will apply the precautionary principle when selecting materials for public lands where credible evidence identifies potential risks to human health or ecosystems.
    4. Any decisions on artificial turf installations will consider long‑term waste, end‑of‑life disposal, and legacy impacts passed to future communities.

  3. Confirms that natural turf is the preferred default surface treatment for Council‑owned or managed parks, sports fields, passive open space and landscaped areas and that any proposal for new synthetic turf must:
    1. be reported to Council for approval
    2. demonstrate:
      1. Why natural turf or non‑plastic alternatives are not viable for the site;
      2. How climate, heat, hydrology, health and end‑of‑life impacts are to be avoided or minimised; and
      3. That the proposal aligns with Council’s adopted vision and strategic objectives.

  4. Investigates potential amendments to the Development Control Plan (DCP) that would:
    1. Discourage the use of synthetic turf and plastic ground coverings in new developments where natural alternatives are viable; and
    2. Support water‑sensitive, climate‑responsive and high‑amenity landscape outcomes.

  5. Recognises the importance of accessible, robust and climate‑resilient sporting and recreational facilities, and request staff, as part of future reporting, to identify options to maintain or improve field capacity using:
    1. Improved natural turf construction and maintenance techniques;
    2. Enhanced drainage and soil health solutions;
    3. Scheduling, rest and field‑rotation strategies;
    4. Climate‑resilient grass species and non‑plastic surface approaches.

  6. Develops community guidance material promoting climate‑appropriate, low‑maintenance and ecologically sound landscaping alternatives suitable for Byron Shire’s environment and recreational needs.

The motion was put to the vote and declared carried.
Cr Lyon, Cr Lowe, Cr Kay, Cr Hauge, Cr Ndiaye, Cr Dods, Cr Warth, Cr Swain, Cr Doherty voted in favour of the motion. 
None voted against the motion.

    3. Council will apply the precautionary principle when selecting materials for public lands where credible evidence identifies potential risks to human health or ecosystems.
    4. Any decisions on artificial turf installations will consider long‑term waste, end‑of‑life disposal, and legacy impacts passed to future communities.

  3. Confirms that natural turf is the preferred default surface treatment for Council‑owned or managed parks, sports fields, passive open space and landscaped areas and that any proposal for new synthetic turf must:
    1. be reported to Council for approval
    2. demonstrate:
      1. Why natural turf or non‑plastic alternatives are not viable for the site;
      2. How climate, heat, hydrology, health and end‑of‑life impacts are to be avoided or minimised; and
      3. That the proposal aligns with Council’s adopted vision and strategic objectives.

  4. Investigates potential amendments to the Development Control Plan (DCP) that would:
    1. Discourage the use of synthetic turf and plastic ground coverings in new developments where natural alternatives are viable; and
    2. Support water‑sensitive, climate‑responsive and high‑amenity landscape outcomes.

  5. Recognises the importance of accessible, robust and climate‑resilient sporting and recreational facilities, and request staff, as part of future reporting, to identify options to maintain or improve field capacity using:
    1. Improved natural turf construction and maintenance techniques;
    2. Enhanced drainage and soil health solutions;
    3. Scheduling, rest and field‑rotation strategies;
    4. Climate‑resilient grass species and non‑plastic surface approaches.

  6. Develops community guidance material promoting climate‑appropriate, low‑maintenance and ecologically sound landscaping alternatives suitable for Byron Shire’s environment and recreational needs.

That, pursuant to Section 4.16 of the Environmental Planning & Assessment Act 1979, Development Application No. 10.2025.494.1 for alterations and additions to a tourist and visitor accommodation unit, be refused for the following reasons:

  1. Pursuant to section 4.15(1)(a)(i) of the Environmental Planning and Assessment Act 1979, the proposed development contravenes the maximum floor space ratio development standard under clause 4.4 of the Byron Local Environmental Plan 2014. The applicant’s written request has failed to adequately demonstrate that compliance with the development standard is unreasonable or unnecessary in the circumstances, or that there are sufficient environmental planning grounds to justify the proposed contravention

  2. Pursuant to Section 4. 15(1)(e) of the Environmental Planning and Assessment Act 1979 the proposal is contrary to the public interest and would create an undesirable precedent.


The motion was put to the vote and declared carried.
Cr Lowe, Cr Kay, Cr Hauge, Cr Ndiaye, Cr Warth, Cr Doherty voted in favour of the motion. 
Cr Lyon, Cr Dods, Cr Swain voted against the motion.

Moved: Cr Hauge Seconded: Cr Ndiaye
26-103 Resolved:
That Council:

  1. Notes:
    1. that Byron Shire is experiencing increasing climate impacts — including the 2019–20 bushfires, the 2022 floods, Ex-Tropical Cyclone Alfred in 2025, chronic coastal erosion, and increasing tidal inundation — placing growing pressure on local infrastructure, services and community wellbeing.
    2. the rising costs experienced by households, businesses, community organisations and primary producers in responding to these climate impacts, including damage to homes and the natural environment, loss of income and business disruption, increasing insurance premiums, and impacts on physical and mental health.
    3. the growing financial pressure on Council's budget from disaster response and infrastructure repair, and that passing escalating climate-related costs onto ratepayers is neither fair nor sustainable.

  2. Notes that the polluter pays principle holds that those responsible for pollution should contribute to managing its impacts, and that this principle is not currently being applied to climate damage at the national level.

  3. Calls on the Australian Government to:
    1. Establish a Climate Compensation Fund to support communities, households and local governments in meeting the costs of climate adaptation, resilience and disaster recovery; 
    2. Introduce a Climate Pollution Levy on coal, gas and oil export corporations to raise funds for the Climate Compensation Fund; 
    3. Ensure the Climate Compensation Fund includes a dedicated funding stream for local governments commensurate with the scale of financial risks identified in the 2025 National Climate Risk Assessment; and 
    4. Establish a Parliamentary Inquiry into the adequacy of the 2025 National Adaptation Plan, specifically addressing the lack of additional funding for local governments to deliver mandated adaptation responses.

  4. Calls on the Federal Government to provide sustained, legislated funding that enables Byron Shire Council to plan and deliver climate solutions with certainty.

  5. Supports the City of Sydney's motion to the ALGA National General Assembly in June 2026 on national climate adaptation funding and accountability for Australian cities.

  6. Writes to the Federal Minister for Climate Change and Energy and the Federal Member for Richmond, outlining Council's position.

  7. Acknowledges the petition tabled at the Ordinary Meeting.

The motion was put to the vote and declared carried.
Cr Lowe, Cr Kay, Cr Hauge, Cr Ndiaye, Cr Warth voted in favour of the motion. 
Cr Lyon, Cr Dods, Cr Swain, Cr Doherty voted against the motion.

[IGNORE_INDENT][OUTLINE_NUMBER_FULL_NO_PERIOD][AGENDA_ITEM_NAME]

Moved: Cr Hauge Seconded: Cr Ndiaye
26-104 Resolved:
That Council:

  1. Reaffirms its declaration of a housing emergency in Byron Shire.

  2. Notes that “affordable housing” is defined as:
    1. 30% or less of a household’s gross income in Clause 13 of the NSW Housing SEPP, or
    2. 80% or less of market rent in the NSW Affordable Housing Ministerial Guidelines, or
    3. less than 75% of market rent for a Community Housing Provider to retain their charitable tax status.

  3. Acknowledges that we receive contributions of land, housing or money under Affordable Housing Contribution Schemes and Voluntary Planning Agreements , which are then distributed under the Affordable Housing Distribution Plan , and this Distribution Plan states that “households should pay no more than 30% of their gross income in rent” under the SEPP, and that the Minister’s guidelines “also provide for affordable housing to be let at a discount of at least 20% of market rent".

  4. Clarifies that our definition of “affordable housing” is a maximum of 30% of a household’s gross income or 80% of market rent, whichever results in the lower rent for the specific household, and must be retained as such in perpetuity.

  5. Receives a report on the mechanisms by which we ensure such housing is retained under this definition of “affordable” in perpetuity.

  6. Ensures that the definition in Part 4 is:
    1. stated clearly in the AHCSs, all future relevant VPAs, the AHDP and any future Local Housing Distribution Plans ; and
    2. applied for the planned developments at 57 Station St, the old Mullumbimby Hospital Site, and any future affordable housing developments led by Council.

  7. Identifies potential situations where the definition may not apply (e.g. shared equity schemes) and mechanisms by which we can ensure affordability in such situations, and reports this information back to an Ordinary Council Meeting.

  8. Confirms the definition in Part 4 with all Community Housing Providers on our register, asks that they identify if any of their current tenants pay above the rates defined in Part 4 (in general, regardless of LGA of residence), and reports this information back to an Ordinary Council Meeting.

  9. Considers a community education piece to ensure our community is aware of the definition in Part 4 and how it is applied by CHPs on our register.

[IGNORE_INDENT][OUTLINE_NUMBER_FULL_NO_PERIOD][AGENDA_ITEM_NAME]
","reportContent":null,"minutesDiscussion":"
Moved: Cr Hauge Seconded: Cr Ndiaye
26-106 Resolved:
That Council:

  1. Notes:
    1. the growing evidence that the 1% Annual Exceedance Probability (AEP) (1-in-100-year) flood planning standard is insufficient in a climate-changed environment, and that Tweed Shire Council adopted a 0.2% AEP (1-in-500-year) standard as its interim flood planning level in March 2026; and 
    2. that the NSW Department of Climate Change, Energy, the Environment and Water's Coastal Hazards under Sea-Level Rise snapshot (November 2025) now provides NSW-wide coastal erosion and inundation projections to 2150 under multiple emissions scenarios.

  2. Receives a report so that Council can consider the processes for adopting 0.2% AEP (1-in-500-year) as Byron Shire's flood planning standard for new development, and of applying coastal hazard lines projected to 2150 under a high-emissions scenario to land use planning and coastal management decisions, including: 
    1. Identification of all planning, floodplain management, and coastal management instruments that would require amendment; 
    2. Outlining a process for identification of any sites currently included in the Business and Industrial Land Strategy and/or Byron Shire Residential Strategy 2041 that fall within the 0.2% AEP flood extent or the updated coastal hazard lines; and 
    3. Outlining a process and timeline for amending/updating the relevant instruments, plans and strategies, including a community engagement process at IAP2 "Collaborate" level, recognising that decisions about where and how Byron Shire grows in a climate-changed environment are questions the community should help shape.

  3. Holds a joint workshop of the Floodplain Risk Management Advisory Committee, the Coastal Management and ICOLL Advisory Committee, and Councillors, to discuss and provide feedback on the report (prior to the report returning to Council).

  4. Notes that the report is intended to provide a framework for updating land use planning standards for climate resilience, so may also inform actions within the next review of Council's Climate Change Adaptation Plan and Strategy.

The motion was put to the vote and declared carried.
Cr Lowe, Cr Kay, Cr Hauge, Cr Ndiaye, Cr Warth voted in favour of the motion. 
Cr Lyon, Cr Dods, Cr Swain, Cr Doherty voted against the motion.

[IGNORE_INDENT][OUTLINE_NUMBER_FULL_NO_PERIOD][AGENDA_ITEM_NAME]
","reportContent":null,"minutesDiscussion":"
Moved: Cr Hauge Seconded: Cr Lowe
26-107 Resolved:
That Council:

  1. Notes the objective of the Bill is to provide for measures to prevent cats from:
    1. Escaping from the place where the cat is kept, or
    2. Leaving the place without being under the control of a person.

  2. Notes the Bill:
    1. Creates a clear duty for cat owners to keep their cats contained to their property,
    2. Empowers councils to make and enforce reasonable orders to prevent their cats from escaping,
    3. Protects vulnerable people through fair and compassionate enforcement, and
    4. Helps stop the flow of lost and abandoned pets into the feral cat population.

  3. Acknowledges effective domestic cat containment will:
    1. Protect native wildlife and local biodiversity by reducing injury and death from domestic roaming cat predation,
    2. Improve the wellbeing of domestic cats by reducing their risk of injury or death from vehicle strikes, dog attacks, ticks, poisoning, infections from cat fights and contracting diseases like feline aids virus
    3. Provide significant emotional and financial benefits to cat owners with their cats able to live longer, healthier lives along with the reduced risk of expensive vet bills and pet cats becoming lost.

  4. Write to all NSW State Ministers and MPs to:
    1. Express Council’s support for the Bill,
    2. Urge Ministers and MPs support the Bill, and
    3. Request State funding for councils to support education, compliance and animal shelter capacity.

The motion was put to the vote and declared carried.
Cr Lyon, Cr Lowe, Cr Kay, Cr Hauge, Cr Ndiaye, Cr Dods, Cr Warth, Cr Doherty voted in favour of the motion. 
Cr Swain voted against the motion.

    • Sustainable coastal services and values

  3. Approves the attendance of interested councillors, including Cr Elia Hauge, Cr Sarah Ndiaye, Cr Michelle Lowe, and Cr David Warth, at the conference (and invites any other interested councillors).

  5. Requests that attending councillors provide a report back to Council on key learnings and opportunities relevant to Council’s coastal management responsibilities.

The motion was put to the vote and declared carried.
Cr Lyon, Cr Lowe, Cr Kay, Cr Hauge, Cr Ndiaye, Cr Dods, Cr Swain, Cr Doherty voted in favour of the motion. 
None voted against the motion.
Cr Warth was not present for the vote.

[IGNORE_INDENT][OUTLINE_NUMBER_FULL_NO_PERIOD][AGENDA_ITEM_NAME]
","reportContent":null,"minutesDiscussion":"Cr Warth returned to the meeting at 6:57pm.

Moved: Cr Ndiaye Seconded: Cr Hauge
26-110 Resolved: 
That Council:

  1. Requests a report outlining potential alternative options available to Council to improve long-term financial sustainability, with a primary focus on options that do not involve the sale of public assets.

  2. Requests that the report include:
    1. An assessment of a range of revenue opportunities, including but not limited to:
      1. Expansion or introduction of paid parking in appropriate locations across the Shire;
      2. Review of fees and charges and cost recovery opportunities, including modelling of increases to pay parking fees and holiday park tourist rates, and a focus on fees and charges with the least impact on low-income community members
      3. Commercial opportunities, including at Tyagarah Airstrip, and other income-generating initiatives such as leasing, licensing or naming rights;
    2. Identification of Council-owned land and assets that may be underutilised, with:
      1. A focus on opportunities to enhance community use and generate revenue without overall divestment, for example by reinvesting funds in public assets such as housing.;
      2. An assessment of whether identified assets are strategic or non-strategic, and options to optimise their use for community benefit;
    3. Analysis of expenditure on external consultants
    4. Analysis of the opportunities, risks, benefits, and limitations associated with each option;
    5. High-level indicative valuations or potential revenue estimates where appropriate (excluding any presumption of sale);
    6. Consideration of the financial and community impacts of these options;
    7. Commentary on alignment with Council’s Community Strategic Plan and long-term objectives.

  3. Notes that:
    1. The exploration of asset-related options does not indicate a Council position to dispose of public assets, but rather seeks to ensure all options are transparently considered;
    2. Maintaining public assets in public ownership remains an important principle for Council and the community;
    3. A combination of measures will be required to address Council’s long-term financial sustainability challenges.

  4. Requests that the information be reported as it becomes available, to inform ongoing budget deliberations and community engagement, with a view to implementing a participatory budgeting process for the Long-Term Financial Plan.

The motion was put to the vote and declared carried.
Cr Lyon, Cr Lowe, Cr Kay, Cr Hauge, Cr Ndiaye, Cr Dods, Cr Warth, Cr Swain, Cr Doherty voted in favour of the motion. 
None voted against the motion.

","reportContent":null,"minutesDiscussion":"Council remained in Confidential Session for the following reasons:

  1. That pursuant to Section 10A(2)(g) of the Local Government Act 1993, Council resolves to move into Confidential Session to discuss the report CONFIDENTIAL - Land and Environment Court development appeal - DA 10.2024.230.1 for 1 Julian Place, Byron Bay.

  2. That the reason for closing the meeting to the public to consider this item is that the report contains advice concerning litigation, or advice that would otherwise be privileged from production in legal proceedings on the ground of legal professional privilege.

  3. That on the balance it is considered that receipt and discussion of the matter in open Council would be contrary to the public interest, as the report discusses a confidential and without prejudice conciliation process as part of ongoing Land and Environment Court proceedings.

Jisella Corradini-Bird of Marsdens Law Group briefed Council.

Moved: Cr Dods Seconded: Cr Hauge
26-146 Resolved: 
  1. That Council instructs Marsdens Law Group to do all things necessary for Council to enter a conciliation agreement resolving the Land and Environment Court development appeal initiated by Raes Residences Pty Ltd regarding DA 10.2024.230.1 (as amended by agreement).

  2. That the above instructions are subject to the outstanding matters detailed in the report, including groundwater and ecological impacts, being resolved to the satisfaction of Council's experts in the proceedings.

The motion was put to the vote and declared carried.
Cr Lyon, Cr Kay, Cr Hauge, Cr Ndiaye, Cr Dods, Cr Warth, Cr Swain, Cr Doherty voted in favour of the motion. 
Cr Lowe voted against the motion.


PROCEDURAL MOTION
Moved: Cr Ndiaye
26-155 Resolved that the meeting move out of Confidential Session.
The motion was put to the vote and declared carried.

The meeting adjourned at 4:16pm for a recess break and reconvened at 4:22pm.

Moved: Cr Lyon Seconded: Cr Ndiaye
26-181 Resolved: 
That Council:

  1. Acknowledges and thanks the Economic Activation Group members and participants for their input to Stage One engagement and Action Plan refinement.

  2. Notes the successful outcomes the Economic Activation Group’s Stage One and the process undertaken to refine the Action Plans which deliver the Byron Shire Economic Strategy 2025–2035.

  3. Places the updated Action Plans on public exhibition for 28 days, and reports submissions to council with finalised Action Plans for adoption, for the following Action Plans:
    1. Business and Industry (Attachment 1, E2026/52091)
    2. Destination Management and Visitor Economy (Attachment 2, E2026/52092)
    3. Events (Attachment 3, E2026/52093)

  4. Endorses the Draft Terms of Reference for Stage Two of the Economic Activation Group, for the Group’s confirmation at their first meeting (Attachment 4, E2026/56197).

  5. Invites up to three Councillors to nominate as members of the Economic Activation Group, with the Mayor or delegate to act as Chair in accordance with the Terms of Reference:
    1. Chair: Cr Ndiaye
    2. Councillor 2: Cr Swain
    3. Councillor 3: Cr Warth

The motion was put to the vote and declared carried.
Cr Lyon, Cr Kay, Cr Hauge, Cr Lowe, Cr Ndiaye, Cr Dods, Cr Warth, Cr Swain, Cr Doherty voted in favour of the motion. 
None voted against the motion.

26-166 Resolved: 
That Council rescinds parts 2-4 of Resolution 25-592:

Moved: Cr Hauge Seconded: Cr Swain
26-171 Resolved: 
That Council:

  1. Notes it has previously committed to fund Byron Youth Services up to $25,000 to deliver an alternative, mutually agreed youth safety program until June 2027.

  2. Endorses the alternative proposed Youth Safe Spaces Project (Attachment 1 - E2026/49416), to be operated by Byron Youth Services in 2026/27, subject to the adoption of the 2026/27 Council budget.

  3. Agrees to continue to fund Byron Youth Services for $25,000 (plus CPI) per annum, to deliver the Youth Safe Spaces Project for a further two years in 2027/28 and 2028/29, subject to compliance with its Funding Agreement and adoption of Council's respective annual budgets.

  4. Notes that triennial funding proposed in point 3, is standard across government grants and recognises the essential community value of recipients while reducing administrative burden for both funders and community organisations.

  5. Notes that subject to this report, and adoption of the 2026/27 budget, officers will negotiate a three-year Funding Agreement with Byron Youth Services from 1st July 2026 to 30 June 2029.

  6. Notes that the Youth Safe Spaces Project has been developed by Byron Youth Services Management in collaboration with Council officers and the Byron Youth Council, and that this program seeks to address relevant operational risk, Work Health and Safety, and legislative compliance, identified in the review of the former Street Cruise program.

The motion was put to the vote and declared carried.
Cr Lyon, Cr Kay, Cr Hauge, Cr Lowe, Cr Ndiaye, Cr Warth, Cr Swain, Cr Doherty voted in favour of the motion. 
None voted against the motion.
Cr Dods was not present for the vote.

26-172 Resolved:

  1. Notes the submissions received during the public exhibition period for the Operational Plan 2026-27 (including the Budget, Statement of Revenue Policy, and Fees and Charges) and Long-Term Financial Plan 2026-36 provided in Confidential Attachment 1 (E2026/62284) and outlined in the Community Engagement Report at Attachment 2 (E2026/61496).

  2. Adopts the following documents:
    1. 2026/27 Operational Plan at Attachment 3 (E2026/59686) with the amendments outlined in this Report under the heading 'Proposed amendments to the Operational Plan'
    2. 2026/27 Budget Estimates as exhibited, with the amendments discussed in the report under the heading 'Draft 2026/27 Budget Estimates (Statement of Revenue Policy)' and included at Attachment 4 (#E2026/60888)
    3. 2026/27 Statement of Revenue Policy including Fees and Charges as exhibited, with amendments included in Attachment 5 (#E2026/62486) discussed in the report under the headings 'Draft General Land Rates and Charges (Statement of Revenue Policy)' and Draft Fees and Charges (Statement of Revenue Policy)'
    4. 2026-2036 Long Term Financial Plan as exhibited, with the amendments discussed in the report under the heading 'Draft 2026-2036 Long Term Financial Plan and included at Attachment 6 (#E2026/62620)

  3. In accordance with Section 610(F) of the Local Government Act 1993, place the fees and charges on public exhibition for 28 days outlined under the heading 'Significant changes to fees and charges 2026/27, and
    1. If no submissions are received following public exhibition, Council adopts those fees and charges; or
    2. If submissions are received, they be reported to Council for determination of the fees and charges.

  4. Adopts the amendment to the 2026-2029 Delivery Program to include 'Work Health and Safety' as a Priority area. 

The motion was put to the vote and declared carried.
Cr Lyon, Cr Kay, Cr Hauge, Cr Lowe, Cr Ndiaye, Cr Dods, Cr Warth, Cr Swain, Cr Doherty voted in favour of the motion. 
None voted against the motion.

26-196 Resolved:
  1. That pursuant to Section 10A(2)(c) of the Local Government Act 1993, Council resolves to move into Confidential Session to discuss the report Proposed Road Closure and Sale - Part Lee Lane Road Reserve adjoining Lot 1 DP 246414, 134 Lighthouse Road, Byron Bay, NSW 2481.

  2. That the reason for closing the meeting to the public to consider this item be that the report contains:
    (c) information that would, if disclosed, confer a commercial advantage on a person with whom the council is conducting (or proposes to conduct) business

  3. That on the balance it is considered that receipt and discussion of the matter in open Council would be contrary to the public interest, to discuss the contents of the Confidential Attachments.

The motion was put to the vote and declared carried.

Moved: Cr Lowe Seconded: Cr Hauge
26-197 Resolved: 
That Council:

  1. Notes the completed pedestrian connectivity assessment, which identifies a viable option that relies on the part of Road Reserve in Lee Lane that is proposed for sale, and notes the absence of a secured funding source for any identified option. 

  2. Does not sell any part of the Road Reserve in Lee Lane adjoining 134 Lighthouse Road, Lot 1 DP246414, before the detailed design of a pathway connection between the end of the Arakwal National Park lighthouse trail on Lee Ln and the boardwalk at Bawii lookout/carpark is complete.

  3. Proceeds with lease negotiations under the Roads Act for the part of the Road Reserve in Lee Lane adjoining 134 Lighthouse Road, Lot 1 DP246414 
     
  4. Continues development of a standalone Encroachments Policy to provide a clear framework for Council evaluation and decision-making on encroachments

The motion was put to the vote and declared carried.
Cr Lyon, Cr Kay, Cr Hauge, Cr Lowe, Cr Ndiaye, Cr Dods, Cr Warth, Cr Swain, Cr Doherty voted in favour of the motion. 
None voted against the motion.

PROCEDURAL MOTION
Moved: Cr Ndiaye Seconded: Cr Dods
26-228 Resolved that the meeting move out of Confidential Session.
The motion was put to the vote and declared carried.

PROCEDURAL MOTION
Moved: Cr Hauge Seconded: Cr Ndiaye
26-229 Resolved that Report No. 13.30 rest on the table.
The motion was put to the vote and declared carried.

  2. That the reason for closing the meeting to the public to consider this item be that the report contains:

Moved: Cr Ndiaye Seconded: Cr Lyon
26-232 Resolved that the matter of ALGA motion regarding Disaster Recovery Funding Arrangements be discussed as a matter of urgency, the urgency being that the Australian Local Government Association (ALGA) National General Assembly is being held next week. For Council to submit an urgency motion for consideration at the Assembly, it must be resolved at today’s meeting.
The motion was put to the vote and declared carried.

The Mayor ruled it a matter of great urgency.

Moved: Cr Ndiaye Seconded: Cr Hauge
26-233 Resolved: 
That Council lodges an urgent motion to the ALGA National General Assembly calling on the Federal Government to:

  1. Abandon the proposed changes to the Disaster Recovery Funding Arrangements (DRFA) that would shift the Commonwealth/State funding split from 65/35 to 50/50; and

  2. Maintain existing Commonwealth funding proportions to ensure local councils are not further burdened in recovering from natural disasters.

The motion was put to the vote and declared carried.
Cr Lyon, Cr Kay, Cr Hauge, Cr Lowe, Cr Ndiaye, Cr Dods, Cr Warth, Cr Swain, Cr Doherty voted in favour of the motion. 
None voted against the motion.


There being no further business, the meeting concluded at 06:45 PM.



I hereby certify that these are the true and correct Minutes of this Meeting
as confirmed at Council’s Planning Meeting on 20 August 2026.
 
 

……………………………….
Mayor Sarah Ndiaye

Moved: Cr Warth Seconded: Cr Ndiaye
26-184 Resolved: 
That Council:

  1. Does not approve the proposed Traffic Signalised Crossing on Ewingsdale Road (MR545) at this time; and

  2. Writes to the applicant to state Council's support for deleting the condition of consent to provide a signalised or grade separated crossing or amending the condition to provide at grade median crossings at the proposed roundabout instead, should they accept to submit a Modification to the Consent.

  3. Failing point 2, requests a further staff report that addresses:
    1. A genuine feasibility assessment of grade separated crossing options, including a pedestrian underpass and overpass, with reference to TfNSW's "Pedestrian underpass design guideline" document, and consideration of design innovations that may address flooding, acid sulphate soil, and crime prevention concerns;
    2. A clear staging framework that identifies what development thresholds or milestones would trigger implementation of pedestrian crossing infrastructure, with a recommendation that any crossing be deferred to later stages of the development; and

  4. Receives a report on costing and delivery of a 'Ewingsdale Rd Corridor Masterplan' to guide future upgrades to this road including;
    1. Updating of Council's 2016 'Ewingsdale Rd Upgrade Works Concept Design' civil plans for a 4-lane road from the Cavanbah roundabout to Sunrise Blvd.
    2.  Landscaping, wayfinding, median designs, materiality, surface treatments, at grade crossing locations, etc to guide all future upgrades (council or developer led) 
    3. Engagement of Council's Place Planning team in the drafting of said Masterplan

  5. Notes that very few residents are currently living in the West Byron Urban Release Area and that master planning for the precinct should inform pedestrian and cyclist infrastructure decisions before commitments are made to TfNSW.

The motion was put to the vote and declared carried.
Cr Lyon, Cr Kay, Cr Hauge, Cr Lowe, Cr Ndiaye, Cr Dods, Cr Warth, Cr Swain, Cr Doherty voted in favour of the motion. 
None voted against the motion.

[IGNORE_INDENT][OUTLINE_NUMBER_FULL_NO_PERIOD][AGENDA_ITEM_NAME]
","reportContent":null,"minutesDiscussion":"
Moved: Cr Warth Seconded: Cr Hauge
26-200 Resolved: 
That Council:

  1. Notes:
    1. The latest Secure Yield Study prepared by HARC (E2026/55948) demonstrates that, even with climate change, 85% of the time there will be more than 2.0 ML/day flow over the Lavertys Gap weir compared to Mullumbimby’s daily demand of about 1.5 ML/day.
    2. That historically water from Lavertys Gap has cost far less per kL compared to Rous water
    3. That the Hydrosphere options comparison presented in the previous term of council assumed minimal environmental impact from relying on Rous to supply Mullumbimby despite Rous’ continued push to build the Dunoon Dam, used an outdated and superseded method of modelling climate impacts to water supply, and did not consider the resilience benefits of diverse water supplies, raising significant concerns regarding the outcome of their assessment

  2. Acknowledges the need for a “Strategic Planning Assessment” to consider options for the future of Mullumbimby’s water supply, given the matters outlined in Part 1 and the staff advice regarding Section 60 approvals.

  3. Requests a cost estimate for an options study/strategic planning assessment so that a hybrid concept (if supported by the options assessment) is ready to develop when funding streams are available, including the following options:
    1. A “time-based” hybrid system, where water from Lavertys Gap supplies both Left Bank Rd and Azalea St reservoirs (i.e. all of Mullumbimby except the industrial estate) most of the time, and is supplemented with water from Rous in times of very low flow (drought) and very high flow (turbid floodwaters), including
      1. modelling of the additional operational cost for water quality monitoring during the periods of Rous water usage
      2. an environmental flow allocation proxy, for example as the minimum required flow for fish passage over the weir
      3. a new water treatment plant at the existing site
    2. A “time-based” hybrid system with the same characteristics as described in Part 3a), with the variation of a potential boundary adjustment at the existing site to allow for a larger water treatment plant
    3. A geographical separation of supplies where Lavertys Gap supplies the Left Bank Road reservoir with an expanded supply zone, and Rous supplies the Azalea St reservoir (as shown in E2026/55949), including
      1. an environmental flow allocation proxy, for example as the minimum required flow for fish passage over the weir
      2. a new water treatment plant at the existing site
    4. Complete reliance on Rous for all of Mullumbimby, including a pumped system to supply the 13 rural properties between Lavertys Gap and the Left Bank Rd reservoir.

  4. Writes to the NSW Government requesting an urgent update on the timeline for policy review and grant programs for water planning and infrastructure in regional NSW.

PROCEDURAL MOTION
Moved: Cr Ndiaye Seconded: Cr Lowe
26-215 Resolved That Cr Hauge be granted a two minute extension to their speech.
The motion was put to the vote and declared carried.
Cr Swain and Cr Doherty voted against the motion.

The motion (26-200) was put to the vote and declared carried.
Cr Kay, Cr Hauge, Cr Lowe, Cr Ndiaye, Cr Warth voted in favour of the motion. 
Cr Lyon, Cr Dods, Cr Swain, Cr Doherty voted against the motion.

Moved: Cr Hauge Seconded: Cr Ndiaye
26-177 Resolved: 
That Council:

  1. Notes that at the May meeting, Council requested substantial further information to inform discussion of all options for financial sustainability, and that this information should also inform community engagement on financial sustainability in comparison to the SRV option.

  2. Endorses the Community Engagement Plan for 'Financial Sustainability and Potential Special Rate Variation' as attached.

  3. Requests that the engagement also asks community opinion on options that redistribute the total rates collected to lessen the burden on low value properties. 

  4. Requests an update at the August Councillor workshop on the detailed engagement approaches (including draft materials and detailed timelines)

  5. Approves the implementation of the Plan to undertake community engagement in accordance with IPART requirements.

  6. Notes that the outcomes of the engagement process will be reported back to Council prior to any formal decision to apply for a Special Rate Variation.

  7. Allocates $120,000 in the 2026/27 Budget for the purposes of undertaking the Community Engagement Plan funded from the Risk Management Reserve.

PROCEDURAL MOTION
Moved: Cr Ndiaye Seconded: Cr Lowe
26-176 Resolved that Cr Hauge be granted a two minute extension to their speech.

Moved: Cr Ndiaye Seconded: Cr Hauge
26-141 Resolved: 
That Council:

  1. Notes the significant economic, cultural and community importance of the Easter period to Byron Shire, including its role in supporting local businesses, tourism operators, accommodation providers, venues, artists, markets, hospitality, transport providers and the broader visitor economy.

  2. Acknowledges that Easter 2027 will require additional coordination with the absence of Bluesfest, including liaison with industry, coordination of Council support services, visitor information, digital promotion, traffic and transport planning, waste servicing and open space cleaning.

  3. Allocates $100,000 from pay parking revenue to resource the coordination of Easter 2027 planning and delivery.

  4. Seeks grant funding to support Easter 2027 transport and additional activation.

  5. Establishes an internal working group to progress Easter 2027 planning.

  6. Receives a report following Easter 2027 outlining activities supported, coordination undertaken, costs incurred, lessons learned, and recommendations for future Easter planning and funding.

The motion was put to the vote and declared carried.
Cr Hauge, Cr Lowe, Cr Ndiaye, Cr Warth, Cr Doherty voted in favour of the motion. 
Cr Lyon, Cr Kay, Cr Dods, Cr Swain voted against the motion.

Moved: Cr Ndiaye Seconded: Cr Hauge
26-145 Resolved: 
That Council:

  1. Notes Resolution 25-626, which resolved to commence development of a Memorandum of Understanding (MoU) between Byron Shire Council and Homes NSW to establish a framework for collaboration on housing outcomes across the Byron Shire Local Government Area;

  2. Notes that the purpose of the MoU is to support the expedited delivery of new social and affordable housing, including renewed and accessible housing, while maintaining strong community outcomes;

  3. Acknowledges the severity of the housing and homelessness crisis in Byron Shire, including the 245 people recorded sleeping rough in the 2026 NSW Street Count, representing the second-highest figure in New South Wales;

  4. Recognises the work already underway across a range of sites and initiatives, including the former Mullumbimby Hospital site feasibility study, the 57 Station Street affordable housing project, key worker accommodation proposals at Byron CoLab, the retention of the Brunswick Bayside pods as well as the work done through the policy and planning framework with the Affordable Housing Contribution Scheme and the Council Led Lands Trust;

  5. Endorses community engagement as a central principle of all housing delivery under this framework, and commits to keeping the Byron Shire community informed and involved as partnership projects develop;

  6. Receives and notes the attached copy of the Memorandum of Understanding between Byron Shire Council and Homes NSW, which will be executed by the General Manager and the Homes NSW CEO.

The motion was put to the vote and declared carried.
Cr Lyon, Cr Kay, Cr Hauge, Cr Lowe, Cr Ndiaye, Cr Dods, Cr Warth, Cr Swain, Cr Doherty voted in favour of the motion. 
None voted against the motion.

Moved: Cr Dods Seconded: Cr Swain
26-162 Resolved: 
That Council:

  1. Commits to maintaining public access across the Helen Street footbridge through repair or replacement works as required.

  2. Prioritises keeping the bridge safely open and minimising any full closure period, including investigation of temporary or staged works where practicable.

  3. Prioritises timely delivery of the necessary works, ensuring assessment, design and procurement processes focus on maintaining this critical community connection with minimal disruption.

  4. Investigates repair, refurbishment and replacement options including:
     a. staged deck replacement works;
     b. alternative handrail systems that improve future maintenance access and reduce the need for prolonged closures; and
     c. prefabricated or modular replacement options capable of rapid installation.

  5. Receive a report outlining options, associated costs, delivery timeframes, and opportunities to reprioritise existing works programs or secure external funding to expedite delivery.

The motion was put to the vote and declared carried.
Cr Lyon, Cr Kay, Cr Hauge, Cr Lowe, Cr Ndiaye, Cr Dods, Cr Warth, Cr Swain, Cr Doherty voted in favour of the motion. 
None voted against the motion.

[IGNORE_INDENT][OUTLINE_NUMBER_FULL_NO_PERIOD][AGENDA_ITEM_NAME]
","reportContent":null,"minutesDiscussion":"
Moved: Cr Hauge Seconded: Cr Lowe
26-163 Resolved: 
That Council:

  1. Notes that the former Mullumbimby Hospital site represents one of the most significant public land decisions in the Shire's recent history, and that the community has a long-standing and legitimate interest in the outcome of negotiations regarding the site.

  2. Notes that existing statutory consultation processes, while necessary, are not sufficient to ensure meaningful community involvement in evaluating proposals regarding the site's development.

  3. Notes that the Memorandum of Understanding (MoU) between HomesNSW and Council identifies the old Mullumbimby Hospital site as a priority project, and the next stages of this project will require more detailed proposals for how HomesNSW will deliver the vision for the site, including defining project objectives under a "Project Charter".

  4. Requests that the “Project Charter” and objectives be reported to Council for adoption

  5. Establishes a site-specific Design Excellence Panel to provide advice on the built form, with panel terms and membership to return to Council for adoption

  6. Receives a report, as soon as practicable after the next meeting with HomesNSW, on options for the evaluation process of the feasibility study for the site, including:
    1. an option for community representatives to work alongside Councillors and staff to review and evaluate any proposal
    2. a standalone Community Assessment Panel - constituted under similar terms to an Advisory Committee - to provide structured community input into Council's evaluation
    3. discussion of the each option’s membership, considering representation from the Mullumbimby Hospital Action Group, housing and homelessness advocates, and residents representative of the demographic diversity of the Shire
    4. cost estimates and budget considerations for the engagement

  7. Notes that these engagement mechanisms should be established and ready to convene upon receipt of any detailed proposal from HomesNSW to avoid unnecessary project delays.


PROCEDURAL MOTION
Moved: Cr Ndiaye Seconded: Cr Lowe
26-198 Resolved that Cr Hauge be granted a two minute extension to their speech.
The motion was put to the vote and declared carried.

The motion (26-163) was put to the vote and declared carried.
Cr Kay, Cr Hauge, Cr Lowe, Cr Ndiaye, Cr Warth voted in favour of the motion. 
Cr Lyon, Cr Dods, Cr Swain, Cr Doherty voted against the motion.

[IGNORE_INDENT][OUTLINE_NUMBER_FULL_NO_PERIOD][AGENDA_ITEM_NAME]
","reportContent":null,"minutesDiscussion":"
Moved: Cr Ndiaye Seconded: Cr Dods
26-164 Resolved: 
That Council receives a report on the:

  1. Outcome of the Regional Precincts and Partnerships Program application for rail trail funding, including:
    1. formal feedback received from the Australian Government administering agency
    2. key strengths and weaknesses of the application, and 
    3. recommendations to improve future rail trail funding applications for Byron Shire.
  1. Exploration of alternative funding and delivery models that may support rail trail delivery within Byron Shire, including philanthropic contributions, charitable sponsorship frameworks, lotteries, “sponsor a section” models, public-private partnerships, tourism partnerships and other innovative funding mechanisms.

  2. Grant funding opportunities that may support future delivery of rail trail sections in Byron Shire.

  3. Progress update of rail trail planning and delivery for rail trail sections within Byron Shire, including current constraints, approvals, TfNSW coordination requirements and indicative delivery sequencing.

  4. Development of a publicly available Rail Trail Masterplan for Byron Shire, similar to work undertaken by Richmond Valley Council, including high-level concept plans, interface treatments and urban design outcomes for key locations including:
    1. Mullumbimby;
    2. Billinudgel;
    3. Ocean Shores West;
    4. Byron Bay CBD South;
    5. Tyagarah / M1 interface;
    6. Cemetery Road / Roadhouse precinct; and
    7. Bangalow town centre.

  1. Opportunities to divide the Byron Shire rail trail into smaller, more deliverable and fundable stages, including but not limited to:
    1. Crabbes Creek – Billinudgel;
    2. Billinudgel – Ocean Shores West;
    3. Ocean Shores West – Mullumbimby;
    4. Mullumbimby – Byron Bay;
    5. Byron Bay – Cemetery Road;
    6. Cemetery Road – Bangalow East (A&I Hall);
    7. Bangalow Central (A&I Hall – Raftons Road) – Dudgeons Lane; and
    8. Dudgeons Lane – Booyong.

  2. Prioritisation of future rail trail sections, including consideration of:
    1. community benefit;
    2. active transport outcomes;
    3. tourism and economic activation;
    4. engineering complexity and cost;
    5. deliverability and funding readiness;
    6. connections to existing walking and cycling infrastructure; and
    7. opportunities for early delivery of high-impact sections.

PROCEDURAL MOTION
Moved: Cr Ndiaye Seconded: Cr Lowe
26-217 Resolved that Cr Dods be granted a two minute extension to their speech.
The motion was put to the vote and declared carried.

PROCEDURAL MOTION
Moved: Cr Ndiaye Seconded: Cr Hauge
26-218 Resolved that Cr Ndiaye be granted a two minute extension to their speech.
The motion was put to the vote and declared carried.

The motion (26-164) was put to the vote and declared carried.
Cr Lyon, Cr Kay, Cr Hauge, Cr Ndiaye, Cr Dods, Cr Swain, Cr Doherty voted in favour of the motion. 
Cr Lowe, Cr Warth voted against the motion.

  3. Progress update of rail trail planning and delivery for rail trail sections within Byron Shire, including current constraints, approvals, TfNSW coordination requirements and indicative delivery sequencing.

  4. Development of a publicly available Rail Trail Masterplan for Byron Shire, similar to work undertaken by Richmond Valley Council, including high-level concept plans, interface treatments and urban design outcomes for key locations including:
    1. Mullumbimby;
    2. Billinudgel;
    3. Ocean Shores West;
    4. Byron Bay CBD South;
    5. Tyagarah / M1 interface;
    6. Cemetery Road / Roadhouse precinct; and
    7. Bangalow town centre.

  1. Opportunities to divide the Byron Shire rail trail into smaller, more deliverable and fundable stages, including but not limited to:
    1. Crabbes Creek – Billinudgel;
    2. Billinudgel – Ocean Shores West;
    3. Ocean Shores West – Mullumbimby;
    4. Mullumbimby – Byron Bay;
    5. Byron Bay – Cemetery Road;
    6. Cemetery Road – Bangalow East (A&I Hall);
    7. Bangalow Central (A&I Hall – Raftons Road) – Dudgeons Lane; and
    8. Dudgeons Lane – Booyong.

  2. Prioritisation of future rail trail sections, including consideration of:
    1. community benefit;
    2. active transport outcomes;
    3. tourism and economic activation;
    4. engineering complexity and cost;
    5. deliverability and funding readiness;
    6. connections to existing walking and cycling infrastructure; and
    7. opportunities for early delivery of high-impact sections.

Questions

Question No. 1 57 Station Street
Peter Brennan on behalf of the Mullumbimby Residents Association asked the following question:
"In Council’s view, has the applicant adequately dealt with the issues raised in the 2025 Requests for Further Information? If not, has Council written to the applicant or will Council write to the applicant asking them to further amend the DA to address these matters prior to its submission to the NRPP?"
The Mayor took the question on notice.


Question No. 2 Baywood Chase Lake – Operational Plan
Kelly Minahan on behalf of the Suffolk Park Community Association asked the following question:
"Given that Baywood Chase Lake drains to the Tallow Creek ICOLL, on what basis has staff determined that management work concerning these coastal-connected stormwater assets falls outside the scope of Operational Plan Activity 3.3.1.4?"

The Mayor took the question on notice.


Question No. 3 Selection of 57 Station Street for Housing Project
Anando Hefley asked the following question:
"We now know 57 Station Street is in fact the least suitable regarding zoning (it is restricted by a shop-top limitation) and size (it is less than half the size of Council carpark, or the State land north of Woollies which was earmarked for affordable housing by Council in 2022). Does Council still consider 57 Station Street the best choice — and if so, on what basis?"

The Mayor took the question on notice.


Question No. 4 57 Station Street DA
Paul Cholakos asked the following question:
" What is the total number of submissions Council received on the amended DA, how many of those were objections to the proposal and how does Council intend to deal with the proposal’s lack of social licence evidenced by the community’s overwhelming rejection of the proposal?"

The Mayor took the question on notice.
