Moved: Cr Ndiaye Seconded: Cr Warth
26-286 Resolved Change the order of business to deal with Reports 16.3, 16.1 and 16.2 next on the Agenda.
The motion was put to the vote and declared carried.

Moved: Cr Ndiaye Seconded: Cr Warth
26-287 Resolved: 
  1. That pursuant to Section 10A(2)(c), (d) and (d)&(g), respectively, of the Local Government Act 1993, Council resolves to move into Confidential Session to discuss the following reports:
    1.  CONFIDENTIAL - Land Valuation and Funding Source for Lot 97 DP238450, 32 Coomburra Crescent, Ocean Shores;
    2. CONFIDENTIAL - 2026-5381 Left Bank Road Bridge Tender Award; and
    3. CONFIDENTIAL - Voluntary Planning Agreement to support Gulgan Village rezoning

  2. That the reason for closing the meeting to the public to consider this item be that the report contains, respectively:
    1.  information that would, if disclosed, confer a commercial advantage or disadvantage on a person with whom the council is conducting (or proposes to conduct) business.
    2. prejudice the commercial position of the person who supplied it, or confer a commercial advantage on a competitor of the council, or reveal a trade secret,
    3. commercial information of a confidential nature that would, if disclosed: i) prejudice the commercial position of the person who supplied it, or ii) confer a commercial advantage on a competitor of the council, or iii) reveal a trade secret, or   advice concerning litigation, or advice that would otherwise be privileged from production in legal proceedings on the ground of legal professional privilege.

  3. That on the balance it is considered that receipt and discussion of the matter in open Council would be contrary to the public interest, respectively, as it:
    1. involves commercially sensitive land valuations and potential acquisition for flood risk management purposes.
    2. contains commercial information of a confidential nature that would, if disclosed may prejudice the commercial position of the person who supplied it, or confer a commercial advantage on a competitor of the council.
    3. the terms of the Planning Agreement contains information that would be privileged, and of a commercial nature.


The motion was put to the vote and declared carried.
Cr Lyon, Cr Kay, Cr Hauge, Cr Lowe, Cr Ndiaye, Cr Dods, Cr Warth, Cr Swain voted in favour of the motion. 
None voted against the motion.

Moved: Cr Lowe Seconded: Cr Swain
26-249 Resolved: 
That Council:
  1. Approves the recommended projects for the 2026/27 Community Initiatives Program as per Confidential Attachment 1 (E2026/77082);

  2. Subject to this report, authorises officers to negotiate a Funding Agreement with the successful applicants for 2026/27;

  3. Notes that projects not recommended for funding will be offered the opportunity to receive feedback about their application;

  4. Notes that, as part of Council’s annual review process, some improvements are recommended and will be proposed for the 2027/28 Community Initiatives Program, including a stronger alignment with the updated Financial Assistance Section 356 Policy (subject to approval), incentivising more timely returns of grant acquittals, and providing further clarification regarding organisational 'not for profit' eligibility;

  5. Approves an additional out of round $5,000 'one off' funding contribution to Red Frogs Inc from the 'safety projects' budget line, to support their medic services at the 2026 Schoolies event; and

  6. Notes that any future funding applications from Red Frogs will only be accepted via the advertised Community Initiatives Program.
The motion was put to the vote and declared carried.
Cr Lyon, Cr Kay, Cr Hauge, Cr Lowe, Cr Ndiaye, Cr Dods, Cr Warth, Cr Swain voted in favour of the motion. 
None voted against the motion.

Moved: Cr Ndiaye 
26-263 Resolved That Report No. 13.16 be lifted from the table.

Cr Kay left the meeting at 2:09pm in accordance with her Declaration of Interest.


PROCEDURAL MOTIONS
Moved: Cr Ndiaye Seconded: Cr Warth
26-264 Resolved That Cr Dods be granted a two minute extension to his speech.
The motion was put to the vote and declared carried.

Moved: Cr Dods Seconded: Cr Lowe
26-265 Resolved That Cr Ndiaye be granted a two minute extension to her speech.
The motion was put to the vote and declared carried.


Moved: Cr Dods Seconded: Cr Lyon
26-266 Resolved: 
That Council:
  1. Agrees to provide in-principle support to the terms in the Letter of Offer to enter into a Planning Agreement (PA) for the Jonson Street Road Reserve Extension associated with State Significant Development SSD-106851722, Attachment 2 (#E2026/84944), subject to the staff amendments shown in Table 1 of the report;

  2. Requests the developer to prepare a draft Planning Agreement (PA) on the basis of the Council resolution and resubmit this to staff, and process the Planning Agreement in accordance with the Environmental Planning and Assessment Act 1979;

  3. The staff are delegated to settle a draft PA for exhibition and report back to Council post exhibition of the draft PA;

  4. Notes that staff will prepare a submission to the SSD application once it is placed on exhibition and notification is received from the NSW Government;

  5. Requests that the final street design plans be reported back to Council along with the draft Planning Agreement for endorsement post exhibition; and

  6. Council provide landowner’s consent to lodgement of the SSD application so far as it relates to Council’s land and the works contemplated in the Letter of Offer.
The motion was put to the vote and declared carried.
Cr Lyon, Cr Hauge, Cr Ndiaye, Cr Dods, Cr Warth, Cr Swain voted in favour of the motion. 
Cr Lowe voted against the motion.

Moved: Cr Ndiaye Seconded: Cr Hauge
26-271 Resolved That Cr Lowe be granted a two minute extension to her speech.
The motion was put to the vote and declared carried.


Moved: Cr Lowe Seconded: Cr Hauge
26-272 Resolved: 
That Council:
  1. Notes the status report on Development Applications with bodies such as the Northern Regional Planning Panel (NRPP);

  2. Notes with concern the increasing number of major development proposals in Byron Shire progressing through the Housing Delivery Authority (HDA) and State Significant Development (SSD) pathways, including 70 units at 11 Butler Street and 160 units at 148–158 Jonson Street, Byron Bay;

  3. Notes with concern that the State Government is in the process of removing the Local Government planning determination role of Councillors; and

  4. Requests a report to Council outlining the implications of the HDA and SSD pathways for Byron Shire, including impacts on local planning and environmental controls, affordable housing outcomes, community engagement and options for Council to formally respond or seek an exemption.
The motion was put to the vote and declared carried.
Cr Lyon, Cr Kay, Cr Hauge, Cr Lowe, Cr Ndiaye, Cr Dods, Cr Warth, Cr Swain voted in favour of the motion. 
None voted against the motion.

That Council:
  1. Notes the progress of Voluntary Planning Agreement negotiations to date in relation to the Gulgan Village Planning Proposal, including the most recent legal advice dated 17 August 2026 and provided in Attachment 2 (E2026/93121);

  2. Notes that staff and the proponent have since had further discussions regarding the key outstanding issues and reached agreement on an amended Voluntary Planning Agreement (VPA), as provided in Attachment 8 (E2026/95271);

  3. Requests that the proponent provide an updated irrevocable letter of offer prior to placing the amended VPA on public exhibition, scheduled for Monday, 24 August 2026;

  4. Endorses the amended Voluntary Planning Agreement (Attachment 8 - E2026/95271) for public exhibition, subject to receipt of the updated irrevocable letter of offer from the proponent.  If the updated irrevocable letter of offer is not received by Monday, 24 August 2026, Council will not proceed to place the amended VPA on public exhibition and will consider alternative actions at a subsequent meeting; and

  5. Notes the time-sensitive nature of the Gulgan Village Planning Proposal, which must be finalised by Tuesday, 27 October 2026 in accordance with the current Gateway determination.
The motion was put to the vote and declared carried.
Cr Lyon, Cr Kay, Cr Hauge, Cr Lowe, Cr Ndiaye, Cr Dods, Cr Warth, Cr Swain voted in favour of the motion. 
None voted against the motion.

[IGNORE_INDENT][OUTLINE_NUMBER_FULL_NO_PERIOD][AGENDA_ITEM_NAME]
","reportContent":null,"minutesDiscussion":"
Moved: Cr Ndiaye Seconded: Cr Lowe
26-238 Resolved: 
I move that Council:
  1. Welcomes the Federal Government’s recent announcement recognising the very real challenge of financial sustainability impacting the Local Government sector and committing to a meaningful, ongoing annual increase in the level of Financial Assistance Grants;

  2. Welcomes the announcement of the Federation Compact with Local Government that commits to:
    1. Ongoing annual increases to Financial Assistance Grants to return them to historic levels;
    2. Ensure Roads to Recovery funding can be used to purchase plant and equipment to enable councils to carry out their own road maintenance with their own trained workers, to the extent possible;
    3. Support and increase the availability of apprenticeships in Local Government, as well as other employment programs in a local government context;
    4. Deliver new capabilities to improve outcomes in housing, planning, emergency management and aged care; and
    5. Ensure the Government publishes an annual summary of funding for Local Government.

  3. Writes to the Prime Minister and Local Government Minister Catherine King welcoming their commitment to address the crisis in Local Government financial sustainability and urging them to work with the Local Government sector to urgently progress the Federation Compact with Local Government. 
The motion was put to the vote and declared carried.
Cr Lyon, Cr Kay, Cr Hauge, Cr Lowe, Cr Ndiaye, Cr Dods, Cr Warth, Cr Swain voted in favour of the motion. 
None voted against the motion.

26-239 Resolved That Cr Hauge be granted a two minutes extension to her speech.
The motion was put to the vote and declared carried.


Moved: Cr Hauge Seconded: Cr Kay
26-240 Resolved: 
I move that Council:

  1. Notes the ongoing poor water quality in Baywood Chase Lake, which flows to the Tallow Creek ICOLL in Arakwal National Park;

  2. Notes that Council’s own CMP Stage 2 Study: Byron Shire ICOLL Water pollution Source Tracking and Control Programs for Belongil Creek, Tallow Creek and Ti-Tree Lake Study by Hydrosphere Consulting 2023 ranks this lake the number one pollution source into Tallow Creek estuary, and that eight years on since a Management Plan for the Lake was first drafted for Council by Australian Wetlands Consulting in 2018, no action has been undertaken by Council to improve the health of the Lake;

  3. Notes that the Tallow Creek CMP has fallen significantly behind its original planned timeline, and that as the Open Coast CMP and Belongil Estuary CMP are of a higher priority than the Tallow Creek CMP, it is unlikely to be completed or adopted in the next 12 months;

  4. Receives a scoping report by the December 2026 Ordinary meeting on early-win interventions such as aeration, including consideration of a solar aeration pilot, to improve water quality in Baywood Chase Lake that can be implemented prior to the adoption of a Tallow Creek CMP that would achieve benefits to overall estuary health, and that the report also consider cost, funding pathways and grant options;

  5. Requests that the draft Baywood Chase Lake Management Plan (2018/2024) be reported to Council's September 2026 meeting (for information if adoption is not appropriate); and

  6. Supports a community planting day for the tributaries that feed Baywood Chase Lake, and facilitates a meeting between relevant Council staff, representatives of the Suffolk Park Community Association's Environmental Working Group, the local Landcare group, and the Byron Coast and ICOLL Centre, to discuss a collaboration for this potential event (with a funding request to come to the next Council meeting if such an event can't be covered through Council's existing environmental education, bush regeneration or stormwater/open spaces maintenance programs).
The motion was put to the vote and declared carried.
Cr Lyon, Cr Kay, Cr Hauge, Cr Lowe, Cr Ndiaye, Cr Dods, Cr Warth, Cr Swain voted in favour of the motion. 
None voted against the motion.

Moved: Cr Ndiaye Seconded: None
26-241 Resolved: 
I move that Council:
  1. Writes to the Hon. Anthony Albanese MP, Prime Minister of Australia; the Hon. Chris Minns MP, Premier of New South Wales; the Hon. Janelle Saffin MP, Minister for Recovery and the North Coast; and relevant Federal and State Members, expressing Byron Shire Council’s serious concerns regarding large-scale flood detention basins identified through Phase Two of the Northern Rivers Resilience Initiative, noting that these structures are dams. They trap water behind massive concrete walls and operate as dams in flood conditions;

  2. Calls on the Commonwealth and NSW Governments to investigate nature-based flood mitigation measures and other scientifically supported alternatives instead of large-scale detention dams, not alongside them, using the current $3 million in study funding;

  3. States Council’s opposition to any further progression of large-scale detention dam proposals unless and until:
    1. full public disclosure of proposed locations and potential land acquisition requirements has occurred;
    2. comprehensive, genuine consultation with potentially affected landholders, local communities and councils has taken place;
    3. transparent assessment of economic, environmental, social, cultural, agricultural and infrastructure impacts has been completed;
    4. impacts on roads, bridges, farming enterprises, biodiversity and native habitat have been assessed;
    5. anticipated construction and ongoing maintenance costs have been disclosed;
    6. the organisations responsible for ongoing operation and maintenance have been identified; and
    7. funding arrangements, compensation mechanisms and project timeframes have been made public.

  4. Calls for future regional flood mitigation investigations to rule out, as a starting principle, the permanent loss or significant impairment of productive agricultural land, rural communities, environmental values, cultural heritage and critical local infrastructure;

  5. States that Council does not support large-scale detention dam infrastructure proceeding to construction, and that this position stands unless a full, transparent, community-led assessment demonstrates a case that genuinely outweighs the impacts to affected land, communities and environment;

  6. Seeks assurance that flood mitigation works already identified as priorities in other Northern Rivers communities will urgently proceed, including Byron Shire’s Jonson Street flood protection works and other necessary upgrades, accompanied by extended funding for the Northern Rivers Watershed Initiative;

  7. Notes with concern that the Brunswick River catchment was excluded from the scope of the Northern Rivers Resilience Initiative, despite Byron Shire’s own experience of flooding and landslip damage;

  8. Notes that flood resilience across the Northern Rivers requires a genuinely regional approach, and that measures designed to protect one community must not create unreasonable environmental, social or economic impacts for another; and

  9. Reaffirms Byron Shire Council’s support for evidence-based regional flood mitigation, meaningful community consultation and transparent assessment of all reasonable options, and places on record its concern that nature-based solutions have been excluded from this study. 
The motion was put to the vote and declared carried.
Cr Lyon, Cr Kay, Cr Hauge, Cr Lowe, Cr Ndiaye, Cr Dods, Cr Warth, Cr Swain voted in favour of the motion. 
None voted against the motion.

Moved: Cr Lyon Seconded: Cr Swain
26-289 Resolved: 
I move that council: 
  1. Acknowledges the Gateway Determination report by the NSW Department of Planning and Infrastructure of Council’s previous application for heritage listing;

  2. Recognises that the unique role as a social and cultural hub played by the Bangalow Bowlo was not sufficiently addressed in the previous Heritage Report;

  3. Notes the essential historical role that the Bowlo has played as a regional and national centre for live music, including the evidence outlined in “Musicland” by Tricia Shantz, that includes helping launch the careers of Michael Hutchence, Peter Garrett, Cold Chisel and others;

  4. Notes the unique role that the Bangalow Bowlo has as a ‘third place’ in bringing together multiple generations under one roof for live music, sports, family celebrations, community mourning and traditional bowling. This is a unique aspect of the Bangalow Bowlo compared to other clubs in the Shire;

  5. Notes the introduction of the “Tifdwarf” grass variety in the 70s that revolutionised bowling greens in the sub-tropics;

  6. Notes that the Bowlo has in the past fallen outside the scope of the Heritage area in Bangalow township and will ensure that heritage listing of the Bowlo be included in future heritage plans for Bangalow; and

  7. Resubmits a heritage listing planning proposal to ensure the Bowlo retains is historical role as a social centre and essential hub of live music.
The motion was put to the vote and declared carried.
Cr Lyon, Cr Kay, Cr Hauge, Cr Lowe, Cr Ndiaye, Cr Dods, Cr Warth, Cr Swain voted in favour of the motion. 
None voted against the motion.


There being no further business, the meeting concluded at 4:11pm.

 

I hereby certify that these are the true and correct Minutes of this Meeting

as confirmed at Council’s Ordinary Meeting on 17 September 2026.

 
  

​

……………………………….

Mayor Sarah Ndiaye

Moved: Cr Lyon Seconded: Cr Ndiaye
26-308 Resolved: 
That Council:
  1. Notes the submissions received during exhibition of the Gulgan Village Planning Proposal and Development Control Plan (DCP);

  2. Amends the exhibited Planning Proposal in Attachment 1 (E2026/60591) to: 
    1. reduce the extent of the R1 zone as outlined in this report.

  3. Adopts the Gulgan Village Development Control Plan – post-exhibition with the proposed changes identified in this report and incorporated in Attachment 9 (E2026/103261);

  4. Notes the binding letter of offer (Attachment 12) to enter into the amended Voluntary Planning Agreement (Attachment 13) attached to this report and that the exhibited Voluntary Planning Agreement (VPA) remains on public exhibition until 21 September 2026;

  5. Conditionally endorses the exhibited Voluntary Planning Agreement and accompanying Letter of Offer, subject to: 
    1. consideration of any submissions received during the exhibition period; and 
    2. no material issues being raised that, in the opinion of the General Manager, warrant further consideration by Council;

  6. Delegates authority to the General Manager to finalise and execute the Voluntary Planning Agreement on behalf of Council;

  7. Should material issues be raised through the exhibition of the Voluntary Planning Agreement, receives a further report on those matters prior to execution of the Agreement; and

  8. Following satisfaction of item 5 and execution of the Voluntary Planning Agreement by both parties, forwards the amended Planning Proposal to the NSW Department of Planning, Housing and Infrastructure (DPHI) requesting finalisation.
The motion was put to the vote and declared carried.
Cr Lyon, Cr Kay, Cr Hauge, Cr Lowe, Cr Ndiaye, Cr Dods, Cr Warth, Cr Swain voted in favour of the motion. 
None voted against the motion.

It is recommended, pursuant to Section 4.55 of the Environmental Planning and Assessment Act 1979, that Application No. 10.2024.14.2 to modify building envelopes and subdivision layout, and remove electricity grid connection requirement within an approve 15-lot community title subdivision, be approved by modifying Development Consent 10.2024.14.1 in accordance with the conditions contained in Attachment 2 (E2026/98793) and the following amendment to Condition 46(a):

46. Section 88B Instrument
A Section 88B Instrument and one (1) copy are to be submitted with the application for a subdivision certificate. The final plan of subdivision and accompanying Section 88B Instrument are to provide for:
  1. Building Envelopes
    Restrictions are to be imposed limiting the erection of dwellings and the installation of on-site sewage management systems to the nominated building envelope on each lot, unless otherwise approved by Council. The building envelopes are to be generally in accordance with the 2100 Flood Planning Level Draft Building Envelope Plan, by Balanced Systems, dated August 2026.
The motion was put to the vote and declared carried.
Cr Lyon, Cr Kay, Cr Hauge, Cr Lowe, Cr Ndiaye, Cr Dods, Cr Warth, Cr Swain voted in favour of the motion. 
None voted against the motion.

It is recommended, pursuant to Section 4.55 of the Environmental Planning and Assessment Act 1979, that Application No. 10.2024.14.2 to modify conditions 1, 14 and 58 in relation to design of administration building, road upgrades, and hours of operation, be approved by modifying Development Consent 10.2024.305.2 in accordance with the conditions in Attachment 2 (E2026/98079) and Condition 58 being amended to read as follows:


58. Operating Hours

Activities at the premises may only be undertaken at the times specified in the table below. Activities may be undertaken outside of the specified times during emergency situations (e.g. flood).

  

Activity

Permitted Hours 

Heavy livestock vehicle access and egress

Monday to Friday 7 am to 4 pm.

Sundays 10 am to 3 pm. 

Refrigerated heavy vehicle

Monday to Saturday: 7 am to 9 pm, Sundays: Nil.

Other vehicle access

7 days a week, 24 hours a day

Holding of pigs in pens

Monday to Friday: 24 hours a day.

Saturday: 12 am to 5 pm.

Sunday: 10 am to midnight.

Slaughtering of pigs

Monday to Friday: 5:30 am to 6 pm. Saturday: 5:30 am to 3:30 pm.

Use of mobile plant within premise boundary

Monday to Saturday: 5:30 am to 6 pm.

Non-slaughter activities that are inaudible at adjacent and nearby residences

7 days a week, 24 hours a day

Mechanical and electrical services

7 days a week, 24 hours a day

Construction or building works

Monday to Friday: 7 am to 6 pm.

Saturday: 8 am to 1 pm


The motion was put to the vote and declared carried.
Cr Lyon, Cr Kay, Cr Hauge, Cr Lowe, Cr Ndiaye, Cr Dods, Cr Warth, Cr Swain voted in favour of the motion. 
None voted against the motion.

Moved: Cr Ndiaye Seconded: Cr Lowe
26-350 Resolved That Cr Dods be granted a two minute extension to his speech.
The motion was put to the vote and declared carried.


Moved: Cr Dods Seconded: Cr Ndiaye
26-335 Resolved: 
That, pursuant to Section 4.16 of the Environmental Planning and Assessment Act 1979, Development Application No.10.2025.601.1 for a Demolition of an existing multi-dwelling residential development and construction of a new dual occupancy be granted consent subject to the conditions of approval in Attachment 2 (E2026/95784) and the following Condition 8, 12 and 48 to be amended to read as follows, and any red mark ups on plans to be corrected accordingly:
 
8Reduction in Building Height
The architectural plans must be amended to reduce the height of the upper levels of the development as follows:
 
  • the roof terrace level must be lowered to a maximum RL 32220 mm  AHD; and 
  • the first floor level must be lowered to a maximum RL 29220 mm AHD 
  • The ground floor must be lowered to a maximum RL 26020 mm AHD
  • The lower floor level 1 must be lowered to a maximum RL 22820mm AHD and 
  • The Lower level  must be lowered to a maximum of RL21380mm AHD
 
All associated roof forms, walls, balustrades, windows, doors and other building elements must be adjusted accordingly to reflect the reduced floor levels.
 
The amended plans must demonstrate compliance with these requirements prior to the issue of a Construction Certificate.
 
12Building Height 
Prior to the issue of a Construction Certificate, a Registered Surveyor must certify that the proposed development, as detailed in the Construction Certificate plans, does not exceed the maximum building height of RL 32220 mm AHD for the roof terrace, RL 29220 mm AHD for the first floor level, the ground floor level to RL 26020 mm AHD, the lower floor level 1 to RL 22820 mm and the lower floor level 2 to RL 21380 mm AHD.
 
Note: No approval is granted for any lift overrun above the roof terrace as per the approved elevations and sections.

48Building Height 
Prior to the issue of an Occupation Certificate, a Registered Surveyor must provide certification, supported by an as-built survey, demonstrating that the completed development does not exceed the maximum building height of RL 32220 mm AHD for the roof terrace, RL 29220 mm AHD for the first floor level, the ground floor level to RL 26020mm AHD, the lower floor level 1 to RL 22820 mm and the lower floor level 2 to RL 21380 mm AHD.  
 

The motion was put to the vote and declared carried.
Cr Lyon, Cr Kay, Cr Hauge, Cr Ndiaye, Cr Dods, Cr Warth, Cr Swain voted in favour of the motion. 
Cr Lowe voted against the motion.

Moved: Cr Ndiaye Seconded: Cr Hauge
26-300 Resolved: 
That:
  1. Council elects a Deputy Mayor for the period from 17 September 2026 until the Ordinary Meeting of Council in September 2027;

  2. The method of election of the Deputy Mayor be by way of ordinary ballot; and

  3. That prior to the election, any candidate nominated for Deputy Mayor be given an opportunity to speak for 3 minutes.
The motion was put to the vote and declared carried.
Cr Lyon, Cr Kay, Cr Hauge, Cr Lowe, Cr Ndiaye, Cr Dods, Cr Warth, Cr Swain voted in favour of the motion. 
None voted against the motion.

Moved: Cr Warth Seconded: Cr Ndiaye
26-336 Resolved: 
That Council: 
  1. Notes the draft Baywood Chase Lake Management Plan (2024) is a draft technical document and is not considered suitable for public presentation in its current form. Relevant findings and management options will instead be considered through the formal CMP process, including future Councillor workshops;

  2. Notwithstanding 1 above, the draft Baywood Chase Lake Management Plan (2024) is provided as Attachment 1 (E2026/10026) for information and record-keeping purposes, noting the document is clearly watermarked to indicate its draft status and should not be regarded as a final or adopted Council position;

  3. Requests staff, as part of the scoping report already due at the December 2026 Ordinary Meeting on early-win interventions such as aeration, to include baseline water quality monitoring (including dissolved oxygen, nutrients, algae and bacteria/E. coli) so that any pilot intervention can be measured against a starting point; and

  4. Requests staff to continue identifying and pursuing grant funding opportunities to support water quality and biodiversity outcomes at Baywood Chase Lake, including through the NSW Environmental Trust and the Coastal and Estuary Grants Program, and to report available options back to Council as part of the December 2026 scoping report.

  5. That staff investigate opportunities for community education programs for drain buddies or other mechanisms that help improve waste catchment.
The motion was put to the vote and declared carried.
Cr Lyon, Cr Kay, Cr Hauge, Cr Lowe, Cr Ndiaye, Cr Dods, Cr Warth, Cr Swain voted in favour of the motion. 
None voted against the motion.

Moved: Cr Hauge Seconded: Cr Ndiaye
26-341 Resolved: 
That Council:
  1. Notes the submissions received during public exhibition and targeted industry engagement for the proposed amendments relating to All-electric (no gas) development (Attachments 2 and 4 E2026/17953 and E2026/83992, respectively).

  2. Notes that the consultation identified broad support for encouraging all-electric development, while also identifying practical implementation issues relating to energy resilience, specialised operational requirements and flexibility within the Development Control Plan.

  3. Adopts the revised Development Control Plan Chapters, D1 Residential Accommodation in Urban Village and Special Purpose Zones (E2026/82241), D2 Residential Accommodation and Ancillary Development in Rural Zones (E2026/83625), D3 Tourist Accommodation (E2026/83629) with the amendments contained in Attachments 5-8 (which establish all-electric development as the preferred outcome for new development while providing flexibility where an alternative energy source can be justified on operational, technical or resilience grounds) and the following further amendments in all three chapters: 
  • Objective 3: To reduce the ongoing operating costs of development by encouraging efficient electric appliances, compatibility with renewable energy systems, and avoiding reliance on gas connections and appliances; 
  • Objective 4: To provide flexibility only where gas can be demonstrated to be unavoidably necessary to achieve an operational, technical or emergency resilience requirement; 
  • Performance Criteria 1: Development should be designed and constructed to operate solely on electricity, unless there is a demonstrated operational, technical or resilience requirement that necessitates a gas connection; 
  • Performance Criteria 2: Reliance on gas infrastructure and gas-fired appliances should be avoided;
  • Prescriptive Measure 1: All-Electric Infrastructure – Development must be designed to operate without gas infrastructure, including gas pipes, meters and associated infrastructure; 
  • Alternative measures to be numbered accordingly;
  • Alternative measure 3: Emergency resilience or disaster preparedness considerations appropriate to the proposed development only where electric and battery storage options are demonstrated to be infeasible. 
  1. Adopts D4 Commercial and Retail Development (E2026/82245)  with the amendments contained in Attachments 5-8 (which establish all-electric development as the preferred outcome for new development while providing flexibility where an alternative energy source can be justified on operational, technical or resilience grounds) and the following further amendments 
  • Additional Alternative solution measure for D4.2.14: 
    Commercial cooking premises – Where a food and drink premises cannot practicably meet the operational requirements of particular commercial cooking equipment using electricity, or where doing so would require substantial augmentation of the available electrical supply or associated infrastructure, having regard to the scale and nature of the proposed use, gas may be used for that equipment or process. Any alternative solution should be limited to the equipment or process for which the need has been demonstrated and must demonstrate consistency with the objectives of this section. 
  • Additional exemption for D.4.2.14:
 4. Commercial kitchens
The use of gas appliances within a commercial kitchen may be permitted where the applicant demonstrates that:
  • gas is necessary for the operational requirements of the proposed use; and 
  • a practicable all-electric alternative is not reasonably available. 
The exemption should apply only to commercial cooking equipment and not to other services, such as space heating or water heating, which are to remain all-electric.
 
  1. Publishes the adopted Byron DCP 2014 Chapters D1-D4 on its website and provides copies to the NSW DPHI in accordance with the Environmental Planning and Assessment Act 1979, and Regulation 2021.
The motion was put to the vote and declared carried.
Cr Lyon, Cr Kay, Cr Hauge, Cr Lowe, Cr Ndiaye, Cr Warth, Cr Swain voted in favour of the motion. 
Cr Dods voted against the motion.

The meeting adjourned at 4:52pm for a break and reconvened at 5:02pm.

","reportContent":null,"minutesDiscussion":"PROCEDURAL MOTION
Moved: Cr Ndiaye Seconded: Cr Lowe
26-319 Resolved That Cr Swain be granted a two minute extension to her speech.
The motion was put to the vote and declared carried.

MOTION
Moved: Cr Swain Seconded: Cr Dods
Moved: 
That Council:
  1. Notes that Mullumbimby is being supplied with drinking water through its existing connection to the Rous County Council regional water supply, following the shutdown of the Mullumbimby Water Treatment Plant;

  2. Ceases all further work on the Mullumbimby Water Supply Strategic Planning Process;

  3. Returns all available remaining unspent project funds to the Water Fund; and

  4. Pursues a full and permanent connection to the Rous County Council regional water supply for the town of Mullumbimby, and requests staff to progress the necessary arrangements.
The motion was put to the vote and declared lost.
Cr Lyon, Cr Dods, Cr Swain voted in favour of the motion. 
Cr Kay, Cr Hauge, Cr Lowe, Cr Ndiaye, Cr Warth voted against the motion.

PROCEDURAL MOTION
Moved: Cr Lowe Seconded: Cr Hauge
26-349 Resolved That Cr Ndiaye be granted a two minute extension to her speech.
The motion was put to the vote and declared carried.

FORESHADOWED MOTION
Moved: Cr Ndiaye Seconded: Cr Hauge
26-332 Resolved: 
That the Water and Sewer Advisory Committee recommends that Council:
  1. Notes staff findings in relation to Resolution 26-200, namely:
    1. that undertaking a strategic planning assessment of water supply options for Mullumbimby will cost a minimum of $322,000.
    2. that there is currently no State Government funding available for water planning and infrastructure projects, and it is unclear when (or if) funding will be available in the near future.

  2. Allocates an additional $62,000, in addition to the currently available project funds ($260,000), for the strategic planning assessment process.

  3. Based on the adopted Long-Term Financial Plan (LTFP), there is scope in the Water Fund to allow for the required additional project funds.
The foreshadowed motion was put to the vote and declared carried.
Cr Kay, Cr Hauge, Cr Lowe, Cr Ndiaye, Cr Warth voted in favour of the foreshadowed motion. 
Cr Lyon, Cr Dods, Cr Swain voted against the foreshadowed motion.

Questions

Question No. 1 - 57 Station Street - Reason for Site Selection
Anando Hefley on behalf of the Mullumbimby Residents Association asked the following question: 
"Landcom advised us in writing that the studies underpinning the site selection for 57 Station St were commissioned by Council, and said “a request for their release is best directed to Council.” Can Council please identify the studies referred to by Landcom and release them so the public can understand the process and rationale for selecting this site." 
The Mayor took the question on notice.

Question No. 2 - State Significant Developments
Maxine Hawker asked the following question: 
"Has Council noted that all State Significant Development (SSD) housing projects, including those classified as 'affordable housing', are currently proposed or located within land zoned for 365-day short term holiday let precincts. Furthermore, has Council noted the size of these apartments? If so, what assessment has been undertaken regarding the cumulative impact of these developments?"
The Mayor took the question on notice.

Cr Lyon responded:
"I have noted the housing projects are in the 365 days area, however, I do not believe they are related.  The fact that it is a 365 day area is not the reason they want to put the projects in so they can benefit from the big bonus and holiday letting.  I think it's just a coincidence that the same area we did a 365 day zone, being the CBD where we want tourists to be, is also a good area for development in the way these SSD provisions are being put forward.  I think it's a coincidence.  I don't think it's some conspiracy to create big holiday let developments."

Cr Ndiaye responded:
"I don't think that the Jason Dunn development and the Mitre 10 site actually falls inside the 365 days but the other ones all do."

Cr Lowe responded:
"I agree that it's probably not a conspiracy however, it does open up the developments that fall within the 365 day short term stay cap to holiday letting as opposed to going onto the permanent housing market and that's a deep concern particularly as none of those apartments are affordable for normal people and it means that they can be holiday let.  That's a big issue in my thoughts."

Question No. 3 - Report 13.14 Implications of SSD Pathways
Peter Wilkosz asked the following question: 
"If Council adopts the staff report regarding SSD's and HDA Pathways at today's meeting, will you seek an urgent meeting with the minister? Will you work with other Councils on this issue? Will you investigate other statutory or legal options to protect Byron's planning framework?"
The Mayor took the question on notice.

Question No. 4 - Mullumbimby Car Parking
Jan Barham asked the following question: 
"Can Council clarify the Development Contributions collected from all stages of Tallowood Estate, Mullumbimby and if new car parking was delivered from those funds and if so where? and if
not, why not? noting the parking impacts were a key consideration for this development and required new parking to meet the impact."
The Mayor took the question on notice.

  1. Reviews and confirms Councillor membership of the following advisory committees, for the remainder of the 2024-2028 term of Council:
    1. Arts Advisory Committee – 2 Councillors
      1. Remove Cr Dods as the alternate
      2. Amend Terms of Reference to reduce membership to 2 Councillors (quorum 1 Councillor)
    2. Audit, Risk and Improvement Advisory Committee - 1 Councillor (non voting) 
      1. Remove Cr Hauge
      2. Appoint Cr Dods
    3. Biodiversity and Agricultural Advisory Committee – 3 Councillors
    4. Climate Change and Resource Recovery Advisory Committee – 3 Councillors
    5. Coast and ICOLL Advisory Committee – 3 Councillors
    6. Finance Advisory Committee – 4 Councillors
    7. Floodplain Risk Management Advisory Committee – 4 Councillors
      1. Appoint Cr Doherty
      2. Amend Terms of Reference to include 5 Councillors
    8. Local Traffic Forum - Director Infrastructure Services (Council Representative)
    9. Transport and Infrastructure Advisory Committee – 4 Councillors
      1. Appoint Cr Swain
      2. Amend Terms of Reference to include 5 Councillors
    10. Water and Sewer Advisory Committee – 4 Councillors
  2. Reviews the number of Councillor representatives on each committee.
The motion was put to the vote and declared carried.
Cr Lyon, Cr Hauge, Cr Lowe, Cr Ndiaye, Cr Dods, Cr Warth, Cr Swain, Cr Doherty voted in favour of the motion. 
None voted against the motion.

Moved: Cr Ndiaye Seconded: Cr Lowe
26-373 Resolved That Cr Ndiaye be granted a two minute extension to her speech.
The motion was put to the vote and declared carried.

Moved: Cr Lowe Seconded: Cr Ndiaye
26-372 Resolved: 
That Council:
  1. Formally writes to the NSW Minister for Planning:
    1. Seeking a Byron Shire specific exclusion from the HDA/SSD pathway (like for the Byron Bay Town Centre and Design Excellence Precinct), on the basis that Byron Shire has an endorsed Residential Strategy and established local planning controls and has demonstrated performance in the planning of housing delivery.
    2. Requesting a "distinctive character settlement" or equivalent State planning category to be considered by HDA/SSD recognising the special character, environmental sensitivity and coastal context of Byron Shire's towns.
    3. Requesting a pause/review of existing HDA/SSD declarations in Byron Shire, particularly where proposals conflict materially with established strategic planning.
    4. Requesting a cumulative-impact assessment where several major State projects are proposed within the same town centre covering housing yield, traffic, parking, water/sewer, flooding, coastal hazards, public space, infrastructure and town character.
    5. Requesting a requirement for State projects to comply with Council's affordable-housing contribution framework or provide an equivalent or better outcome.
    6. Seeking a formal protocol requiring early Council involvement at the HDA/EOI and SEAR stages, rather than Council first becoming substantially involved once the project is already declared.
    7. Seeking State funding/reimbursement for Council's technical assessment and infrastructure advice, given as part of assessing major State projects.; and
  2. Notwithstanding 1, continues to make detailed staff submissions during every SSD exhibition and seek robust conditions of consent.
The motion was put to the vote and declared carried.
Cr Lyon, Cr Hauge, Cr Lowe, Cr Ndiaye, Cr Dods, Cr Warth, Cr Swain, Cr Doherty voted in favour of the motion. 
None voted against the motion.

Moved: Cr Swain Seconded: Cr Hauge
26-377 Resolved: 
That the Biodiversity & Agricultural Advisory Committee recommends that Council:
  1. Notes that options for the formation of a Byron LGA Conservation Trust (as per Resolution 25-228) have been investigated, and that the Committee agrees with the Council staff recommendation in Update Resolution 24-235 that alternatives to the Conservation Trust are pursued instead;
  2. Notes alternative solutions to fulfil the aims of the trust “to identify and manage land with high ecological value within the LGA for the purpose of long-term habitat conservation, regeneration and rewilding” have been identified;
  3. Notes that the most cost effective and powerful action to support this goal of long term habitat conservation is to support appropriate zoning of High Ecological Value land to prevent degradation through development and land clearing;
  4. Supports an ‘opt in’ C2 Environmental Conservation zone for landowners wanting to support habitat conservation on their land;
  5. Provides an ongoing process whereby landowners can submit their requests for a conservation zone, and that these will be administered through Council’s regular housekeeping amendments at no cost to the landowners;
  6. Engages with Brunswick Valley Landcare to create a template by working with ‘opt in’ landowners to submit information to get land rezoned into a Conservation Zone; and
  7. Notes the importance of Council’s continued support to deliver actions outlined in the Byron Biodiversity Conservation Strategy and restoration projects across the Shire.
The motion was put to the vote and declared carried.
Cr Lyon, Cr Hauge, Cr Lowe, Cr Ndiaye, Cr Dods, Cr Warth, Cr Swain, Cr Doherty voted in favour of the motion. 
None voted against the motion.

Moved: Cr Swain Seconded: Cr Hauge
26-366 Resolved: 

That Council:

  1. Notes the release of an Expression of Interest (EOI) for lease of 125 Tweed Street Brunswick Heads on 11 September 2026, closing 26 October 2026;
  2. Notes that the EOI requires a financially self-sustaining operating model, with no subsidy available from Council to fund operations of the temporary housing village;
  3. Notes that Council is unable to waive or reduce the lease fee without equal compensation to the Sewerage Fund, in accordance with section 409 of the Local Government Act 1993;
  4. Notes that community consultation in accordance with Resolution 25-273(d) is being undertaken from 16 September to 23 October 2026 to inform the community about the EOI; and
  5. Notes that the community consultation process and the EOI outcomes will be reported to the 17 December 2026 Ordinary Meeting, with a recommendation on whether requirements to proceed to a lease have been met.
The motion was put to the vote and declared carried.

Moved: Cr Hauge Seconded: Cr Lowe
26-383 Resolved: 
That Council:
  1. Endorses the DRAFT Sports Field and Sport Facility User Policy (Attachment 1 - E2026/96591) be placed on public exhibition for 28 days to allow for submissions;
  2. Endorses the DRAFT Artificial Intelligence Policy (Attachment 2 - E2026/89865) be placed on public exhibition for 28 days to allow for submissions, with an amendment to include the following policy principle;
    1. Personal information: Personal and health information must not be entered into, or made accessible to, any AI tool. Exceptions may be permitted where a specific privacy impact assessment has been completed and approved for that specific use, with a register reported to ARIC, or where consent has been given by the individual to enter their personal data into an AI tool. Any approved use must be consistent with the purpose for which the information was originally collected. It must also comply with the PPIP Act, the HRIP Act, the Data Governance Policy and Council’s information classification standard. 
  3. Following the 28 day public exhibition of the policies listed in part 1:
    1. should submissions be received, the policy(s) be reported back to Council to consider submissions prior to adoption; or
    2. should no submissions be received the policy(s) be adopted.;
  4. Endorses the repeal of the Wet Weather Sporting Ground Closure Policy (Attachment 3 - E2021/46219), and instead adopts a guideline to accompany the Sports Field and Sports Facility User Policy on the website (Attachment 4 - E2026/97872); and
  5. Endorses the repeal of the Companion Animal Exercise Policy (Attachment 5 - E2022/103808).
The motion was put to the vote and declared carried.
Cr Lyon, Cr Hauge, Cr Lowe, Cr Ndiaye, Cr Dods, Cr Warth, Cr Swain, Cr Doherty voted in favour of the motion. 
None voted against the motion.

Moved: Cr Lowe Seconded: Cr Hauge
26-384 Resolved: 
I move that Council:
  1. Requests staff to investigate and report back on the option to:
    1. Prohibit the use of AI-enabled smart glasses and other wearable eyewear incorporating cameras, audio recording, live-streaming or similar recording technology by members of the public, contractors, visitors, Councillors and staff within:
      1. Byron Shire Council workplaces and offices;
      2. Council-operated swimming pools and aquatic centres;
      3. associated pool change rooms, amenities and other areas where privacy and personal dignity are reasonably expected.
      4. Council owned childcare facilities
      5. Council owned libraries
      6. Council owned and managed parks and playgrounds
    2. Develop and implement conditions of entry and workplace procedures to give effect to this prohibition, including appropriate signage and procedures for Council staff to identify and respond to the use of prohibited devices.
    3. Ensure that the prohibition is technology-neutral, applying to Meta AI/Ray-Ban Meta glasses and equivalent current or future devices capable of covert or inconspicuous recording, photography, audio capture, live-streaming or AI-enabled observation.
    4. Provide an appropriate exemption or reasonable adjustment for people who require smart glasses or equivalent technology because of disability or accessibility needs, subject to safeguards that protect the privacy and dignity of other people using Council facilities.
    5. Include legal, strategic, financial or policy implications any necessary amendments to relevant:
      1. conditions of entry;
      2. workplace policies and procedures;
      3. aquatic facility rules;
      4. privacy and child-safety procedures; and
      5. staff training and signage,to implement this policy.
    6. Consider appropriate signage that acknowledges the prohibition and the public safety and privacy priorities
  2. Writes to the NSW Government and Australian Government supporting the development of nationally consistent privacy and child-safety protections for AI-enabled wearable recording devices.
  3. Writes to the NSW Government seeking support and advice on Council's ability to prohibit the use of AI-enable smart glasses etc on Council managed Crown reserves, including parks and beaches.
The motion was put to the vote and declared carried.
Cr Lyon, Cr Hauge, Cr Lowe, Cr Ndiaye, Cr Dods, Cr Warth, Cr Swain, Cr Doherty voted in favour of the motion. 
None voted against the motion.

Moved: Cr Ndiaye Seconded: Cr Hauge
26-338 Resolved: 
That Council:
  1. Notes that fees charged to schools for swimming and water safety programs under current pool management appear higher than those effectively charged by previous operators, and that this may reflect inconsistent past application of Council's adopted Fees and Charges rather than a genuine increase;

  2. Requests the General Manager to prepare a report to Council investigating the feasibility of a reduced fee for school swimming and water safety programs delivered at Byron Shire Council pools, broadly in line with the rates previously experienced by schools, including the estimated cost to Council, participation data, and any impact on other pool users;

  3. Requests that this report include consultation with Belgravia Leisure and with local schools within the Lighthouse Valley Learning Community, and be brought back to Council by the December 2026 Council Ordinary meeting; and

  4. Notes that any adjusted fee would apply prospectively and transparently to all schools within the Shire, consistent with Council's obligations under its adopted Fees and Charges policy.
The motion was put to the vote and declared carried.
Cr Lyon, Cr Hauge, Cr Lowe, Cr Ndiaye, Cr Dods, Cr Warth, Cr Swain, Cr Doherty voted in favour of the motion. 
None voted against the motion.

[IGNORE_INDENT][OUTLINE_NUMBER_FULL_NO_PERIOD][AGENDA_ITEM_NAME]
","reportContent":null,"minutesDiscussion":"
Moved: Cr Ndiaye Seconded: Cr Lowe
26-354 Resolved: 
That Council:
  1. Submits the following Notice of Motion to the 2026 Local Government NSW Annual Conference calling on LGNSW to advocate strongly to the NSW Government for the retention of planning powers by regional and rural councils and the protection of local democratic oversight in planning decision-making: 
    That Local Government NSW strongly advocates to the NSW Government to:
    1. Protect and retain the existing strategic planning, statutory planning and development assessment powers of elected regional and rural councils, including the authority to determine whether a Local Planning Panel is established, and not transfer these powers to State appointed or centrally controlled bodies without the agreement of the affected council.
    2. Recognise the distinct circumstances of regional and rural local government areas and avoid imposing blanket planning controls and development standards that fail to adequately reflect differences in population, geography, development pressures, infrastructure capacity, environmental constraints and community expectations.
    3. Protect regional and rural councils ability to undertake additional community consultation and notification where local circumstances warrant engagement beyond minimum statutory requirements.
    4. Consult with regional and rural councils and Local Government NSW before finalising any planning reforms that reduce, transfer or diminish local government planning powers, and demonstrate how council feedback has been considered.
    5. Recognise distinctive towns and villages as a planning category that protects smaller, historic or distinct towns, not only regional centres.
  2. Notes that this motion is informed by Byron Shire Council's experience with the Housing Delivery Authority and State Significant Development pathways, which have facilitated planning decisions outside local planning controls, as well as recent legislative changes that significantly reduce the role of elected councillors in the assessment and determination of development applications. 
  3. Authorises the General Manager to finalise the wording of the motion, consistent with LGNSW submission requirements, and lodge via the LGNSW Conference Portal before the submission deadline of 25 October 2026.
The motion was put to the vote and declared carried.
Cr Lyon, Cr Hauge, Cr Lowe, Cr Ndiaye, Cr Dods, Cr Warth, Cr Swain, Cr Doherty voted in favour of the motion. 
None voted against the motion.

Moved: Cr Ndiaye Seconded: Cr Lowe
26-385 Resolved That Cr Ndiaye be granted a two minute extension to her speech.
The motion was put to the vote and declared carried.

Moved: Cr Ndiaye Seconded: Cr Lowe
26-355 Resolved: 
That Council submits the following Notice of Motion to the 2026 Local Government NSW Annual Conference calling on LGNSW to advocate strongly that the NSW Government:
  1. Notes that data centres are being proposed across metropolitan, regional and rural NSW, and that many are assessed as State Significant Development, bypassing local planning controls;
  2. Notes that the NSW Data Centre Guidelines are not mandatory and have no enforcement or public reporting requirements;
  3. Calls on the NSW Government to pause approvals of new large-scale data centres until a mandatory, enforceable planning framework is in place, including:
    1. binding energy and water targets, with public reporting;
    2. meaningful community and council consultation; and
    3. developer contributions to fund local infrastructure.; 
  4. Calls on the Federal Government to deliver enforceable national standards for data centres and AI infrastructure; and
  5. Authorises the General Manager to finalise the wording of the motion, consistent with LGNSW requirements, and lodge via the Conference Portal before the deadline of 25 October 2026. 
The motion was put to the vote and declared carried.
Cr Lyon, Cr Hauge, Cr Lowe, Cr Ndiaye, Cr Dods, Cr Warth, Cr Swain, Cr Doherty voted in favour of the motion. 
None voted against the motion.

Moved: Cr Lowe Seconded: Cr Ndiaye
26-357 Resolved: 
That Council:
  1. Notes that data centres are being proposed across NSW, including in regional and rural areas, and that many are assessed as State Significant Development, bypassing local planning controls;
  2. Notes that the NSW Data Centre Guidelines outline a 75-day fast track for compliant applications, but are not mandatory and have no enforcement or public reporting requirements;
  3. Notes that the federal expectations for data centres and AI infrastructure developers, published in March 2026, are not enforceable;
  4. Resolves that Council's position is that no data centre should be approved in Byron Shire until a mandatory, enforceable planning framework is in place and our community has been properly consulted;
  5. Requests staff prepare a report on:
    1. how data centres are currently defined and treated under the Byron LEP and DCP;
    2. gaps in local controls for energy use, water use, land use and community impact;
    3. the likely pressures on local infrastructure, water supply and the electricity grid; and
    4. options to address these gaps, including draft planning provisions.;
  6. Writes to the Premier and the Minister for Planning calling for:
    1. a pause on approvals of new large-scale data centres until a mandatory framework is in place;
    2. binding energy and water targets with public reporting;
    3. genuine consultation with councils and communities before approval; and
    4. developer contributions to fund local infrastructure.;
  7. Writes to the Federal Minister for Industry calling for enforceable national standards for data centres and AI infrastructure;
  8. Submits a motion to LGNSW so councils across NSW can advocate together.
The motion was put to the vote and declared carried.
Cr Lyon, Cr Hauge, Cr Lowe, Cr Ndiaye, Cr Dods, Cr Warth, Cr Swain, Cr Doherty voted in favour of the motion. 
None voted against the motion.

Moved: Cr Ndiaye Seconded: Cr Hauge
26-358 Resolved: 
That Local Government NSW calls on the NSW Government to ensure:
  1. The Financial Assistance Grant allocations exclude Disaster Recovery Funding Arrangements including recovery, reconstruction, betterment and resilience funding received by councils from calculations of grant income, revenue capacity or financial need.
  2. That no council is worse off, and any change to the distribution formula is accompanied by an increase in total Financial Assistance Grants.
  3. Any change to the Financial Assistance Grant methodology is introduced in a staged implementation, providing councils sufficient time to adjust workforce and operational planning, revise budgets and Integrated Planning and Reporting (IP&R) documents and, where necessary, apply to IPART for a Special Rate Variation to general income. 
The motion was put to the vote and declared carried.
Cr Lyon, Cr Hauge, Cr Lowe, Cr Ndiaye, Cr Dods, Cr Warth, Cr Swain, Cr Doherty voted in favour of the motion. 
None voted against the motion.
